            question_id: BQ-c9d7c39f6380eb60
            text: Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal
              review before the Nov 15 close?
            revision: legacy:6abf4a45ae87313af8db04b89d546e0e1a1c6137341b3d3c0d159c66cf64d54c
            dossier_revision: 08ac82685421cfccb819f5a516ae033746a14d373ea73b4540bd5c66e953798d

            source_action_key: null

          issue:
            issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-65ae94508dcda1bf
            title: State money-transmission authority after the asset purchase
            why_it_matters: The migration plan assumes Harbor’s licenses will permit
              service in four new markets. An asset purchase might not transfer those
              licenses or their operating authority to Mosaic.
            parent_issue_id: null
            fact_ids: []
          facts:
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-182bcc
            text: Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
              weeks out).
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-551367
            text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance and full access to Mosaic's product set.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9a0c61
            text: Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC'd by Harbor.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-33293c
            text: Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
              Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-aea8ec
            text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
              has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
              for users onboarded before 2023.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-073838
            text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor's transaction feed at
              Mosaic's engine on day 1.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-19aebc
            text: Marketing wants a 'Welcome' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
              launching close+1.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-adf2cb
            text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-4c1fd8
            text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f2c49f
            text: Plan is no re-verification of Harbor's existing KYC; Harbor users
              were already KYC'd.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-13d4c1
            text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
              results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
              users onboarded before 2023.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-78d5cd
            text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
              Relay's engine on day 1.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9f7bde
            text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-ed9f06
            text: How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
              buys Harbor's assets)
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-b5e71e
            text: Does Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program currently permit relying on
              another institution's prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
              required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-849b00
            text: What is known about Harbor's ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f0fb01
            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
              Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor's existing licenses or apply
              for its own? — Use/assume Harbor's licenses
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-620c62
            text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
              what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
              Relay's AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance
              must confirm.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-070aec
            text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
              been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
              have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-771ee1
            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
              what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
              before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to
              use or assume Harbor's licenses for the four new markets.
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
          assumptions:
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-29b823
            text: Mosaic Relay's existing money transmission licenses and Harbor's
              MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition without
              new state approval
            reason: Needed to continue
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-3c5756
            text: The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay's
              own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents
            reason: Needed to continue
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-1a519f
            text: The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and validated
              before close without a monitoring gap
            reason: Needed to continue
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-ca7dfd
            text: Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state MTL
              regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).
            reason: Needed to continue
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-d40239
            text: Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states
              (per the request).
            reason: Needed to continue
          - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-57e86b
            text: The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase, which
              affects whether Harbor's licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).
            reason: Needed to continue
          questions:
          - question_id: Q-SAR
            text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
              been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
            consequence: Unread open alerts and SARs are the highest-risk item; they
              can create BSA/AML exposure that must be addressed before close and
              could affect the deal itself.
            state: answered
            answer: The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain
              in diligence.
            answer_kind: reported_fact
            linked_fact_ids:
            - FACT-20260909-070aec
          - question_id: Q-KYC
            text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
              what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations?
            consequence: Whether the missing underlying documents create a compliance
              gap depends on how Mosaic plans to satisfy its own CIP/recordkeeping
              obligations for these users.
            state: answered
            answer: It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program permits
              reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must confirm.
            answer_kind: reported_fact
            linked_fact_ids:
            - FACT-20260909-620c62
          - question_id: Q-MTL
            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
              what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
              before onboarding those customers?
            consequence: Whether the four new markets can be served at close depends
              on license transferability and state approval, which is a gating regulatory
              question.
            state: answered
            answer: Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's licenses
              for the four new markets.
            answer_kind: reported_fact
            linked_fact_ids:
            - FACT-20260909-771ee1
          - question_id: Q-BONUS
            text: How is the $50 welcome bonus structured?
            consequence: The structure determines whether the bonus triggers consumer
              disclosure, funds-flow, or state promotional requirements.
            state: left_open
            answer: null
            answer_kind: null
            linked_fact_ids: []

              "content": "## Working position\n\nThe Harbor Pay migration needs legal
              and compliance review before the planned close. The leading concern
              is that an asset purchase generally requires Mosaic Relay to confirm
              its own authority to operate in each state; the current plan to use
              or assume Harbor''s licenses is not established as legally effective.\n\nThe
              second concern is BSA/AML readiness. Mosaic Relay has not confirmed
              whether its AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC,
              and underlying records are missing for some pre-2023 users. Harbor''s
              open alerts and SAR history also remain unread. These gaps make a day-one
              migration without re-verification or account restrictions difficult
              to support.\n\nTransaction monitoring continuity is also material because
              Harbor''s vendor ends at close. The repointed feed should be tested
              and validated before migrated users receive full access. The $50 bonus
              is lower priority but still needs review once its eligibility, funding,
              terms, and disclosures are known.\n\n## Plausible alternatives\n\nA
              narrower launch could exclude the four new markets, restrict users whose
              KYC evidence is incomplete, or delay full product access until alert
              review and monitoring validation finish. A full day-one launch remains
              possible only if state licensing, AML/CIP reliance, alert handling,
              and monitoring continuity are confirmed.\n\n## Material facts and assumptions\n\nReported
              facts include the asset-purchase structure, the current plan to rely
              on Harbor''s licenses, the lack of a compliance answer on KYC reliance,
              and the unread alerts and SAR history. The analysis assumes both entities
              conduct regulated money-transmission activity and that Mosaic Relay
              will become the operating provider immediately after close. It does
              not assume that Harbor''s licenses transfer or that Harbor''s KYC is
              sufficient.\n\n## What could change this view\n\nThe view could change
              if state counsel confirms an effective licensing path for each affected
              state, compliance confirms permissible reliance with adequate records
              or remediation, diligence clears the alerts and SAR history, and testing
              shows no monitoring gap. The bonus structure remains unknown.\n\n##

              "source_records": [{"source_id": "SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c", "source_hash":
              "58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409",

              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md",
              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md", "title": "facts.md",
              "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
              "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted
              Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k
              business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with
              one unified account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product
              set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
              by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
              Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four
              new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in
              2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying
              documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction
              monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
              plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s engine on
              day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
              first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts
              and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read
              them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
              into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
              and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC;
              Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone but underlying
              documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
              engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful''
              of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How
              is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys
              Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently
              permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
              or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-
              What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four
              new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan
              to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its own? —
              Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023 Harbor users with
              no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s
              own BSA/AML customer identification and recordkeeping obligations? —
              It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits
              reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have the
              ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed,
              and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history have not
              been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For the four new markets opened
              by the combined license footprint, what is the plan for state money
              transmission licensing or approval before onboarding those customers?
              — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for
              the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s
              existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable
              or can be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n-
              [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
              Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents\n-
              [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
              validated before close without a monitoring gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor
              Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state MTL regimes and
              federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption] Mosaic
              Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
              [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
              which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0,
              "end": 3962, "text": "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor
              Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k
              consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on
              day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and full access
              to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users
              were already KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses
              (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44
              states, opening four new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but
              not the underlying documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s
              engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50
              bonus on first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40
              open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor;
              nobody has read them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and
              12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close,
              with one unified account and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification
              of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s
              KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist
              for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded
              before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS
              whose contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
              feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open
              alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none
              have been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured?
              — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s
              AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another institution''s prior
              KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification required? — Not sure
              / need to check with compliance\n- What is known about Harbor''s ~40
              open alerts and the SARs from the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet
              — still in diligence\n- For the four new markets opened by the combined
              footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing
              licenses or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For
              the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is
              the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
              Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance
              must confirm.\n- Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from
              the last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
              and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For
              the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
              is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before
              onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or
              assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n-
              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
              Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
              without new state approval\n- [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results
              are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations
              without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction monitoring
              repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring
              gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
              to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n-
              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
              41 states (per the request).\n- [Assumption] The acquisition is structured
              as an asset or stock purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses
              and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).\n"}],

              "SRC-LOCAL-db6468aeb552bb44aa7b", "source_hash": "916b7009f261c21b7029be2ac4bab07fb4fd2909920244882bc8c02250c75dac",

              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/issues.md", "title": "issues.md",
              "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
              "# Issues and workstreams\n\n- Money transmission licensing: whether
              Mosaic Relay can operate under the combined 44-state footprint and whether
              Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition\n- BSA/AML and KYC:
              whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing underlying documents
              for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations\n-
              SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor''s
              ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability\n- Monitoring vendor
              transition: continuity of transaction monitoring when the SaaS contract
              terminates at close\n- Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer
              and any state money transmission or consumer protection implications\n-
              Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
              -->\n- Open alerts, suspicious activity history, and acquisition diligence
              <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-d22ea3957f21252a -->\n- State money-transmission
              authority after the asset purchase <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-65ae94508dcda1bf
              -->\n- Reliance on Harbor’s prior identity verification <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-30caa16a9234ccf2
              -->\n- Transaction-monitoring continuity at cutover <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-1d13a6636b8fbe60
              -->\n- Purchase-agreement authority and risk allocation <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-29efc151650e76a2

              {"source_id": "SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538", "source_version": "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a",
              "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act", "extraction_state":
              "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000014", "start": 0,
              "end": 1963, "page_number": 14, "section_label": null, "body_hash":
              "5b5d2f6c388b9bcf98252d205bb001dbdce26951229e0e6896dfecf0358be545",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000014.md",
              "text": "14 \n \nARTICLE V \nMoney Transmission Licenses \nSection 5.01
              License Required. \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the business of
              money transmission or \nadvertise, solicit, or hold itself out as providing
              money transmission unless the person is licensed \nunder this [Act];
              \n(b) \n[Section 5.01(a)] does not apply to: \n(1) \nA person that is
              an authorized delegate of a person licensed under \nthis [Act] acting
              within the scope of authority conferred by a written contract with the
              \nlicensee; or \n(2) \nA person that is exempt pursuant to [Section
              3.01] and does not \nengage in money transmission outside the scope
              of such exemption. \n(c) \nA license issued under [Section 5.05] is
              not transferable or assignable. \nSection 5.02 Consistent State Licensing.
              \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing between [this state] and other
              states, the \n[Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to: \n(1)
              \nimplement all licensing provisions of this [Act] in a manner that
              is \nconsistent with other states that have adopted this [Act]or multistate
              licensing processes; \nand \n(2) \nparticipate in nationwide protocols
              for licensing cooperation and \ncoordination among state regulators
              provided that such protocols are consistent with this \n[Act]. \n(b)
              \nIn order to fulfill the purposes of this [Act], the [Commissioner]
              is \nauthorized and encouraged to establish relationships or contracts
              with NMLS or other entities \ndesignated by NMLS to enable the [Commissioner]
              to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain records; \n(2) \ncoordinate multistate
              licensing processes and supervision processes; \n(3) \nprocess fees;
              and \n(4) \nfacilitate communication between [state] and licensees or
              other \npersons subject to this [Act]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] is
              authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS for all \naspects of licensing
              in accordance with this [Act], including but not limited to, license
              applications, \napplications for acquisitions of control, surety bonds,
              reporting, criminal history background\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved",

              CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete",
              "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000019", "start": 0, "end": 2376,

              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000019.md",
              "text": "19 \n \n(C) \nEmployment history; \n(D) \nMedia history, including
              an electronic search of national and \nlocal publications, wire services,
              and business applications; and \n(E) \nFinancial services-related regulatory
              history, including but \nnot limited to, money transmission, securities,
              banking, insurance, and mortgage-\nrelated industries. \nSection 5.05
              Issuance of License. \n(a) \nWhen an application for an original license
              under this [Act] appears to \ninclude all the items and addresses all
              of the matters that are required, the application is complete \nand
              the [Commissioner] shall promptly notify the applicant in a record of
              the date on which the \napplication is determined to be complete, and:13
              \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] shall approve or deny the application within
              \n120 days after the completion date; or \n(2) \nif the application
              is not approved or denied within 120 days after the \ncompletion date:
              \n(A) \nthe application is approved; and \n(B) \nthe license takes effect
              as of the first business day after \nexpiration of the 120-day period.
              \n(C) \nThe [Commissioner] may for good cause extend the \napplication
              period. \n(b) \nA determination by the [Commissioner] that an application
              is complete and \nis accepted for processing means only that the application,
              on its face, appears to include all of the \nitems, including the Criminal
              Background Check response from the FBI, and address all of the \nmatters
              that are required, and is not an assessment of the substance of the
              application or of the \nsufficiency of the information provided. \n(c)
              \nWhen an application is filed and considered complete under this [Section
              \n5.05], the [Commissioner] shall investigate the applicant''s financial
              condition and responsibility, \nfinancial and business experience, character,
              and general fitness. The [Commissioner] may \nconduct an on-site investigation
              of the applicant, the reasonable cost of which the applicant must \npay.
              The [Commissioner] shall issue a license to an applicant under this
              [Section 5.05] if the \n[Commissioner] finds that all of the following
              conditions have been fulfilled: \n \n13 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate
              and streamline the process of communicating when applications are \nreceived
              and when states consider them to have been complete. The intent of this
              [Act] is for the application period to \nbegin on the day an application
              is determined to be complete.\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved", "url":

              {"source_id": "SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538", "source_version": "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a",

              "text": "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. The renewal
              report must state or contain a \ndescription of each material change
              in information submitted by the licensee in its original license \napplication
              which has not been reported to the [Commissioner]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner]
              for good cause may grant an extension of the renewal \ndate. \n(d) \nThe
              [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS to \nprocess
              license renewals provided that such functionality is consistent with
              this [Section 5.06]. \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of License. \n(a) \nIf
              a licensee does not continue to meet the qualifications or satisfy the
              \nrequirements that apply to an applicant for a new money transmission
              license, the [Commissioner] \nmay suspend or revoke the licensee''s
              license in accordance with the procedures established by this \n[Act]
              or other applicable state law for such suspension or revocation. \n(b)
              \nAn applicant for a money transmission license must demonstrate that
              it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission licensee must at all
              times meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03]
              of this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control and Change of Key
              Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition of Control. \n(a) \nAny person,
              or group of persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof
              a licensee shall obtain the written approval of the [Commissioner] prior
              to acquiring control. \nAn individual is not deemed to acquire control
              of a licensee and is not subject to these acquisition \nof control provisions
              when that individual becomes a key individual in the ordinary course
              of \nbusiness. \n(b) \nA person, or group of persons acting in concert,
              seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall, in cooperation with
              the licensee: \n(1) \nSubmit an application in a form and in a medium
              prescribed by the \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable
              fee of [$X] with the request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the
              [Commissioner] may permit a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons
              acting in concert, to submit some or all information required by the
              \n[Commissioner] pursuant to [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS.
              \n(d) \nThe application required by [Section 6.01(b)(1)] shall include
              information \nrequired by [Section 5.04] for any new key individuals
              that have not previously completed the \nrequirements of [Section 5.04]
              for a licensee.\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",
              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/RUN-20260911-d08e84-37ee676da5b354ba8538-fetch.md.bin",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000021.md",
              "source_hash": "5638ae03ab2c6c110a80e30639b8ccd42a1c585fdc2818a38e4f2f0fc69a5e06",
              "source_label": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — Page
              21, characters 0–2389", "unit_id": "p000021", "locator": "Page 21, characters
              0–2389", "available_excerpt": "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the
              [Commissioner]. The renewal report must state or contain a \ndescription
              of each material change in information submitted by the licensee in
              its original license \napplication which has not been reported to the
              [Commissioner]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] for good cause may grant
              an extension of the renewal \ndate. \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized
              and encouraged to utilize NMLS to \nprocess license renewals provided
              that such functionality is consistent with this [Section 5.06]. \nSection
              5.07 Maintenance of License. \n(a) \nIf a licensee does not continue
              to meet the qualifications or satisfy the \nrequirements that apply
              to an applicant for a new money transmission license, the [Commissioner]
              \nmay suspend or revoke the licensee''s license in accordance with the
              procedures established by this \n[Act] or other applicable state law
              for such suspension or revocation. \n(b) \nAn applicant for a money
              transmission license must demonstrate that it \nmeets or will meet,
              and a money transmission licensee must at all times meet, the requirements
              in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI
              \nAcquisition of Control and Change of Key Individual \nSection 6.01
              Acquisition of Control. \n(a) \nAny person, or group of persons acting
              in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall obtain
              the written approval of the [Commissioner] prior to acquiring control.
              \nAn individual is not deemed to acquire control of a licensee and is
              not subject to these acquisition \nof control provisions when that individual
              becomes a key individual in the ordinary course of \nbusiness. \n(b)
              \nA person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire
              control \nof a licensee shall, in cooperation with the licensee: \n(1)
              \nSubmit an application in a form and in a medium prescribed by the
              \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable fee of [$X] with
              the request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner] may
              permit a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons acting in concert,
              to submit some or all information required by the \n[Commissioner] pursuant
              to [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe application
              required by [Section 6.01(b)(1)] shall include information \nrequired
              by [Section 5.04] for any new key individuals that have not previously
              completed the \nrequirements of [Section 5.04] for a licensee.\n"},
              {"source_id": "SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538", "source_version": "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a",
              "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act", "extraction_state":
              "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000022", "start": 0,
              "end": 2612, "page_number": 22, "section_label": null, "body_hash":
              "175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000022.md",
              "text": "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control
              under this [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items and address
              all of the matters that are required, the application shall \nbe considered
              complete and the [Commissioner] shall promptly notify the applicant
              in a record of \nthe date on which the application was determined to
              be complete and:15 \n \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] shall approve or deny
              the application within 60 \ndays after the completion date; or \n(2)
              \nif the application is not approved or denied within 60 days after
              the \ncompletion date: \n(A) \nthe application is approved; and \n(B)
              \nthe person, or group of persons acting in concert, are not \nprohibited
              from acquiring control. \n(3) \nThe [Commissioner] may for good cause
              extend the application \nperiod. \n(f) \nA determination by the [Commissioner]
              that an application is complete and \nis accepted for processing means
              only that the application, on its face, appears to include all of the
              \nitems and address all of the matters that are required, and is not
              an assessment of the substance of \nthe application or of the sufficiency
              of the information provided. \n(g) \nWhen an application is filed and
              considered complete under [Section \n6.01(e)], the [Commissioner] shall
              investigate the financial condition and responsibility, financial \nand
              business experience, character, and general fitness of the person, or
              group of persons acting in \nconcert, seeking to acquire control. The
              [Commissioner] shall approve an acquisition of control \npursuant to
              this [Section 6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds that all of the following
              conditions have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe requirements of subsections
              (b) and (d) have been met, as \napplicable; and \n(2) \nthe financial
              condition and responsibility, financial and business \nexperience, competence,
              character, and general fitness of the person, or group of persons \nacting
              in concert, seeking to acquire control; and the competence, experience,
              character, \nand general fitness of the key individuals and persons
              that would be in control of the \nlicensee after the acquisition of
              control indicate that it is in the interest of the public to \npermit
              the person, or group of persons acting in concert, to control the licensee.
              \n(h) \nIf an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to a multistate
              licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and streamline the
              process of communicating when applications are \nreceived and when states
              consider them to have been complete. The intent of this Act is for the
              application period to \nbegin on the day an application is determined
              to be complete.\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",

              "source_hash": "175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748",

              "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a", "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission
              Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages":
              [{"unit_id": "p000023", "start": 0, "end": 2523, "page_number": 23,
              "section_label": null, "body_hash": "83a664c778fbc9de0b4d13270e2a918f6488b461db1a6617e3d36032163068ca",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000023.md",
              "text": "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized and
              encouraged to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead investigative
              state for the purpose of [Section 6.01(g)] if the \nlead investigative
              state has sufficient staffing, expertise, and minimum standards; or
              \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead investigative state, the [Commissioner]
              is \nauthorized and encouraged to investigate the applicant pursuant
              to [Section 6.01(g)] and \nthe timeframes established by agreement through
              the multistate licensing process. \n(i) \nThe [Commissioner] shall issue
              a formal written notice of the denial of an \napplication to acquire
              control within thirty (30) days of the decision to deny the application.
              The \n[Commissioner] shall set forth in the notice of denial the specific
              reasons for the denial of the \napplication. An applicant whose application
              is denied by the [Commissioner] under this [Section \n6.01(i)] may appeal
              within thirty (30) days16 after receipt of the written notice of the
              denial \n[pursuant to state administrative law procedures]. \n(j) \nThe
              requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to any of the
              \nfollowing: \n(1) \nA person that acts as a proxy for the sole purpose
              of voting at a \ndesignated meeting of the shareholders or holders of
              voting shares or voting interests of a \nlicensee or a person in control
              of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person that acquires control of a licensee
              by devise or descent; \n(3) \nA person that acquires control of a licensee
              as a personal \nrepresentative, custodian, guardian, conservator, or
              trustee, or as an officer appointed by a \ncourt of competent jurisdiction
              or by operation of law; \n(4) \nA person that is exempt under [Section
              3.01(g)]; \n(5) \nA person that the [Commissioner] determines is not
              subject to \n[Section 6.01(a)] based on the public interest; \n(6) \nA
              public offering of securities of a licensee or a person in control of
              \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn internal reorganization of a person in control
              of the licensee \nwhere the ultimate person in control of the licensee
              remains the same. \n(k) \nPersons in [Sections 6.01(j)(2), (3), (4),
              (6), (7)] in cooperation with the \nlicensee shall notify the [Commissioner]
              within [15] days after the acquisition of control.17 \n \n16 Commentary:
              Administrative procedures for challenging a departmental decision may
              be derived from other \naspects of state law. In such a case, this Act
              should be adjusted to reflect the relevant administrative process. \n17
              Commentary: Notice is satisfied upon updating the licensee’s NMLS record.\n"}],

              "page_number": 24, "section_label": null, "body_hash": "4732d9c2b053975a4d3cb27db8e99faa4baf45f71eb350fa519e31b5890ac680",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000024.md",
              "text": "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1) \nThe
              requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson
              that has complied with and received approval to engage in money transmission
              \nunder this [Act] or was identified as a person in control in a prior
              application filed with and \napproved by the [Commissioner] or by an
              MSB accredited state pursuant to a multistate \nlicensing process, provided
              that: \n(A) \nthe person has not had a license revoked or suspended
              or \ncontrolled a licensee that has had a license revoked or suspended
              while the person \nwas in control of the licensee in the previous 5-years;
              \n(B) \nif the person is a licensee, the person is well managed and
              \nhas received at least a satisfactory rating for compliance at its
              most recent \nexamination by an MSB accredited state if such rating
              was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee to be acquired is projected to meet
              the \nrequirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act]
              after the acquisition \nof control is completed, and if the person acquiring
              control is a licensee, that \nlicensee is also projected to meet the
              requirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and \n10.03] of this [Act] after
              the acquisition of control is completed; \n(D) \nthe licensee to be
              acquired will not implement any material \nchanges to its business plan
              as a result of the acquisition of control, and if the person \nacquiring
              control is a licensee, that licensee also will not implement any material
              \nchanges to its business plan as a result of the acquisition of control;  and
              \n(E) \nthe person provides notice of the acquisition in cooperation
              \nwith the licensee and attests to [Section 6.01(l)(1)(A), (B), (C),
              and (D)] in a form \nand in a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner].
              \n(2) \nIf the notice is not disapproved within 30 days after the date
              on \nwhich the notice was determined to be complete, the notice is deemed
              approved. \n(m) \nBefore filing an application for approval to acquire
              control of a licensee a \nperson may request in writing a determination
              from the [Commissioner] as to whether the person \nwould be considered
              a person in control of a licensee upon consummation of a proposed \ntransaction.
              If the [Commissioner] determines that the person would not be a person
              in control of \na licensee, the proposed Person and transaction is not
              subject to the requirements of [Section \n6.01(a) and (b)] of this [Act].
              \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing process includes a determination pursuant
              to \n[Section 6.01(m)] and an applicant avails itself or is otherwise
              subject to the multistate licensing \nprocess: \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner]
              is authorized and encouraged to accept the \ncontrol determination of
              a lead investigative state with sufficient staffing, expertise, and
              \nminimum standards for the purpose of [Section 6.01(m)]; or\n"}], "support_state":

              "58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409",

              "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted
              Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k
              business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with
              one unified account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product
              set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
              by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
              Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four
              new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in
              2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying
              documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction
              monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
              plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s engine on
              day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
              first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts
              and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read
              them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
              into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
              and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC;
              Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone but underlying
              documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
              engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful''
              of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How
              is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys
              Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently
              permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
              or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-
              What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four
              new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan
              to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its own? —
              Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023 Harbor users with
              no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s
              own BSA/AML customer identification and recordkeeping obligations? —
              It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits
              reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have the
              ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed,
              and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history have not
              been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For the four new markets opened
              by the combined license footprint, what is the plan for state money
              transmission licensing or approval before onboarding those customers?
              — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for
              the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s
              existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable
              or can be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n-
              [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
              Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents\n-
              [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
              validated before close without a monitoring gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor
              Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state MTL regimes and
              federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption] Mosaic
              Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
              [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
              which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0,

              KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist

              whose contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
              feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open

              — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s

              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and

              without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction monitoring
              repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring
              gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
              to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n-
              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
              41 states (per the request).\n- [Assumption] The acquisition is structured
              as an asset or stock purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses
              and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).\n"}],

              "title": "SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md", "support_state": "supplied",
              "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt": "# Known Facts\n\n-
              Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
              out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
              into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
              and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no
              re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor
              holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic Relay holds
              41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.\n- Harbor''s
              KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has pass/fail
              results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users onboarded
              before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS
              whose contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction
              feed at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome''
              campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence
              flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year
              at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer
              users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close,
              with one unified account and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification
              of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s
              KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist
              for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded
              before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS
              whose contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
              feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open
              alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none
              have been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured?
              — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s
              AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another institution''s prior
              KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification required? — Not sure
              / need to check with compliance\n- What is known about Harbor''s ~40
              open alerts and the SARs from the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet
              — still in diligence\n- For the four new markets opened by the combined
              footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing
              licenses or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For
              the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is
              the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
              Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance
              must confirm.\n- Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from
              the last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
              and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For
              the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
              is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before
              onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or
              assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n-
              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
              Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
              without new state approval\n- [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results
              are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations
              without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction monitoring
              repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring
              gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
              to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n-
              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
              41 states (per the request).\n- [Assumption] The acquisition is structured
              as an asset or stock purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses
              and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).\n",

              "available_excerpt": "# Research this issue for the dossier: Monitoring
              vendor transition: continuity\n\n## Question\n\nResearch this issue
              for the dossier: Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction
              monitoring when the SaaS contract terminates at close. Harbor''s monitoring
              contract ends at close. A failed or untested change could create an
              immediate gap in detection, records, and case handling.\nLawyer''s accepted
              priorities (private matter context):\nMake KYC, alert resolution, and
              monitoring continuity formal close and migration gates.: These linked
              controls affect the full migrated population and can create immediate
              exposure that is difficult to repair later.\nProposed date leads; resolve

              handling.\nLawyer''s accepted priorities (private matter context):\nMake
              KYC, alert resolution, and monitoring continuity formal close and migration
              gates.: These linked controls affect the full migrated population and
              can create immediate exposure that is difficult to repair later.\nProposed

              CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete",
              "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000027", "start": 0, "end": 1943,
              "page_number": 27, "section_label": null, "body_hash": "512d4a7a3e1afc61a66c79b53548e6795e9f434d557b21d346fd4662aaafc705",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000027.md",
              "text": "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements shall include
              or be accompanied by a \ncertificate of opinion of the independent certified
              public accountant or independent public \naccountant that is satisfactory
              in form and content to the [Commissioner]. If the certificate or \nopinion
              is qualified, the [Commissioner] may order the licensee to take any
              action as the \n[Commissioner] may find necessary to enable the independent
              or certified public accountant or \nindependent public accountant to
              remove the qualification. \nSection 7.03 Authorized Delegate Reporting.
              \n(a) \nEach licensee shall submit a report of authorized delegates
              within 45 days \nof the end of the calendar quarter.20 The [Commissioner]
              is authorized and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS for the submission of
              the report required by this [Section 7.03(a)] provided that such \nfunctionality
              is consistent with the requirements of this [Section 7.03]. \n(b) \nThe
              authorized delegate report shall include, at a minimum, each authorized
              \ndelegate''s: \n(1) \nCompany legal name; \n(2) \nTaxpayer employer
              identification number; \n(3) \nPrincipal provider identifier; \n(4)
              \nPhysical address; \n(5) \nMailing address; \n(6) \nAny business conducted
              in other states; \n(7) \nAny fictitious or trade name; \n(8) \nContact
              person name, phone number, and email \n(9) \nStart date as licensee’s
              authorized delegate; \n(10) \nEnd date acting as licensee’s authorized
              delegate, if applicable;  \n(11) \n[Court orders pursuant to [Section
              8.03];] and \n(12) \nAny other information the [Commissioner] reasonably
              requires with \nrespect to the authorized delegate. \nSection 7.04 Reports
              of Certain Events.21 \n \n20 Commentary: This language is designed to
              implement state use of the NMLS Uniform Authorized Agent Reporting \n(UAAR)
              process. \n21 Commentary: States are encouraged to utilize NMLS to satisfy
              Section 7.04 reporting requirements if NMLS \ndevelops new functionality
              to prioritize reporting of significant events.\n"}], "support_state":

              "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a", "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission
              Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages":
              [{"unit_id": "p000028", "start": 0, "end": 2132, "page_number": 28,
              "section_label": null, "body_hash": "80c098d06593529d6d6335e3b8a4fe8e8db356a8c5d82eb34a2001d27d642973",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000028.md",
              "text": "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner]
              within one business \nday after the licensee has reason to know of the
              occurrence of any of the following events: \n(1) \nthe filing of a petition
              by or against the licensee under the \nUnited States Bankruptcy Code,
              11 U.S.C. Section 101-110, as amended or recodified from \ntime to time,
              for bankruptcy or reorganization; \n(2) \nthe filing of a petition by
              or against the licensee for \nreceivership, the commencement of any
              other judicial or administrative proceeding for its \ndissolution or
              reorganization, or the making of a general assignment for the benefit
              of its \ncreditors; or \n(3) \nthe commencement of a proceeding to revoke
              or suspend its \nlicense in a state or country in which the licensee
              engages in business or is licensed. \n(b) \nA licensee shall file a
              report with the [Commissioner] within three business \nday after the
              licensee has reason to know of the occurrence of any of the following
              events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of the licensee or of a key
              individual \nor person in control of the licensee for a felony; or \n(2)
              \na [charge or] conviction of an authorized delegate for a \nfelony.
              \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee and an authorized
              delegate shall file all reports required by federal currency \nreporting,
              record keeping, and suspicious activity reporting requirements as set
              forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and other federal and state laws pertaining
              to money laundering. The timely filing of \na complete and accurate
              report required under this [Section 7.05] with the appropriate federal
              \nagency is deemed compliant with the requirements of this [Section
              7.05]. \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a) \nLicensee shall maintain the following
              records, for determining its \ncompliance with this [Act] for at least
              [three] years: \n(1) \na record of each outstanding money transmission
              obligation \nsold; \n(2) \na general ledger posted at least monthly
              containing all asset, \nliability, capital, income, and expense accounts;
              \n(3) \nbank statements and bank reconciliation records; \n(4) \nrecords
              of outstanding money transmission obligations;\n"}], "support_state":

              "source_hash": "80c098d06593529d6d6335e3b8a4fe8e8db356a8c5d82eb34a2001d27d642973",

              28, characters 0–2132", "unit_id": "p000028", "locator": "Page 28, characters
              0–2132", "available_excerpt": "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a
              report with the [Commissioner] within one business \nday after the licensee
              has reason to know of the occurrence of any of the following events:
              \n(1) \nthe filing of a petition by or against the licensee under the
              \nUnited States Bankruptcy Code, 11 U.S.C. Section 101-110, as amended
              or recodified from \ntime to time, for bankruptcy or reorganization;
              \n(2) \nthe filing of a petition by or against the licensee for \nreceivership,
              the commencement of any other judicial or administrative proceeding
              for its \ndissolution or reorganization, or the making of a general
              assignment for the benefit of its \ncreditors; or \n(3) \nthe commencement
              of a proceeding to revoke or suspend its \nlicense in a state or country
              in which the licensee engages in business or is licensed. \n(b) \nA
              licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner] within three business
              \nday after the licensee has reason to know of the occurrence of any
              of the following events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of the licensee
              or of a key individual \nor person in control of the licensee for a
              felony; or \n(2) \na [charge or] conviction of an authorized delegate
              for a \nfelony. \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee
              and an authorized delegate shall file all reports required by federal
              currency \nreporting, record keeping, and suspicious activity reporting
              requirements as set forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and other federal
              and state laws pertaining to money laundering. The timely filing of
              \na complete and accurate report required under this [Section 7.05]
              with the appropriate federal \nagency is deemed compliant with the requirements
              of this [Section 7.05]. \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a) \nLicensee shall
              maintain the following records, for determining its \ncompliance with
              this [Act] for at least [three] years: \n(1) \na record of each outstanding
              money transmission obligation \nsold; \n(2) \na general ledger posted
              at least monthly containing all asset, \nliability, capital, income,
              and expense accounts; \n(3) \nbank statements and bank reconciliation
              records; \n(4) \nrecords of outstanding money transmission obligations;\n"},

              "text": "29 \n \n(5) \nrecords of each outstanding money transmission

              may be maintained in any form of \nrecord. \n(c) \nRecords specified
              in [Section 7.06(a)] may be maintained outside this state \nif they
              are made accessible to the [Commissioner] on [seven] business-days''
              notice that is sent in \na record. \n(d) \nAll records maintained by
              the licensee as required in [Section 7.06(a)–(c)] \nare open to inspection
              by the [Commissioner] pursuant to [Section 4.03(a)]. \n \nARTICLE VIII
              \nAuthorized Delegates \nSection 8.01 Relationship Between Licensee
              and Authorized Delegate. \n(a) \nIn this [Section 8.01], \"remit\" means
              to make direct payments of money to \na licensee or its representative
              authorized to receive money or to deposit money in a bank in an \naccount
              specified by the licensee. \n(b) \nBefore a licensee is authorized to
              conduct business through an authorized \ndelegate or allows a person
              to act as the licensee''s authorized delegate, the licensee must: \n(1)
              \nadopt, and update as necessary, written policies and procedures \nreasonably
              designed to ensure that the licensee''s authorized delegates comply
              with \napplicable state and federal law; \n(2) \nenter into a written
              contract that complies with [Section 8.01(d)]; \nand \n(3) \nconduct
              a reasonable risk-based background investigation sufficient \nfor the
              licensee to determine whether the authorized delegate has complied and
              will likely \ncomply with applicable state and federal law. \n(c) \nAn
              authorized delegate must operate in full compliance with this [Act].
              \n(d) \nThe written contract required by [Section 8.01(b)] must be signed
              by the \nlicensee and the authorized delegate and, at a minimum, must:\n"}],

              "text": "12 \n \n(4) \nThe terms of or a copy of any bond filed by a

              and \n(e) \nImposition of an administrative fine or penalty under this
              [Act]. \nSection 4.03 Supervision. \n(a) \nThe [Commissioner] may conduct
              an examination or investigation of a \nlicensee or authorized delegate
              or otherwise take independent action authorized by this [Act] or by
              \na rule adopted or order issued under this [Act] as reasonably necessary
              or appropriate to administer \nand enforce this [Act], regulations implementing
              this [Act], and other applicable law, including \nthe Bank Secrecy Act
              and the USA PATRIOT ACT.  The [Commissioner] may: \n(1) \nconduct an
              examination either on-site or off-site as the \n[Commissioner] may reasonably
              require; \n(2) \nconduct an examination in conjunction with an examination
              \nconducted by representatives of other state agencies or agencies of
              another state or of the \nfederal government; \n(3) \n  accept the examination
              report of another state agency or an agency \nof another state or of
              the federal government, or a report prepared by an independent \naccounting
              firm, which on being accepted is considered for all purposes as an official
              report \nof the [Commissioner]; and \n(4) \nsummon and examine under
              oath a key individual or employee of a \nlicensee or authorized delegate
              and require the person to produce records regarding any \nmatter related
              to the condition and business of the licensee or authorized delegate.
              \n(b) \nA licensee or authorized delegate shall provide, and the [Commissioner]
              \nshall have full and complete access to, all records the [Commissioner]
              may reasonably require to \nconduct a complete examination. The records
              must be provided at the location and in the format \nspecified by the
              [Commissioner], provided, the [Commissioner] may utilize multistate
              record \nproduction standards and examination procedures when such standards
              will reasonably achieve \nthe requirements of this [Section 4.03(b)].8

              shall pay all \ncosts reasonably incurred in connection with an examination

              "# Issues and workstreams\n\n- Money transmission licensing: whether

              for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations\n-
              SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor''s

              "source_hash": "58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409",

              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md",
              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md", "title": "facts.md",
              "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
              "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted
              Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k
              business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with
              one unified account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product
              set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
              by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
              Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four
              new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in
              2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying
              documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction
              monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
              plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s engine on
