              "# Harbor 2 — Harbor Pay acquisition migration (matter dossier)\n\nMatter
              MAT-20260909-d89ad8 · prepared from captured records dated Sep 9–10,
              2026. Business question supplied by the matter record; direction unchanged.\n\n##
              Current position\n\nYes — material parts of the Harbor Pay migration
              need legal review before the Nov 15 close, and one item should be reviewed
              before the deal terms are settled, not merely before launch. This is
              not \"just a data migration\": the day-1 plan depends on results the
              records show are unconfirmed — license coverage in the added markets,
              the ability to rely on Harbor''s KYC without the underlying records,
              and a monitoring cutover with no gap.\n\nThree conditions decide how
              much of the full day-1 migration survives:\n\n- **Whether Mosaic can
              lawfully serve each added market on day 1.** The plan \"use/assume Harbor''s
              licenses\" is not established for an asset purchase. If approvals are
              missing, those markets are a post-close target, not day-1 access. (The
              number of added states is itself unresolved — see Record conflicts.)\n\n-
              **Whether Mosaic''s AML/CIP program and applicable rule permit reliance
              on Harbor''s prior KYC**, and whether the pre-2023 cohort with missing
              documents can keep full access without re-verification or limits.\n\n-
              **What the ~40 open alerts and the SAR history show**, and whether monitoring
              transfers without a gap. The alert/SAR review is the most decision-changing
              item because it can affect deal protections and how affected customers
              are handled at migration.\n\nThe $50 bonus (launching close+1) and the
              customer-records/terms side of the data move do not block close on today''s
              record, but each must be reviewed before its own go-live point and each
              needs documents not in the readable record.\n\nWhat can proceed now:
              migration engineering, diligence, the compliance data pull, the licensing
              map, and standing up a controlled review protocol for the alerts/SARs.
              What should wait or change: launching the added markets on Harbor''s
              licenses; full-access onboarding of users whose verification cannot
              be evidenced; the monitoring cutover unless a tested no-gap design or
              a bridge exists; the bonus until its terms are reviewed.\n\nThis draft
              recommends treating those items as pre-close gates and preparing a staged
              launch as the fallback. That is this draft''s recommendation, not a
              recorded decision. The recorded plan is unchanged: day-1 full migration,
              no re-verification, use/assume Harbor''s licenses, bonus at close+1.
              The only recorded lawyer decisions are the Sep 9 intake answers (asset
              purchase; compliance to confirm KYC reliance; alerts/SARs unreviewed;
              use/assume Harbor''s licenses). A complete dossier rewrite was submitted
              as a tracked revision on Sep 10 and, per the record, left the current
              dossier unchanged pending acceptance; generating this draft records
              no new decision.\n\n## Decision question\n\nDoes any part of the Harbor
              Pay acquisition migration need legal review before the Nov 15 close?\n\n##
              Issues\n\nThe four workstreams below are the recorded issue set from
              the Sep 9 initial issue map ([source:MSG-20260909-efcbdd]) and the lawyer''s
              \"four issues\" framing ([source:MSG-20260909-539d02]): licensing, KYC/AML,
              alerts and monitoring, and marketing. The saved issue list and its ISS
              identifiers were not inside this run''s readable material, so no issue
              IDs or markers are asserted here. A fifth issue, newly identified in
              this draft from the recorded migration plan, is included and labeled.\n\nSupport
              status: no retrieved external authority appears in the readable records.
              The record shows the lawyer asked for research with sources ([source:MSG-20260909-660683],
              [source:MSG-20260909-406e0e]), an initial \"research is in progress\"
              statement ([source:MSG-20260909-168b9d]) later corrected ([source:MSG-20260909-91b5ec],
              [source:MSG-20260909-b4cc1f]), and a run described as \"queued or running\"
              with saved source choices ([source:MSG-20260910-c27e90]); no run output
              was readable here. Every legal proposition below is therefore a framework
              or lead, not verified support; named authorities carry **Needs checking**.
              Each issue gets an initial answer; any prior researched issue answers
              in the nine captured documents were not readable in this run and should
              be merged when available.\n\n### 1. State money transmitter licensing
              for the added markets\n\n**Current answer**\n\nNot established for day
              1. An asset purchase does not automatically carry Harbor''s money transmitter
              licenses to Mosaic, and a separate legal entity cannot simply \"use\"
              another company''s licenses. Until a state-by-state path exists — new
              license, transfer or change-of-control approval in the transaction,
              or an arrangement where the licensed entity performs the transmission
              — the added markets should be treated as post-close, not part of day-1
              full access. Even where Mosaic holds its own license, the account migration
              may trigger state notices or filings (unverified).\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nState
              money transmitter statutes generally require a license, or status as
              an authorized delegate of a licensee, to transmit money for others;
              licenses are issued to a specific entity, and state approval is commonly
              required for a change of control or transfer of a licensed business
              [**Needs checking** — the MTL statutes of the specific states; the CSBS
              Money Transmission Modernization Act where adopted]. Federal MSB registration
              (31 C.F.R. § 1022.380) is a separate requirement and does not substitute
              for state licensure [**Needs checking**]. The precise research question:
              for each state where Mosaic lacks a license and Harbor holds one, what
              route lets Mosaic lawfully serve migrated customers — new license, license
              transfer, change-of-control approval, or authorized-delegate arrangement
              — on what timeline, and what customer or regulator notices accompany
              the change?\n\n**Application**\n\nRecorded: asset purchase (intake answer,
              [source:MSG-20260909-2e549e]); Mosaic 41 licenses; Harbor 38; combined
              44; plan \"use/assume Harbor''s licenses\"; full acce", "selected_passages":

              "title": "DOR-20260912-80f5fc.md", "support_state": "supplied", "source_type":
              "workspace", "available_excerpt": "## Harbor 2 — preparation note (close
              targeted Nov 15)\n\n**Controlling question:** does any part of the Harbor
              Pay acquisition migration need legal review before the Nov 15 close?
              The newest turn (\"Generate the Dossier\") and the surrounding bank-held-funds
              comparisons are supporting work; they do not change that question. The
              record contains **no recorded decisions** at all, all five registered
              issues are `open`, and one intake question — how the $50 bonus is structured
              — was left open with no answer.\n\n**Lawyer reframe.** Dana''s framing
              is \"it''s really just a data migration.\" The reframe is that the migration
              *is* the regulated event: on day 1 Mosaic Relay onboards 252,000 accounts
              into its own licensed product set with no re-verification, repoints
              monitoring, and launches a cash offer — under an asset-purchase structure
              in which nothing about Harbor''s licenses or compliance record transfers
              by default. The operative question is therefore not \"can we inherit
              Harbor''s status,\" but **\"what must Mosaic obtain, file, decide or
              preserve in its own name before Nov 15, and which parts of the stated
              deal upside are not actually available at close.\"**\n\n**Three premises
              the record lets us test**\n\n1. *\"Just a data migration.\"* Fails.
              The day-1 cutover is the moment CIP, licensing, monitoring and disclosure
              obligations attach to 252k accounts.\n2. *\"44 states is a nice win
              — opens four new markets.\"* Fails on the arithmetic and on the law.
              Harbor 38 + Mosaic 41 with a 44-state union yields **three** new states,
              not four, and the states are never named; and the plan to \"use/assume\"
              Harbor''s licenses rests on an assumption the record still marks open
              ([source:ASM-20260909-29b823]), against the saved position that transferability
              should not be relied on without a state rule, approval or written regulator
              position.\n3. *\"No re-verification — they were already KYC''d.\"* Unresolved.
              Whether Mosaic''s own AML/CIP program permits reliance is unknown, and
              the pre-2023 records cannot be recovered (vendor shut down in 2024;
              only pass/fail survives).\n\n**Different route the evidence supports.**
              Run the remaining ~9 weeks as a *gated launch*, not a documentation
              exercise: read and preserve the alert/SAR backlog; decide KYC reliance
              per cohort and schedule remediation; prove or drop the Harbor-only states;
              validate the monitoring cutover with a parallel run; paper notice/consent,
              new customer terms and closing conditions. If a gate fails, migrate
              only in the overlapping states on day 1 and onboard KYC-deficient accounts
              with limits — a scoped migration rather than the full one.\n\n**Material
              issues.** Five registered: money transmission licensing (44-state footprint);
              BSA/AML and KYC reliance for pre-2023 users; SAR and alert handling
              (~40 open alerts, unreviewed); monitoring vendor transition at close;
              $50 welcome bonus. Three that are missing and material: **migration
              data handling and customer notice** (the piece the request actually
              calls \"just a data migration,\" never analyzed); **pre-close papering**
              (closing conditions, interim operation, allocation of the alert/SAR
              and KYC-record risk — no draft or terms appear anywhere); and **post-close
              access to Harbor''s alert/case history** (the records live in the SaaS
              system whose contract ends at close).\n\n**Three business priorities**
              — ranked by effect on the business question, time-fixedness and irreversibility,
              not by difficulty:\n\n1. **Read and preserve the alert/SAR backlog before
              anything else is scheduled.** It is the only item that can change the
              deal itself; it is entirely unread, so no one can yet say whether a
              filing is late or an account must be excluded; and the records needed
              to answer it may become inaccessible at close.\n2. **Decide KYC reliance
              for the pre-2023 cohort — rely, re-verify, or restrict access.** It
              determines whether \"no re-verification\" is available at all for the
              largest population; the underlying documents cannot be recreated; and
              re-verifying or limiting a cohort is a multi-week program that has to
              be decided before close, not after.\n3. **Prove the Harbor-only states
              can be served at close, or pull them from day-1 scope.** It tests the
              premise the deal is being sold on, state timelines are the longest external
              dependency and cannot be compressed, and serving a state without authority
              is a violation later paperwork cannot undo.\n\n**Research these first:**
              the SAR/alert backlog ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38]), KYC
              reliance ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045]), and the licensing
              position for the Harbor-only states ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045])
              — in that order. If the team needs the earliest single go/no-go decision,
              licensing converts fastest — but it should still follow the backlog
              read, because a live SAR problem can outrank market access.\n\n**Watch-outs.**
              The bank-held-funds structure is a saved hypothetical and was never
              adopted; later turns ran under that scenario path, and some prior dossier
              drafts carry scenario scope, so their conclusions are not findings about
              this acquisition. The licensing research has **no citable support**
              (4 sources retrieved, 0 passages read; one output headed \"No external
              authority retrieved\"), and repeated \"research queued/running\" messages
              are status, not results. Assumption [source:ASM-20260909-57e86b] still
              calls the structure unconfirmed although the asset purchase is recorded
              and was reconfirmed twice by the user. The matter''s `target_date` field
              (2026-09-11) sits oddly against activity through 2026-09-12 — treat
              it as unverified. Urgent below marks the five items where the close
              date itself fixes the deadline and a mistake cannot be cured afterwards;
              it is not the same as the top-three ranking.\n\n*Not performed: no web
              research. Full-text reads covered the request, facts register, intake
              answers and early analysis; the licensing packet was reviewed at excerpt
              level and prior dossiers treated as fallible synthesis.*\n", "selected_passages":

              position.\n3. *\"No re-verification — they were already KYC''d.\"* Unresolved.
              Whether Mosaic''s own AML/CIP program permits reliance is unknown, and
              the pre-2023 records cannot be recovered (vendor shut down in 2024;
              only pass/fail survives).\n\n**Different route the evidence supports.**
              Run the remaining ~9 weeks as a *gated launch*, not a documentation
              exercise: read and preserve the alert/SAR backlog; decide KYC reliance
              per cohort and schedule remediation; prove or drop the Harbor-only states;
              validate the monitoring cutover with a parallel run; paper notice/consent,
              new customer terms and closing conditions. If a gate fails, migrate
              only in the overlapping states on day 1 and onboard KYC-deficient accounts
              with limits — a scoped migration rather than the full one.\n\n**Material
              issues.** Five registered: money transmission licensing (44-state footprint);
              BSA/AML and KYC reliance for pre-2023 users; SAR and alert handling
              (~40 open alerts, unreviewed); monitoring vendor transition at close;
              $50 welcome bonus. Three that are missing and material: **migration
              data handling and customer notice** (the piece the request actually
              calls \"just a data migration,\" never analyzed); **pre-close papering**
              (closing conditions, interim operation, allocation of the alert/SAR
              and KYC-record risk — no draft or terms appear anywhere); and **post-close
              access to Harbor''s alert/case history** (the records live in the SaaS
              system whose contract ends at close).\n\n**Three business priorities**
              — ranked by effect on the business question, time-fixedness and irreversibility,
              not by difficulty:\n\n1. **Read and preserve the alert/SAR backlog before
              anything else is scheduled.** It is the only item that can change the
              deal itself; it is entirely unread, so no one can yet say whether a
              filing is late or an account must be excluded; and the records needed
              to answer it may become inaccessible at close.\n2. **Decide KYC reliance
              for the pre-2023 cohort — rely, re-verify, or restrict access.** It
              determines whether \"no re-verification\" is available at all for the
              largest population; the underlying documents cannot be recreated; and
              re-verifying or limiting a cohort is a multi-week program that has to
              be decided before close, not after.\n3. **Prove the Harbor-only states
              can be served at close, or pull them from day-1 scope.** It tests the
              premise the deal is being sold on, state timelines are the longest external
              dependency and cannot be compressed, and serving a state without authority
              is a violation later paperwork cannot undo.\n\n**Research these first:**
              the SAR/alert backlog ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38]), KYC
              reliance ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045]), and the licensing
              position for the Harbor-only states ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045])
              — in that order. If the team needs the earliest single go/no-go decision,
              licensing converts fastest — but it should still follow the backlog
              read, because a live SAR problem can outrank market access.\n\n**Watch-outs.**
              The bank-held-funds structure is a saved hypothetical and was never
              adopted; later turns ran under that scenario path, and some prior dossier
              drafts carry scenario scope, so their conclusions are not findings about
              this acquisition. The licensing research has **no citable support**
              (4 sources retrieved, 0 passages read; one output headed \"No external
              authority retrieved\"), and repeated \"research queued/running\" messages
              are status, not results. Assumption [source:ASM-20260909-57e86b] still

              "source_records": [{"source_id": "SRC-LOCAL-db6468aeb552bb44aa7b", "source_hash":
              "916b7009f261c21b7029be2ac4bab07fb4fd2909920244882bc8c02250c75dac",
              "source_version": "916b7009f261c21b7029be2ac4bab07fb4fd2909920244882bc8c02250c75dac",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-db6468aeb552bb44aa7b.md",
              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/issues.md", "title": "issues.md",
              "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
              "# Issues and workstreams\n\n- Money transmission licensing: whether
              Mosaic Relay can operate under the combined 44-state footprint and whether
              Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition\n- BSA/AML and KYC:
              whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing underlying documents
              for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations\n-
              SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor''s
              ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability\n- Monitoring vendor
              transition: continuity of transaction monitoring when the SaaS contract
              terminates at close\n- Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer
              and any state money transmission or consumer protection implications\n-
              Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
              -->\n- Open alerts, suspicious activity history, and acquisition diligence
              <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-d22ea3957f21252a -->\n- State money-transmission
              authority after the asset purchase <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-65ae94508dcda1bf
              -->\n- Reliance on Harbor’s prior identity verification <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-30caa16a9234ccf2
              -->\n- Transaction-monitoring continuity at cutover <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-1d13a6636b8fbe60
              -->\n- Purchase-agreement authority and risk allocation <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-29efc151650e76a2
              -->\n- Customer terms, privacy, data transfers, and welcome bonus <!--
              issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-fcd3954739e05481 -->\n", "selected_passages": [{"start":
              0, "end": 1441, "text": "# Issues and workstreams\n\n- Money transmission
              licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate under the combined 44-state
              footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition\n-
              BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing
              underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent
              CIP/AML obligations\n- SAR and alert handling: obligations to review,
              file, and manage Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability\n-
              Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring when
              the SaaS contract terminates at close\n- Marketing compliance: the $50
              welcome bonus offer and any state money transmission or consumer protection
              implications\n- Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights
              <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06 -->\n- Open alerts, suspicious
              activity history, and acquisition diligence <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-d22ea3957f21252a
              -->\n- State money-transmission authority after the asset purchase <!--
              issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-65ae94508dcda1bf -->\n- Reliance on Harbor’s prior
              identity verification <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-30caa16a9234ccf2 -->\n-
              Transaction-monitoring continuity at cutover <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-1d13a6636b8fbe60
              -->\n- Purchase-agreement authority and risk allocation <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-29efc151650e76a2
              -->\n- Customer terms, privacy, data transfers, and welcome bonus <!--
              issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-fcd3954739e05481 -->\n"}], "content_truncated":
              false, "source_label": "issues.md"}, {"source_id": "SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c",
              "source_hash": "58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409",
              "source_version": "58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md",
              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md", "title": "facts.md",
              "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
              "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted
              Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k
              business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with
              one unified account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product
              set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
              by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
              Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four
              new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in
              2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying
              documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction
              monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
              plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s engine on
              day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
              first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts
              and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read
              them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
              into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
              and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC;
              Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone but underlying
              documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
              engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful''
              of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How
              is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys
              Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently
              permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
              or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-
              What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four
              new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan
              to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its own? —
              Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023 Harbor users with
              no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s
              own BSA/AML customer identification and recordkeeping obligations? —
              It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits
              reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have the
              ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed,
              and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history have not
              been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For the four new markets opened
              by the combined license footprint, what is the plan for state money
              transmission licensing or approval before onboarding those customers?
              — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for
              the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s
              existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable
              or can be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n-
              [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
              Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents\n-
              [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
              validated before close without a monitoring gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor
              Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state MTL regimes and
              federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption] Mosaic
              Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
              [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
              which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0,
              "end": 3962, "text": "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor
              Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k
              consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on
              day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and full access
              to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users
              were already KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses
              (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44
              states, opening four new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but
              not the underlying documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s
              engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50
              bonus on first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40
              open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor;
              nobody has read them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and
              12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close,
              with one unified account and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification
              of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s
              KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist
              for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded
              before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS
              whose contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
              feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open
              alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none
              have been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured?
              — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s
              AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another institution''s prior
              KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification required? — Not sure
              / need to check with compliance\n- What is known about Harbor''s ~40
              open alerts and the SARs from the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet
              — still in diligence\n- For the four new markets opened by the combined
              footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing
              licenses or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For
              the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is
              the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
              Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance
              must confirm.\n- Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from
              the last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
              and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For
              the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
              is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before
              onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or
              assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n-
              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
              Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
              without new state approval\n- [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results
              are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations
              without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction monitoring
              repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring
              gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
              to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n-
              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
              41 states (per the request).\n- [Assumption] The acquisition is structured
              as an asset or stock purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses
              and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).\n"}],

              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md", "title": "facts.md",
              "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
              "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted
              Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k
              business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with
              one unified account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product
              set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
              by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
              Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four
              new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in
              2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying
              documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction
              monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
              plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s engine on
              day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
              first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts
              and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read
              them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
              into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
              and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC;
              Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone but underlying
              documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
              engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful''
              of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How
              is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys
              Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently
              permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
              or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-
              What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four
              new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan
              to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its own? —
              Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023 Harbor users with
              no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s
              own BSA/AML customer identification and recordkeeping obligations? —
              It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits
              reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have the
              ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed,
              and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history have not
              been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For the four new markets opened
              by the combined license footprint, what is the plan for state money
              transmission licensing or approval before onboarding those customers?
              — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for
              the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s
              existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable
              or can be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n-
              [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
              Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents\n-
              [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
              validated before close without a monitoring gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor
              Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state MTL regimes and
              federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption] Mosaic
              Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
              [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
              which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0,
              "end": 3962, "text": "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor
              Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k
              consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on
              day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and full access
              to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users
              were already KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses
              (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44
              states, opening four new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but
              not the underlying documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s
              engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50
              bonus on first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40
              open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor;
              nobody has read them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and
              12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close,
              with one unified account and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification
              of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s
              KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist
              for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded
              before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS
              whose contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
              feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open
              alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none
              have been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured?
              — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s
              AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another institution''s prior
              KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification required? — Not sure
              / need to check with compliance\n- What is known about Harbor''s ~40
              open alerts and the SARs from the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet
              — still in diligence\n- For the four new markets opened by the combined
              footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing
              licenses or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For
              the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is
              the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
              Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance
              must confirm.\n- Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from
              the last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
              and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For
              the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
              is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before
              onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or
              assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n-
              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
              Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
              without new state approval\n- [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results
              are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations
              without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction monitoring
              repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring
              gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
              to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n-
              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
              41 states (per the request).\n- [Assumption] The acquisition is structured
              as an asset or stock purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses
              and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).\n"}],

              "# Issues and workstreams\n\n- Money transmission licensing: whether
              Mosaic Relay can operate under the combined 44-state footprint and whether
              Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition\n- BSA/AML and KYC:
              whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing underlying documents
              for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations\n-
              SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor''s
              ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability\n- Monitoring vendor
              transition: continuity of transaction monitoring when the SaaS contract
              terminates at close\n- Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer
              and any state money transmission or consumer protection implications\n-

              "# Issues and workstreams\n\n- Money transmission licensing: whether

              Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition\n- BSA/AML and KYC:

              "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted
              Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k
              business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with
              one unified account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product
              set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
              by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
              Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four
              new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in
              2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying
              documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction
              monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
              plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s engine on
              day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
              first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts
              and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read
              them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
              into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
              and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC;
              Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone but underlying
              documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
              engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful''
              of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How
              is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys
              Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently
              permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
              or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-
              What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four
              new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan
              to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its own? —
              Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023 Harbor users with
              no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s
              own BSA/AML customer identification and recordkeeping obligations? —
              It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits
              reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have the
              ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed,
              and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history have not
              been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For the four new markets opened
              by the combined license footprint, what is the plan for state money
              transmission licensing or approval before onboarding those customers?
              — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for
              the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s
              existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable
              or can be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n-
              [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
              Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents\n-
              [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
              validated before close without a monitoring gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor
              Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state MTL regimes and
              federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption] Mosaic
              Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
              [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
              which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0,
              "end": 3962, "text": "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor

              consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on
              day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and full access
              to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users
              were already KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses
              (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44
              states, opening four new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but
              not the underlying documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates

              engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50
              bonus on first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40
              open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor;
              nobody has read them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and
              12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close,
              with one unified account and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification
              of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s
              KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist
              for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded
              before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS
              whose contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
              feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open
              alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none
              have been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured?
              — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s
              AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another institution''s prior
              KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification required? — Not sure
              / need to check with compliance\n- What is known about Harbor''s ~40
              open alerts and the SARs from the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet
              — still in diligence\n- For the four new markets opened by the combined
              footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing
              licenses or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For
              the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is
              the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
              Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance
              must confirm.\n- Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from
              the last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
              and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For
              the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
              is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before
              onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or
              assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n-
              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and
              Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition
              without new state approval\n- [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results
              are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations
              without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction monitoring
              repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring
              gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
              to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n-
              [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
              41 states (per the request).\n- [Assumption] The acquisition is structured
              as an asset or stock purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses
              and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).\n"}],

              "workspace", "available_excerpt": "## Preparation note\n\n**Result:**
              Legal and compliance review is required before the Nov 15 close. The
              migration is not only a technical data transfer.\n\n**Lawyer reframe:**
              Determine which pre-close and day-one actions could change the deal
              risk, exceed Mosaic’s legal authority, weaken anti-money-laundering
              controls, or harm customers. Then separate safe preparation from actions
              that require legal clearance.\n\nThe current plan relies on unconfirmed
              assumptions. Harbor’s licenses might not transfer in an asset purchase.
              Mosaic might not be able to rely on Harbor’s identity checks. About
              40 alerts and several suspicious activity reports remain unreviewed.
              Harbor’s monitoring service will end at close, but the replacement has
              not been shown to work.\n\nThe safer route is a staged launch. Mosaic
              can complete reversible technical work before close. It should delay
              affected accounts, new markets, or full product access if a legal or
              compliance gate remains open.\n\n### Material issues\n\n- Unresolved
              alerts and suspicious activity history.\n- State money-transmission
              authority after the asset purchase.\n- Reliance on identity checks that
              lack underlying records.\n- Continuous transaction monitoring at cutover.\n-
              Purchase-agreement limits and allocation of compliance liabilities.\n-
              Customer terms, privacy notices, data transfers, and the $50 bonus.\n\n###
              Three business priorities\n\n1. **Protect the acquisition decision.**
              Review unresolved compliance matters before Mosaic accepts risk that
              is difficult to reverse.\n2. **Confirm lawful day-one service.** Verify
              that Mosaic can serve each account and market after an asset purchase.\n3.
              **Preserve a safe fallback.** Keep monitoring active and permit a staged
              launch if any required control is not ready.\n\n### First three issues
              to research\n\n1. **Open alerts and suspicious activity history.** The
              findings could change deal terms, closing conditions, remediation, or
              account eligibility.\n2. **State licensing.** Regulatory approval could
              take time and could prevent launch in the four new markets.\n3. **Identity-verification
              reliance.** Missing source records affect 240,000 consumers and 12,000
              business accounts and could require re-verification or access limits.\n\n\n\n>
              A requested saved-record read was unavailable. The writer used the material

              "## Preparation note\n\n**Result:** Legal and compliance review is required

              safe preparation from actions that require legal clearance.\n\nThe current

              access if a legal or compliance gate remains open.\n\n### Material issues\n\n-

              to research\n\n1. **Open alerts and suspicious activity history.** The

              {"source_id": "SRC-LOCAL-297efd7bb8430e22ef7b", "source_hash": "8da355f4654a8c9ef63ed45c11e80f7b1870be7b0eee84f77e33b55939d63b73",
              "source_version": "8da355f4654a8c9ef63ed45c11e80f7b1870be7b0eee84f77e33b55939d63b73",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-297efd7bb8430e22ef7b.md",
              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/dossier-requests/DOR-20260912-80f5fc.md",
              "title": "DOR-20260912-80f5fc.md", "support_state": "supplied", "source_type":
              "workspace", "available_excerpt": "## Harbor 2 — preparation note (close
              targeted Nov 15)\n\n**Controlling question:** does any part of the Harbor
              Pay acquisition migration need legal review before the Nov 15 close?
              The newest turn (\"Generate the Dossier\") and the surrounding bank-held-funds
              comparisons are supporting work; they do not change that question. The
              record contains **no recorded decisions** at all, all five registered
              issues are `open`, and one intake question — how the $50 bonus is structured
              — was left open with no answer.\n\n**Lawyer reframe.** Dana''s framing
              is \"it''s really just a data migration.\" The reframe is that the migration
              *is* the regulated event: on day 1 Mosaic Relay onboards 252,000 accounts
              into its own licensed product set with no re-verification, repoints
              monitoring, and launches a cash offer — under an asset-purchase structure
              in which nothing about Harbor''s licenses or compliance record transfers
              by default. The operative question is therefore not \"can we inherit
              Harbor''s status,\" but **\"what must Mosaic obtain, file, decide or
              preserve in its own name before Nov 15, and which parts of the stated
              deal upside are not actually available at close.\"**\n\n**Three premises
              the record lets us test**\n\n1. *\"Just a data migration.\"* Fails.
              The day-1 cutover is the moment CIP, licensing, monitoring and disclosure
              obligations attach to 252k accounts.\n2. *\"44 states is a nice win
              — opens four new markets.\"* Fails on the arithmetic and on the law.
              Harbor 38 + Mosaic 41 with a 44-state union yields **three** new states,
              not four, and the states are never named; and the plan to \"use/assume\"
              Harbor''s licenses rests on an assumption the record still marks open
              ([source:ASM-20260909-29b823]), against the saved position that transferability
              should not be relied on without a state rule, approval or written regulator
              position.\n3. *\"No re-verification — they were already KYC''d.\"* Unresolved.
              Whether Mosaic''s own AML/CIP program permits reliance is unknown, and
              the pre-2023 records cannot be recovered (vendor shut down in 2024;
              only pass/fail survives).\n\n**Different route the evidence supports.**
              Run the remaining ~9 weeks as a *gated launch*, not a documentation
              exercise: read and preserve the alert/SAR backlog; decide KYC reliance
              per cohort and schedule remediation; prove or drop the Harbor-only states;
              validate the monitoring cutover with a parallel run; paper notice/consent,
              new customer terms and closing conditions. If a gate fails, migrate
              only in the overlapping states on day 1 and onboard KYC-deficient accounts
              with limits — a scoped migration rather than the full one.\n\n**Material
              issues.** Five registered: money transmission licensing (44-state footprint);
              BSA/AML and KYC reliance for pre-2023 users; SAR and alert handling
              (~40 open alerts, unreviewed); monitoring vendor transition at close;
              $50 welcome bonus. Three that are missing and material: **migration
              data handling and customer notice** (the piece the request actually
              calls \"just a data migration,\" never analyzed); **pre-close papering**
              (closing conditions, interim operation, allocation of the alert/SAR
              and KYC-record risk — no draft or terms appear anywhere); and **post-close
              access to Harbor''s alert/case history** (the records live in the SaaS
              system whose contract ends at close).\n\n**Three business priorities**
              — ranked by effect on the business question, time-fixedness and irreversibility,
              not by difficulty:\n\n1. **Read and preserve the alert/SAR backlog before
              anything else is scheduled.** It is the only item that can change the
              deal itself; it is entirely unread, so no one can yet say whether a
              filing is late or an account must be excluded; and the records needed
              to answer it may become inaccessible at close.\n2. **Decide KYC reliance
              for the pre-2023 cohort — rely, re-verify, or restrict access.** It
              determines whether \"no re-verification\" is available at all for the
              largest population; the underlying documents cannot be recreated; and
              re-verifying or limiting a cohort is a multi-week program that has to
              be decided before close, not after.\n3. **Prove the Harbor-only states
              can be served at close, or pull them from day-1 scope.** It tests the
              premise the deal is being sold on, state timelines are the longest external
              dependency and cannot be compressed, and serving a state without authority
              is a violation later paperwork cannot undo.\n\n**Research these first:**
              the SAR/alert backlog ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38]), KYC
              reliance ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045]), and the licensing
              position for the Harbor-only states ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045])
              — in that order. If the team needs the earliest single go/no-go decision,
              licensing converts fastest — but it should still follow the backlog
              read, because a live SAR problem can outrank market access.\n\n**Watch-outs.**
              The bank-held-funds structure is a saved hypothetical and was never
              adopted; later turns ran under that scenario path, and some prior dossier
              drafts carry scenario scope, so their conclusions are not findings about
              this acquisition. The licensing research has **no citable support**
              (4 sources retrieved, 0 passages read; one output headed \"No external
              authority retrieved\"), and repeated \"research queued/running\" messages
              are status, not results. Assumption [source:ASM-20260909-57e86b] still
              calls the structure unconfirmed although the asset purchase is recorded
              and was reconfirmed twice by the user. The matter''s `target_date` field
              (2026-09-11) sits oddly against activity through 2026-09-12 — treat
              it as unverified. Urgent below marks the five items where the close
              date itself fixes the deadline and a mistake cannot be cured afterwards;
              it is not the same as the top-three ranking.\n\n*Not performed: no web
              research. Full-text reads covered the request, facts register, intake
              answers and early analysis; the licensing packet was reviewed at excerpt
              level and prior dossiers treated as fallible synthesis.*\n", "selected_passages":

              "source_hash": "58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409",
              "source_version": "58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md",
              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md", "title": "facts.md",
              "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
              "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted
              Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k
              business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with
              one unified account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product
              set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
              by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
              Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four
              new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in
              2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying
              documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction
              monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
              plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s engine on
              day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
              first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts
              and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read
              them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
              into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
              and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC;
              Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone but underlying
              documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
              engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful''
              of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How
              is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys
              Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently
              permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
              or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-
              What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four
              new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan
              to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its own? —
              Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023 Harbor users with
              no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s
              own BSA/AML customer identification and recordkeeping obligations? —
              It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits
              reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have the
              ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed,
              and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history have not
              been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For the four new markets opened
              by the combined license footprint, what is the plan for state money
              transmission licensing or approval before onboarding those customers?
              — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for
              the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s
              existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable
              or can be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n-
              [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
              Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents\n-
              [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
              validated before close without a monitoring gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor
              Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state MTL regimes and
              federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption] Mosaic
              Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
              [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
              which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0,
              "end": 3962, "text": "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor
              Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k
              consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on
              day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and full access
              to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users
              were already KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses
              (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44
              states, opening four new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but
              not the underlying documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s
              engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50
              bonus on first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40

              "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted
              Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k
              business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with
              one unified account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product
              set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
              by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
              Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four
              new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in
              2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying
              documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction
              monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
              plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s engine on
              day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
              first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts
              and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read
              them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
              into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
              and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC;
              Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone but underlying
              documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
              engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful''
              of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How
              is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys
              Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently

              or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-

              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four
              new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan
              to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its own? —
              Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023 Harbor users with

              for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations\n-

              ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability\n- Monitoring vendor
              transition: continuity of transaction monitoring when the SaaS contract
              terminates at close\n- Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer
