              "source_hash": "23fcb27105945705c2b19c1547c310303a49b7d909b07a52e0fe3323e0ae2e9a",
              "source_version": "23fcb27105945705c2b19c1547c310303a49b7d909b07a52e0fe3323e0ae2e9a",
              "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-8f6233be11b7205ffc25.md",
              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/dossier-requests/DOR-20260912-049f9c.md",
              "title": "DOR-20260912-049f9c.md", "support_state": "supplied", "source_type":
              "workspace", "available_excerpt": "## Preparation note\n\n**Result:**
              Legal and compliance review is required before the Nov 15 close. The
              migration is not only a technical data transfer.\n\n**Lawyer reframe:**
              Determine which pre-close and day-one actions could change the deal
              risk, exceed Mosaic’s legal authority, weaken anti-money-laundering
              controls, or harm customers. Then separate safe preparation from actions
              that require legal clearance.\n\nThe current plan relies on unconfirmed
              assumptions. Harbor’s licenses might not transfer in an asset purchase.
              Mosaic might not be able to rely on Harbor’s identity checks. About
              40 alerts and several suspicious activity reports remain unreviewed.
              Harbor’s monitoring service will end at close, but the replacement has
              not been shown to work.\n\nThe safer route is a staged launch. Mosaic
              can complete reversible technical work before close. It should delay
              affected accounts, new markets, or full product access if a legal or
              compliance gate remains open.\n\n### Material issues\n\n- Unresolved
              alerts and suspicious activity history.\n- State money-transmission
              authority after the asset purchase.\n- Reliance on identity checks that
              lack underlying records.\n- Continuous transaction monitoring at cutover.\n-
              Purchase-agreement limits and allocation of compliance liabilities.\n-
              Customer terms, privacy notices, data transfers, and the $50 bonus.\n\n###
              Three business priorities\n\n1. **Protect the acquisition decision.**
              Review unresolved compliance matters before Mosaic accepts risk that
              is difficult to reverse.\n2. **Confirm lawful day-one service.** Verify
              that Mosaic can serve each account and market after an asset purchase.\n3.
              **Preserve a safe fallback.** Keep monitoring active and permit a staged
              launch if any required control is not ready.\n\n### First three issues
              to research\n\n1. **Open alerts and suspicious activity history.** The
              findings could change deal terms, closing conditions, remediation, or
              account eligibility.\n2. **State licensing.** Regulatory approval could
              take time and could prevent launch in the four new markets.\n3. **Identity-verification
              reliance.** Missing source records affect 240,000 consumers and 12,000
              business accounts and could require re-verification or access limits.\n\n\n\n>
              A requested saved-record read was unavailable. The writer used the material
              available.\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0, "end": 2312, "text":
              "## Preparation note\n\n**Result:** Legal and compliance review is required
              before the Nov 15 close. The migration is not only a technical data
              transfer.\n\n**Lawyer reframe:** Determine which pre-close and day-one
              actions could change the deal risk, exceed Mosaic’s legal authority,
              weaken anti-money-laundering controls, or harm customers. Then separate
              safe preparation from actions that require legal clearance.\n\nThe current
              plan relies on unconfirmed assumptions. Harbor’s licenses might not
              transfer in an asset purchase. Mosaic might not be able to rely on Harbor’s
              identity checks. About 40 alerts and several suspicious activity reports
              remain unreviewed. Harbor’s monitoring service will end at close, but
              the replacement has not been shown to work.\n\nThe safer route is a
              staged launch. Mosaic can complete reversible technical work before
              close. It should delay affected accounts, new markets, or full product
              access if a legal or compliance gate remains open.\n\n### Material issues\n\n-
              Unresolved alerts and suspicious activity history.\n- State money-transmission
              authority after the asset purchase.\n- Reliance on identity checks that
              lack underlying records.\n- Continuous transaction monitoring at cutover.\n-
              Purchase-agreement limits and allocation of compliance liabilities.\n-
              Customer terms, privacy notices, data transfers, and the $50 bonus.\n\n###
              Three business priorities\n\n1. **Protect the acquisition decision.**
              Review unresolved compliance matters before Mosaic accepts risk that
              is difficult to reverse.\n2. **Confirm lawful day-one service.** Verify
              that Mosaic can serve each account and market after an asset purchase.\n3.
              **Preserve a safe fallback.** Keep monitoring active and permit a staged
              launch if any required control is not ready.\n\n### First three issues
              to research\n\n1. **Open alerts and suspicious activity history.** The
              findings could change deal terms, closing conditions, remediation, or
              account eligibility.\n2. **State licensing.** Regulatory approval could
              take time and could prevent launch in the four new markets.\n3. **Identity-verification
              reliance.** Missing source records affect 240,000 consumers and 12,000
              business accounts and could require re-verification or access limits.\n\n\n\n>
              A requested saved-record read was unavailable. The writer used the material

              "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/request.md", "title": "request.md",
              "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
              "# Original Request\n\nFrom: Dana, PM — Growth & Integration\nSubject:
              Harbor migration — anything here need legal?\n\nWe''re acquiring Harbor
              Pay. Close is targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks). Migration plan:\n\n240k consumer
              users, 12k business accounts move into our app on day 1 post-close.
              One unified account, one balance, full access to our product set.\nNo
              re-verification — they were already KYC''d by Harbor.\nHarbor holds
              MTLs in 38 states, we hold 41. Combined that''s 44 — nice win, opens
              four new markets.\nHarbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down
              in 2024. We have pass/fail results for everyone, but not the underlying
              documents for users onboarded before 2023.\nHarbor''s monitoring is
              a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close. Plan is to repoint
              their transaction feed at our engine on day 1.\nMarketing wants a \"Welcome\"
              campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer, launching close+1.\nDiligence
              flagged that Harbor has ~40 open alerts and \"a handful\" of SARs from

              [{"start": 0, "end": 1095, "text": "# Original Request\n\nFrom: Dana,

              move into our app on day 1 post-close. One unified account, one balance,
              full access to our product set.\nNo re-verification — they were already
              KYC''d by Harbor.\nHarbor holds MTLs in 38 states, we hold 41. Combined
              that''s 44 — nice win, opens four new markets.\nHarbor''s KYC ran through
              a vendor that shut down in 2024. We have pass/fail results for everyone,
              but not the underlying documents for users onboarded before 2023.\nHarbor''s
              monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close.

              wants a \"Welcome\" campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer, launching
              close+1.\nDiligence flagged that Harbor has ~40 open alerts and \"a

              any of this need legal before close? It''s really just a data migration.\n"}],

              "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted
              Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k
              business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with
              one unified account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product
              set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
              by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
              Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four
              new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in
              2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying
              documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction
              monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
              plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s engine on
              day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
              first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts
              and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read
              them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
              into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
              and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC;
              Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor
              that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone but underlying
              documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
              transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
              engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful''
              of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How
              is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys
              Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently
              permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
              or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-
              What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four
              new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan
              to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its own? —
              Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023 Harbor users with
              no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s
              own BSA/AML customer identification and recordkeeping obligations? —
              It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits
              reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have the
              ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed,
              and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history have not
              been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For the four new markets opened
              by the combined license footprint, what is the plan for state money
              transmission licensing or approval before onboarding those customers?
              — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for
              the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s
              existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable
              or can be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n-
              [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
              Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents\n-
              [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
              validated before close without a monitoring gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor
              Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state MTL regimes and
              federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption] Mosaic
              Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
              [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
              which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0,

              "title": "DOR-20260912-049f9c.md", "support_state": "supplied", "source_type":
              "workspace", "available_excerpt": "## Preparation note\n\n**Result:**
              Legal and compliance review is required before the Nov 15 close. The
              migration is not only a technical data transfer.\n\n**Lawyer reframe:**
              Determine which pre-close and day-one actions could change the deal
              risk, exceed Mosaic’s legal authority, weaken anti-money-laundering
              controls, or harm customers. Then separate safe preparation from actions
              that require legal clearance.\n\nThe current plan relies on unconfirmed
              assumptions. Harbor’s licenses might not transfer in an asset purchase.
              Mosaic might not be able to rely on Harbor’s identity checks. About
              40 alerts and several suspicious activity reports remain unreviewed.
              Harbor’s monitoring service will end at close, but the replacement has
              not been shown to work.\n\nThe safer route is a staged launch. Mosaic
              can complete reversible technical work before close. It should delay
              affected accounts, new markets, or full product access if a legal or
              compliance gate remains open.\n\n### Material issues\n\n- Unresolved
              alerts and suspicious activity history.\n- State money-transmission
              authority after the asset purchase.\n- Reliance on identity checks that
              lack underlying records.\n- Continuous transaction monitoring at cutover.\n-
              Purchase-agreement limits and allocation of compliance liabilities.\n-
              Customer terms, privacy notices, data transfers, and the $50 bonus.\n\n###
              Three business priorities\n\n1. **Protect the acquisition decision.**
              Review unresolved compliance matters before Mosaic accepts risk that
              is difficult to reverse.\n2. **Confirm lawful day-one service.** Verify
              that Mosaic can serve each account and market after an asset purchase.\n3.
              **Preserve a safe fallback.** Keep monitoring active and permit a staged
              launch if any required control is not ready.\n\n### First three issues
              to research\n\n1. **Open alerts and suspicious activity history.** The
              findings could change deal terms, closing conditions, remediation, or
              account eligibility.\n2. **State licensing.** Regulatory approval could
              take time and could prevent launch in the four new markets.\n3. **Identity-verification
              reliance.** Missing source records affect 240,000 consumers and 12,000
              business accounts and could require re-verification or access limits.\n\n\n\n>
              A requested saved-record read was unavailable. The writer used the material
              available.\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0, "end": 2312, "text":

    "content": "## Working position\n\nThe Harbor Pay migration needs legal and compliance
    review before the planned close. The leading concern is that an asset purchase
    generally requires Mosaic Relay to confirm its own authority to operate in each
    state; the current plan to use or assume Harbor''s licenses is not established
    as legally effective.\n\nThe second concern is BSA/AML readiness. Mosaic Relay
    has not confirmed whether its AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior
    KYC, and underlying records are missing for some pre-2023 users. Harbor''s open
    alerts and SAR history also remain unread. These gaps make a day-one migration
    without re-verification or account restrictions difficult to support.\n\nTransaction
    monitoring continuity is also material because Harbor''s vendor ends at close.
    The repointed feed should be tested and validated before migrated users receive
    full access. The $50 bonus is lower priority but still needs review once its eligibility,
    funding, terms, and disclosures are known.\n\n## Plausible alternatives\n\nA narrower
    launch could exclude the four new markets, restrict users whose KYC evidence is
    incomplete, or delay full product access until alert review and monitoring validation
    finish. A full day-one launch remains possible only if state licensing, AML/CIP
    reliance, alert handling, and monitoring continuity are confirmed.\n\n## Material
    facts and assumptions\n\nReported facts include the asset-purchase structure,
    the current plan to rely on Harbor''s licenses, the lack of a compliance answer
    on KYC reliance, and the unread alerts and SAR history. The analysis assumes both
    entities conduct regulated money-transmission activity and that Mosaic Relay will
    become the operating provider immediately after close. It does not assume that
    Harbor''s licenses transfer or that Harbor''s KYC is sufficient.\n\n## What could
    change this view\n\nThe view could change if state counsel confirms an effective
    licensing path for each affected state, compliance confirms permissible reliance
    with adequate records or remediation, diligence clears the alerts and SAR history,
    and testing shows no monitoring gap. The bonus structure remains unknown.\n\n##

    — 2026-09-09T20:57:53+00:00</summary>\n\n**Working position**\n\nThe Harbor Pay
    migration needs legal and compliance review before the planned close. The leading
    concern is that an asset purchase generally requires Mosaic Relay to confirm its
    own authority to operate in each state; the current plan to use or assume Harbor''s
    licenses is not established as legally effective.\n\nThe second concern is BSA/AML
    readiness. Mosaic Relay has not confirmed whether its AML/CIP program permits
    reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC, and underlying records are missing for some pre-2023
    users. Harbor''s open alerts and SAR history also remain unread. These gaps make
    a day-one migration without re-verification or account restrictions difficult
    to support.\n\nTransaction monitoring continuity is also material because Harbor''s
    vendor ends at close. The repointed feed should be tested and validated before
    migrated users receive full access. The $50 bonus is lower priority but still
    needs review once its eligibility, funding, terms, and disclosures are known.\n\n**Plausible
    alternatives**\n\nA narrower launch could exclude the four new markets, restrict
    users whose KYC evidence is incomplete, or delay full product access until alert
    review and monitoring validation finish. A full day-one launch remains possible
    only if state licensing, AML/CIP reliance, alert handling, and monitoring continuity
    are confirmed.\n\n**Material facts and assumptions**\n\nReported facts include
    the asset-purchase structure, the current plan to rely on Harbor''s licenses,
    the lack of a compliance answer on KYC reliance, and the unread alerts and SAR
    history. The analysis assumes both entities conduct regulated money-transmission
    activity and that Mosaic Relay will become the operating provider immediately
    after close. It does not assume that Harbor''s licenses transfer or that Harbor''s
    KYC is sufficient.\n\n**What could change this view**\n\nThe view could change
    if state counsel confirms an effective licensing path for each affected state,
    compliance confirms permissible reliance with adequate records or remediation,
    diligence clears the alerts and SAR history, and testing shows no monitoring gap.
    The bonus structure remains unknown.\n\n**Support limit**\n\nThis is generated
    analysis based on reported matter facts. No external authority was retrieved.\n\n</details>",

    "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md", "title": "facts.md", "support_state":
    "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt": "# Known Facts\n\n-
    Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n-
    Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s
    app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and full access
    to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already
    KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
    Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.\n-
    Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has pass/fail
    results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users onboarded before
    2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
    terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s
    engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
    first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a
    handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.\n- Migration
    moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on
    day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification
    of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC
    ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone
    but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
    transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
    plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.\n-
    Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year
    at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured?
    — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP
    program currently permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
    or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-
    What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last year?
    — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four new markets opened
    by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing
    licenses or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023
    Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic
    Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification and recordkeeping obligations? —
    It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on
    Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have the ~40 open alerts and
    the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
    — The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n-
    For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what is the
    plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before onboarding those
    customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses
    for the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s
    existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can
    be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n- [Assumption]
    The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML
    program obligations without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction
    monitoring repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring
    gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
    MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption]
    Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
    [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase, which
    affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure
    not yet confirmed).\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0, "end": 3962, "text":
    "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15
    (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
    into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance
    and full access to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor
    users were already KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses
    (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening
    four new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024;
    Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents for
    users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party
    SaaS whose contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction
    feed at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with
    a $50 bonus on first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open
    alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read
    them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
    Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.\n-
    Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were already
    KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
    results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded
    before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
    terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
    engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
    from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay
    acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does
    Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another institution''s
    prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification required? — Not sure
    / need to check with compliance\n- What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts
    and the SARs from the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n-
    For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan
    to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its own? — Use/assume
    Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
    what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
    and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP
    program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have
    the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed,
    and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed
    and remain in diligence.\n- For the four new markets opened by the combined license
    footprint, what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
    before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume
    Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption]
    Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable
    or can be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n- [Assumption]
    The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML
    program obligations without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction
    monitoring repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring
    gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
    MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption]
    Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
    [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase, which
    affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure
    not yet confirmed).\n"}], "content_truncated": false, "source_label": "facts.md"},
    {"source_id": "SRC-LOCAL-db6468aeb552bb44aa7b", "source_hash": "916b7009f261c21b7029be2ac4bab07fb4fd2909920244882bc8c02250c75dac",

    "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
    "# Issues and workstreams\n\n- Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay
    can operate under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive
    the acquisition\n- BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with
    missing underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent
    CIP/AML obligations\n- SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and
    manage Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability\n- Monitoring
    vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring when the SaaS contract
    terminates at close\n- Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any
    state money transmission or consumer protection implications\n- Customer account,
    contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
    -->\n- Open alerts, suspicious activity history, and acquisition diligence <!--
    issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-d22ea3957f21252a -->\n- State money-transmission authority
    after the asset purchase <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-65ae94508dcda1bf -->\n- Reliance
    on Harbor’s prior identity verification <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-30caa16a9234ccf2
    -->\n- Transaction-monitoring continuity at cutover <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-1d13a6636b8fbe60
    -->\n- Purchase-agreement authority and risk allocation <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-29efc151650e76a2
    -->\n- Customer terms, privacy, data transfers, and welcome bonus <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-fcd3954739e05481

    "source_version": "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a", "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money
    Transmission Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages":
    [{"unit_id": "p000014", "start": 0, "end": 1963, "page_number": 14, "section_label":
    null, "body_hash": "5b5d2f6c388b9bcf98252d205bb001dbdce26951229e0e6896dfecf0358be545",
    "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000014.md",
    "text": "14 \n \nARTICLE V \nMoney Transmission Licenses \nSection 5.01 License
    Required. \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the business of money transmission
    or \nadvertise, solicit, or hold itself out as providing money transmission unless
    the person is licensed \nunder this [Act]; \n(b) \n[Section 5.01(a)] does not
    apply to: \n(1) \nA person that is an authorized delegate of a person licensed
    under \nthis [Act] acting within the scope of authority conferred by a written
    contract with the \nlicensee; or \n(2) \nA person that is exempt pursuant to [Section
    3.01] and does not \nengage in money transmission outside the scope of such exemption.
    \n(c) \nA license issued under [Section 5.05] is not transferable or assignable.
    \nSection 5.02 Consistent State Licensing. \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing
    between [this state] and other states, the \n[Commissioner] is authorized and
    encouraged to: \n(1) \nimplement all licensing provisions of this [Act] in a manner
    that is \nconsistent with other states that have adopted this [Act]or multistate
    licensing processes; \nand \n(2) \nparticipate in nationwide protocols for licensing
    cooperation and \ncoordination among state regulators provided that such protocols
    are consistent with this \n[Act]. \n(b) \nIn order to fulfill the purposes of
    this [Act], the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to establish relationships
    or contracts with NMLS or other entities \ndesignated by NMLS to enable the [Commissioner]
    to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain records; \n(2) \ncoordinate multistate licensing
    processes and supervision processes; \n(3) \nprocess fees; and \n(4) \nfacilitate
    communication between [state] and licensees or other \npersons subject to this
    [Act]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS
    for all \naspects of licensing in accordance with this [Act], including but not
    limited to, license applications, \napplications for acquisitions of control,
    surety bonds, reporting, criminal history background\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved",
    "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",

    \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the business of money transmission or \nadvertise,
    solicit, or hold itself out as providing money transmission unless the person
    is licensed \nunder this [Act]; \n(b) \n[Section 5.01(a)] does not apply to: \n(1)
    \nA person that is an authorized delegate of a person licensed under \nthis [Act]
    acting within the scope of authority conferred by a written contract with the
    \nlicensee; or \n(2) \nA person that is exempt pursuant to [Section 3.01] and
    does not \nengage in money transmission outside the scope of such exemption. \n(c)
    \nA license issued under [Section 5.05] is not transferable or assignable. \nSection
    5.02 Consistent State Licensing. \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing between
    [this state] and other states, the \n[Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged
    to: \n(1) \nimplement all licensing provisions of this [Act] in a manner that
    is \nconsistent with other states that have adopted this [Act]or multistate licensing
    processes; \nand \n(2) \nparticipate in nationwide protocols for licensing cooperation
    and \ncoordination among state regulators provided that such protocols are consistent
    with this \n[Act]. \n(b) \nIn order to fulfill the purposes of this [Act], the
    [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to establish relationships or contracts
    with NMLS or other entities \ndesignated by NMLS to enable the [Commissioner]
    to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain records; \n(2) \ncoordinate multistate licensing
    processes and supervision processes; \n(3) \nprocess fees; and \n(4) \nfacilitate
    communication between [state] and licensees or other \npersons subject to this
    [Act]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS
    for all \naspects of licensing in accordance with this [Act], including but not
    limited to, license applications, \napplications for acquisitions of control,
    surety bonds, reporting, criminal history background\n"}, {"source_id": "SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538",
    "source_version": "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a", "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money
    Transmission Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages":
    [{"unit_id": "p000019", "start": 0, "end": 2376, "page_number": 19, "section_label":
    null, "body_hash": "b04604e2ac48d187b219bf1482524ee2b75b3d6c17bb0bb3e9ca87aeaff99147",
    "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000019.md",
    "text": "19 \n \n(C) \nEmployment history; \n(D) \nMedia history, including an
    electronic search of national and \nlocal publications, wire services, and business
    applications; and \n(E) \nFinancial services-related regulatory history, including
    but \nnot limited to, money transmission, securities, banking, insurance, and
    mortgage-\nrelated industries. \nSection 5.05 Issuance of License. \n(a) \nWhen
    an application for an original license under this [Act] appears to \ninclude all
    the items and addresses all of the matters that are required, the application
    is complete \nand the [Commissioner] shall promptly notify the applicant in a
    record of the date on which the \napplication is determined to be complete, and:13
    \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] shall approve or deny the application within \n120
    days after the completion date; or \n(2) \nif the application is not approved
    or denied within 120 days after the \ncompletion date: \n(A) \nthe application
    is approved; and \n(B) \nthe license takes effect as of the first business day
    after \nexpiration of the 120-day period. \n(C) \nThe [Commissioner] may for good
    cause extend the \napplication period. \n(b) \nA determination by the [Commissioner]
    that an application is complete and \nis accepted for processing means only that
    the application, on its face, appears to include all of the \nitems, including
    the Criminal Background Check response from the FBI, and address all of the \nmatters
    that are required, and is not an assessment of the substance of the application
    or of the \nsufficiency of the information provided. \n(c) \nWhen an application
    is filed and considered complete under this [Section \n5.05], the [Commissioner]
    shall investigate the applicant''s financial condition and responsibility, \nfinancial
    and business experience, character, and general fitness. The [Commissioner] may
    \nconduct an on-site investigation of the applicant, the reasonable cost of which
    the applicant must \npay. The [Commissioner] shall issue a license to an applicant
    under this [Section 5.05] if the \n[Commissioner] finds that all of the following
    conditions have been fulfilled: \n \n13 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and
    streamline the process of communicating when applications are \nreceived and when
    states consider them to have been complete. The intent of this [Act] is for the
    application period to \nbegin on the day an application is determined to be complete.\n"}],

    "text": "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. The renewal report
    must state or contain a \ndescription of each material change in information submitted
    by the licensee in its original license \napplication which has not been reported
    to the [Commissioner]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] for good cause may grant an
    extension of the renewal \ndate. \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and
    encouraged to utilize NMLS to \nprocess license renewals provided that such functionality
    is consistent with this [Section 5.06]. \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of License.
    \n(a) \nIf a licensee does not continue to meet the qualifications or satisfy
    the \nrequirements that apply to an applicant for a new money transmission license,
    the [Commissioner] \nmay suspend or revoke the licensee''s license in accordance
    with the procedures established by this \n[Act] or other applicable state law
    for such suspension or revocation. \n(b) \nAn applicant for a money transmission
    license must demonstrate that it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission
    licensee must at all times meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02,
    and 10.03] of this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control and Change of
    Key Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition of Control. \n(a) \nAny person, or group
    of persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall
    obtain the written approval of the [Commissioner] prior to acquiring control.
    \nAn individual is not deemed to acquire control of a licensee and is not subject
    to these acquisition \nof control provisions when that individual becomes a key
    individual in the ordinary course of \nbusiness. \n(b) \nA person, or group of
    persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall, in
    cooperation with the licensee: \n(1) \nSubmit an application in a form and in
    a medium prescribed by the \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable
    fee of [$X] with the request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner]
    may permit a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons acting in concert,
    to submit some or all information required by the \n[Commissioner] pursuant to
    [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe application required by [Section
    6.01(b)(1)] shall include information \nrequired by [Section 5.04] for any new
    key individuals that have not previously completed the \nrequirements of [Section
    5.04] for a licensee.\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",

    "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. The renewal report must

    by the licensee in its original license \napplication which has not been reported
    to the [Commissioner]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] for good cause may grant an
    extension of the renewal \ndate. \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and
    encouraged to utilize NMLS to \nprocess license renewals provided that such functionality
    is consistent with this [Section 5.06]. \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of License.
    \n(a) \nIf a licensee does not continue to meet the qualifications or satisfy
    the \nrequirements that apply to an applicant for a new money transmission license,
    the [Commissioner] \nmay suspend or revoke the licensee''s license in accordance
    with the procedures established by this \n[Act] or other applicable state law
    for such suspension or revocation. \n(b) \nAn applicant for a money transmission
    license must demonstrate that it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission
    licensee must at all times meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02,
    and 10.03] of this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control and Change of
    Key Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition of Control. \n(a) \nAny person, or group
    of persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall
    obtain the written approval of the [Commissioner] prior to acquiring control.
    \nAn individual is not deemed to acquire control of a licensee and is not subject
    to these acquisition \nof control provisions when that individual becomes a key
    individual in the ordinary course of \nbusiness. \n(b) \nA person, or group of
    persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall, in
    cooperation with the licensee: \n(1) \nSubmit an application in a form and in
    a medium prescribed by the \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable
    fee of [$X] with the request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner]
    may permit a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons acting in concert,
    to submit some or all information required by the \n[Commissioner] pursuant to
    [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe application required by [Section
    6.01(b)(1)] shall include information \nrequired by [Section 5.04] for any new

    "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a", "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization
    Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000022",
    "start": 0, "end": 2612, "page_number": 22, "section_label": null, "body_hash":
    "175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748", "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000022.md",
    "text": "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control under this
    [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items and address all of the matters
    that are required, the application shall \nbe considered complete and the [Commissioner]
    shall promptly notify the applicant in a record of \nthe date on which the application
    was determined to be complete and:15 \n \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] shall approve
    or deny the application within 60 \ndays after the completion date; or \n(2) \nif
    the application is not approved or denied within 60 days after the \ncompletion
    date: \n(A) \nthe application is approved; and \n(B) \nthe person, or group of
    persons acting in concert, are not \nprohibited from acquiring control. \n(3)
    \nThe [Commissioner] may for good cause extend the application \nperiod. \n(f)
    \nA determination by the [Commissioner] that an application is complete and \nis
    accepted for processing means only that the application, on its face, appears
    to include all of the \nitems and address all of the matters that are required,
    and is not an assessment of the substance of \nthe application or of the sufficiency
    of the information provided. \n(g) \nWhen an application is filed and considered
    complete under [Section \n6.01(e)], the [Commissioner] shall investigate the financial
    condition and responsibility, financial \nand business experience, character,
    and general fitness of the person, or group of persons acting in \nconcert, seeking
    to acquire control. The [Commissioner] shall approve an acquisition of control
    \npursuant to this [Section 6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds that all of the
    following conditions have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe requirements of subsections
    (b) and (d) have been met, as \napplicable; and \n(2) \nthe financial condition
    and responsibility, financial and business \nexperience, competence, character,
    and general fitness of the person, or group of persons \nacting in concert, seeking
    to acquire control; and the competence, experience, character, \nand general fitness
    of the key individuals and persons that would be in control of the \nlicensee
    after the acquisition of control indicate that it is in the interest of the public
    to \npermit the person, or group of persons acting in concert, to control the
    licensee. \n(h) \nIf an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to a multistate
    licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and streamline the process
    of communicating when applications are \nreceived and when states consider them
    to have been complete. The intent of this Act is for the application period to
    \nbegin on the day an application is determined to be complete.\n"}], "support_state":

    date: \n(A) \nthe application is approved; and \n(B) \nthe person, or group of
    persons acting in concert, are not \nprohibited from acquiring control. \n(3)
    \nThe [Commissioner] may for good cause extend the application \nperiod. \n(f)
    \nA determination by the [Commissioner] that an application is complete and \nis
    accepted for processing means only that the application, on its face, appears
    to include all of the \nitems and address all of the matters that are required,
    and is not an assessment of the substance of \nthe application or of the sufficiency
    of the information provided. \n(g) \nWhen an application is filed and considered

    and general fitness of the person, or group of persons acting in \nconcert, seeking

    \npursuant to this [Section 6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds that all of the
    following conditions have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe requirements of subsections
    (b) and (d) have been met, as \napplicable; and \n(2) \nthe financial condition
    and responsibility, financial and business \nexperience, competence, character,
    and general fitness of the person, or group of persons \nacting in concert, seeking
    to acquire control; and the competence, experience, character, \nand general fitness
    of the key individuals and persons that would be in control of the \nlicensee
    after the acquisition of control indicate that it is in the interest of the public
    to \npermit the person, or group of persons acting in concert, to control the
    licensee. \n(h) \nIf an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to a multistate
    licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and streamline the process
    of communicating when applications are \nreceived and when states consider them

    "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act", "extraction_state":
    "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000023", "start": 0, "end": 2523,
    "page_number": 23, "section_label": null, "body_hash": "83a664c778fbc9de0b4d13270e2a918f6488b461db1a6617e3d36032163068ca",
    "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000023.md",
    "text": "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged
    to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead investigative state for the purpose
    of [Section 6.01(g)] if the \nlead investigative state has sufficient staffing,
    expertise, and minimum standards; or \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead investigative
    state, the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to investigate the applicant
    pursuant to [Section 6.01(g)] and \nthe timeframes established by agreement through
    the multistate licensing process. \n(i) \nThe [Commissioner] shall issue a formal
    written notice of the denial of an \napplication to acquire control within thirty
    (30) days of the decision to deny the application. The \n[Commissioner] shall
    set forth in the notice of denial the specific reasons for the denial of the \napplication.
    An applicant whose application is denied by the [Commissioner] under this [Section
    \n6.01(i)] may appeal within thirty (30) days16 after receipt of the written notice
    of the denial \n[pursuant to state administrative law procedures]. \n(j) \nThe
    requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to any of the \nfollowing:
    \n(1) \nA person that acts as a proxy for the sole purpose of voting at a \ndesignated
    meeting of the shareholders or holders of voting shares or voting interests of
    a \nlicensee or a person in control of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person that acquires
    control of a licensee by devise or descent; \n(3) \nA person that acquires control
    of a licensee as a personal \nrepresentative, custodian, guardian, conservator,
    or trustee, or as an officer appointed by a \ncourt of competent jurisdiction
    or by operation of law; \n(4) \nA person that is exempt under [Section 3.01(g)];
    \n(5) \nA person that the [Commissioner] determines is not subject to \n[Section
    6.01(a)] based on the public interest; \n(6) \nA public offering of securities
    of a licensee or a person in control of \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn internal reorganization
    of a person in control of the licensee \nwhere the ultimate person in control
    of the licensee remains the same. \n(k) \nPersons in [Sections 6.01(j)(2), (3),
    (4), (6), (7)] in cooperation with the \nlicensee shall notify the [Commissioner]
    within [15] days after the acquisition of control.17 \n \n16 Commentary: Administrative
    procedures for challenging a departmental decision may be derived from other \naspects
    of state law. In such a case, this Act should be adjusted to reflect the relevant
    administrative process. \n17 Commentary: Notice is satisfied upon updating the
    licensee’s NMLS record.\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",

    "source_hash": "83a664c778fbc9de0b4d13270e2a918f6488b461db1a6617e3d36032163068ca",

    and minimum standards; or \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead investigative state, the
    [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to investigate the applicant pursuant
    to [Section 6.01(g)] and \nthe timeframes established by agreement through the
    multistate licensing process. \n(i) \nThe [Commissioner] shall issue a formal

    set forth in the notice of denial the specific reasons for the denial of the \napplication.
    An applicant whose application is denied by the [Commissioner] under this [Section
    \n6.01(i)] may appeal within thirty (30) days16 after receipt of the written notice
    of the denial \n[pursuant to state administrative law procedures]. \n(j) \nThe
    requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to any of the \nfollowing:
    \n(1) \nA person that acts as a proxy for the sole purpose of voting at a \ndesignated
    meeting of the shareholders or holders of voting shares or voting interests of
    a \nlicensee or a person in control of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person that acquires
    control of a licensee by devise or descent; \n(3) \nA person that acquires control
    of a licensee as a personal \nrepresentative, custodian, guardian, conservator,

    \n(5) \nA person that the [Commissioner] determines is not subject to \n[Section
    6.01(a)] based on the public interest; \n(6) \nA public offering of securities

    "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a", "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization
    Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000024",
    "start": 0, "end": 2799, "page_number": 24, "section_label": null, "body_hash":
    "4732d9c2b053975a4d3cb27db8e99faa4baf45f71eb350fa519e31b5890ac680", "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000024.md",
    "text": "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1) \nThe requirements
    of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson that has complied with
    and received approval to engage in money transmission \nunder this [Act] or was
    identified as a person in control in a prior application filed with and \napproved
    by the [Commissioner] or by an MSB accredited state pursuant to a multistate \nlicensing
    process, provided that: \n(A) \nthe person has not had a license revoked or suspended
    or \ncontrolled a licensee that has had a license revoked or suspended while the
    person \nwas in control of the licensee in the previous 5-years; \n(B) \nif the
    person is a licensee, the person is well managed and \nhas received at least a
    satisfactory rating for compliance at its most recent \nexamination by an MSB
    accredited state if such rating was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee to be acquired
    is projected to meet the \nrequirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03]
    of this [Act] after the acquisition \nof control is completed, and if the person
    acquiring control is a licensee, that \nlicensee is also projected to meet the
    requirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and \n10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition
    of control is completed; \n(D) \nthe licensee to be acquired will not implement
    any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result of the acquisition of
    control, and if the person \nacquiring control is a licensee, that licensee also
    will not implement any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result of
    the acquisition of control;  and \n(E) \nthe person provides notice of the acquisition
    in cooperation \nwith the licensee and attests to [Section 6.01(l)(1)(A), (B),
    (C), and (D)] in a form \nand in a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. \n(2)
    \nIf the notice is not disapproved within 30 days after the date on \nwhich the
    notice was determined to be complete, the notice is deemed approved. \n(m) \nBefore
    filing an application for approval to acquire control of a licensee a \nperson
    may request in writing a determination from the [Commissioner] as to whether the
    person \nwould be considered a person in control of a licensee upon consummation
    of a proposed \ntransaction. If the [Commissioner] determines that the person
    would not be a person in control of \na licensee, the proposed Person and transaction
    is not subject to the requirements of [Section \n6.01(a) and (b)] of this [Act].
    \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing process includes a determination pursuant to
    \n[Section 6.01(m)] and an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to
    the multistate licensing \nprocess: \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and
    encouraged to accept the \ncontrol determination of a lead investigative state
    with sufficient staffing, expertise, and \nminimum standards for the purpose of
    [Section 6.01(m)]; or\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",

    "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md", "title": "facts.md", "support_state":
    "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt": "# Known Facts\n\n-
    Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n-
    Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s
    app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and full access
    to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already
    KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
    Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.\n-
    Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has pass/fail
    results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users onboarded before
    2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
    terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s
    engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
    first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a
    handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.\n- Migration
    moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on
    day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification
    of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC
    ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone
    but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
    transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
    plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.\n-
    Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year
    at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured?
    — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP
    program currently permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
    or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-
    What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last year?
    — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four new markets opened
    by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing
    licenses or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023
    Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic
    Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification and recordkeeping obligations? —
    It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on
    Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have the ~40 open alerts and
    the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
    — The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n-
    For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what is the
    plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before onboarding those
    customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses
    for the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s
    existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can
    be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n- [Assumption]
    The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML
    program obligations without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction
    monitoring repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring
    gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
    MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption]
    Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
    [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase, which
    affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure
    not yet confirmed).\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0, "end": 3962, "text":

    "title": "SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md", "support_state": "supplied", "source_type":
    "workspace", "available_excerpt": "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring
    Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer
    users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close,
    with one unified account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.\n-
    Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor
    holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined
    footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through
    a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but
    not the underlying documents for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction
    monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close; plan is to
    repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.\n- Marketing
    wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer, launching close+1.\n-
    Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year
    at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and
    12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
    account and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC;
    Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut
    down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone but underlying documents are
    missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is
    a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the
    transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40
    open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; none have
    been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
    (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently
    permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
    is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n- What
    is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last year? — Nothing
    reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four new markets opened by the combined
    footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses
    or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023 Harbor
    users with no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s
    own BSA/AML customer identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not
    yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s
    prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful
    of SARs from the last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open
    alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n- For
    the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what is the plan
    for state money transmission licensing or approval before onboarding those customers?
    — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four
    new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money
    transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained
    through the acquisition without new state approval\n- [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail
    results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations
    without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint
    can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring gap\n- [Assumption]
    Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state MTL regimes and federal
    BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself
    a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n- [Assumption] The
    acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase, which affects whether
    Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).\n",

    "# Research this issue for the dossier: Monitoring vendor transition: continuity\n\n##
    Question\n\nResearch this issue for the dossier: Monitoring vendor transition:
    continuity of transaction monitoring when the SaaS contract terminates at close.
    Harbor''s monitoring contract ends at close. A failed or untested change could
    create an immediate gap in detection, records, and case handling.\nLawyer''s accepted
    priorities (private matter context):\nMake KYC, alert resolution, and monitoring
    continuity formal close and migration gates.: These linked controls affect the
    full migrated population and can create immediate exposure that is difficult to
    repair later.\nProposed date leads; resolve each reference in saved records before

    Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000027",
    "start": 0, "end": 1943, "page_number": 27, "section_label": null, "body_hash":
    "512d4a7a3e1afc61a66c79b53548e6795e9f434d557b21d346fd4662aaafc705", "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000027.md",
    "text": "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements shall include or be accompanied
    by a \ncertificate of opinion of the independent certified public accountant or
    independent public \naccountant that is satisfactory in form and content to the
    [Commissioner]. If the certificate or \nopinion is qualified, the [Commissioner]
    may order the licensee to take any action as the \n[Commissioner] may find necessary
    to enable the independent or certified public accountant or \nindependent public
    accountant to remove the qualification. \nSection 7.03 Authorized Delegate Reporting.
    \n(a) \nEach licensee shall submit a report of authorized delegates within 45
    days \nof the end of the calendar quarter.20 The [Commissioner] is authorized
    and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS for the submission of the report required by
    this [Section 7.03(a)] provided that such \nfunctionality is consistent with the
    requirements of this [Section 7.03]. \n(b) \nThe authorized delegate report shall
    include, at a minimum, each authorized \ndelegate''s: \n(1) \nCompany legal name;
    \n(2) \nTaxpayer employer identification number; \n(3) \nPrincipal provider identifier;
    \n(4) \nPhysical address; \n(5) \nMailing address; \n(6) \nAny business conducted
    in other states; \n(7) \nAny fictitious or trade name; \n(8) \nContact person
    name, phone number, and email \n(9) \nStart date as licensee’s authorized delegate;
    \n(10) \nEnd date acting as licensee’s authorized delegate, if applicable;  \n(11)
    \n[Court orders pursuant to [Section 8.03];] and \n(12) \nAny other information
    the [Commissioner] reasonably requires with \nrespect to the authorized delegate.
    \nSection 7.04 Reports of Certain Events.21 \n \n20 Commentary: This language
    is designed to implement state use of the NMLS Uniform Authorized Agent Reporting
    \n(UAAR) process. \n21 Commentary: States are encouraged to utilize NMLS to satisfy
    Section 7.04 reporting requirements if NMLS \ndevelops new functionality to prioritize
    reporting of significant events.\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",

    "source_version": "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a", "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money
    Transmission Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages":
    [{"unit_id": "p000028", "start": 0, "end": 2132, "page_number": 28, "section_label":
    null, "body_hash": "80c098d06593529d6d6335e3b8a4fe8e8db356a8c5d82eb34a2001d27d642973",
    "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000028.md",
    "text": "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner]
    within one business \nday after the licensee has reason to know of the occurrence
    of any of the following events: \n(1) \nthe filing of a petition by or against
    the licensee under the \nUnited States Bankruptcy Code, 11 U.S.C. Section 101-110,
    as amended or recodified from \ntime to time, for bankruptcy or reorganization;
    \n(2) \nthe filing of a petition by or against the licensee for \nreceivership,
    the commencement of any other judicial or administrative proceeding for its \ndissolution
    or reorganization, or the making of a general assignment for the benefit of its
    \ncreditors; or \n(3) \nthe commencement of a proceeding to revoke or suspend
    its \nlicense in a state or country in which the licensee engages in business
    or is licensed. \n(b) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner]
    within three business \nday after the licensee has reason to know of the occurrence
    of any of the following events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of the licensee
    or of a key individual \nor person in control of the licensee for a felony; or
    \n(2) \na [charge or] conviction of an authorized delegate for a \nfelony. \nSection
    7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee and an authorized delegate shall file
    all reports required by federal currency \nreporting, record keeping, and suspicious
    activity reporting requirements as set forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and other
    federal and state laws pertaining to money laundering. The timely filing of \na
    complete and accurate report required under this [Section 7.05] with the appropriate
    federal \nagency is deemed compliant with the requirements of this [Section 7.05].
    \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a) \nLicensee shall maintain the following records,
    for determining its \ncompliance with this [Act] for at least [three] years: \n(1)
    \na record of each outstanding money transmission obligation \nsold; \n(2) \na
    general ledger posted at least monthly containing all asset, \nliability, capital,
    income, and expense accounts; \n(3) \nbank statements and bank reconciliation
    records; \n(4) \nrecords of outstanding money transmission obligations;\n"}],

    licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner] within three business \nday
    after the licensee has reason to know of the occurrence of any of the following
    events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of the licensee or of a key individual
    \nor person in control of the licensee for a felony; or \n(2) \na [charge or]
    conviction of an authorized delegate for a \nfelony. \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy
    Act Reports. \nA licensee and an authorized delegate shall file all reports required
    by federal currency \nreporting, record keeping, and suspicious activity reporting
    requirements as set forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and other federal and state
    laws pertaining to money laundering. The timely filing of \na complete and accurate
    report required under this [Section 7.05] with the appropriate federal \nagency
    is deemed compliant with the requirements of this [Section 7.05]. \nSection 7.06
    Records. \n(a) \nLicensee shall maintain the following records, for determining
    its \ncompliance with this [Act] for at least [three] years: \n(1) \na record
    of each outstanding money transmission obligation \nsold; \n(2) \na general ledger
    posted at least monthly containing all asset, \nliability, capital, income, and
    expense accounts; \n(3) \nbank statements and bank reconciliation records; \n(4)
    \nrecords of outstanding money transmission obligations;\n"}, {"source_id": "SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538",

    "text": "29 \n \n(5) \nrecords of each outstanding money transmission obligation
    \npaid within the [three]-year period; \n(6) \na list of the last known names

    other records the [Commissioner] reasonably requires \nby rule. \n(b) \nThe items
    specified in [Section 7.06(a)] may be maintained in any form of \nrecord. \n(c)
    \nRecords specified in [Section 7.06(a)] may be maintained outside this state
    \nif they are made accessible to the [Commissioner] on [seven] business-days''
    notice that is sent in \na record. \n(d) \nAll records maintained by the licensee
    as required in [Section 7.06(a)–(c)] \nare open to inspection by the [Commissioner]

    8.01 Relationship Between Licensee and Authorized Delegate. \n(a) \nIn this [Section
    8.01], \"remit\" means to make direct payments of money to \na licensee or its
    representative authorized to receive money or to deposit money in a bank in an
    \naccount specified by the licensee. \n(b) \nBefore a licensee is authorized to
    conduct business through an authorized \ndelegate or allows a person to act as
    the licensee''s authorized delegate, the licensee must: \n(1) \nadopt, and update
    as necessary, written policies and procedures \nreasonably designed to ensure
    that the licensee''s authorized delegates comply with \napplicable state and federal
    law; \n(2) \nenter into a written contract that complies with [Section 8.01(d)];
    \nand \n(3) \nconduct a reasonable risk-based background investigation sufficient
    \nfor the licensee to determine whether the authorized delegate has complied and

    delegate must operate in full compliance with this [Act]. \n(d) \nThe written
    contract required by [Section 8.01(b)] must be signed by the \nlicensee and the
    authorized delegate and, at a minimum, must:\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved",

    or authorized delegate and require the person to produce records regarding any
    \nmatter related to the condition and business of the licensee or authorized delegate.

    require to \nconduct a complete examination. The records must be provided at the
    location and in the format \nspecified by the [Commissioner], provided, the [Commissioner]
    may utilize multistate record \nproduction standards and examination procedures

    4.03(b)].8 \n(c) \nUnless otherwise directed by the [Commissioner], a licensee

    "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md", "title": "facts.md", "support_state":
    "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt": "# Known Facts\n\n-
    Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n-
    Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s
    app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and full access
    to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already
    KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
    Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.\n-
    Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has pass/fail
    results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users onboarded before
    2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
    terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s
    engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
    first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a
    handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.\n- Migration
    moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on
    day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification
    of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC
    ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone
    but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
    transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
    plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.\n-
    Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year
    at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured?
    — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP
    program currently permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
    or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-
    What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last year?
    — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four new markets opened
    by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing
    licenses or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023
    Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic
