    "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md", "title": "facts.md", "support_state":
    "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt": "# Known Facts\n\n-
    Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n-
    Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s
    app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and full access
    to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already
    KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
    Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.\n-
    Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has pass/fail
    results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users onboarded before
    2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
    terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s
    engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
    first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a
    handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.\n- Migration
    moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on
    day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification
    of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC
    ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone
    but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
    transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
    plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.\n-
    Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year
    at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured?
    — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP
    program currently permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
    or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-
    What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last year?
    — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four new markets opened
    by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing
    licenses or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023
    Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic
    Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification and recordkeeping obligations? —
    It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on
    Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have the ~40 open alerts and
    the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
    — The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n-
    For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what is the
    plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before onboarding those
    customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses
    for the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s
    existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can
    be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n- [Assumption]
    The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML
    program obligations without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction
    monitoring repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring
    gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
    MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption]
    Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
    [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase, which
    affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure
    not yet confirmed).\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0, "end": 3962, "text":

    "# Issues and workstreams\n\n- Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay
    can operate under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive
    the acquisition\n- BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with
    missing underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent
    CIP/AML obligations\n- SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and
    manage Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability\n- Monitoring
    vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring when the SaaS contract
    terminates at close\n- Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any
    state money transmission or consumer protection implications\n- Customer account,

    "SRC-LOCAL-8f6233be11b7205ffc25", "source_hash": "23fcb27105945705c2b19c1547c310303a49b7d909b07a52e0fe3323e0ae2e9a",

    "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-8f6233be11b7205ffc25.md",
    "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/dossier-requests/DOR-20260912-049f9c.md",
    "title": "DOR-20260912-049f9c.md", "support_state": "supplied", "source_type":
    "workspace", "available_excerpt": "## Preparation note\n\n**Result:** Legal and
    compliance review is required before the Nov 15 close. The migration is not only
    a technical data transfer.\n\n**Lawyer reframe:** Determine which pre-close and
    day-one actions could change the deal risk, exceed Mosaic’s legal authority, weaken
    anti-money-laundering controls, or harm customers. Then separate safe preparation
    from actions that require legal clearance.\n\nThe current plan relies on unconfirmed
    assumptions. Harbor’s licenses might not transfer in an asset purchase. Mosaic
    might not be able to rely on Harbor’s identity checks. About 40 alerts and several
    suspicious activity reports remain unreviewed. Harbor’s monitoring service will
    end at close, but the replacement has not been shown to work.\n\nThe safer route
    is a staged launch. Mosaic can complete reversible technical work before close.
    It should delay affected accounts, new markets, or full product access if a legal
    or compliance gate remains open.\n\n### Material issues\n\n- Unresolved alerts
    and suspicious activity history.\n- State money-transmission authority after the
    asset purchase.\n- Reliance on identity checks that lack underlying records.\n-
    Continuous transaction monitoring at cutover.\n- Purchase-agreement limits and
    allocation of compliance liabilities.\n- Customer terms, privacy notices, data
    transfers, and the $50 bonus.\n\n### Three business priorities\n\n1. **Protect
    the acquisition decision.** Review unresolved compliance matters before Mosaic
    accepts risk that is difficult to reverse.\n2. **Confirm lawful day-one service.**
    Verify that Mosaic can serve each account and market after an asset purchase.\n3.
    **Preserve a safe fallback.** Keep monitoring active and permit a staged launch
    if any required control is not ready.\n\n### First three issues to research\n\n1.
    **Open alerts and suspicious activity history.** The findings could change deal
    terms, closing conditions, remediation, or account eligibility.\n2. **State licensing.**
    Regulatory approval could take time and could prevent launch in the four new markets.\n3.
    **Identity-verification reliance.** Missing source records affect 240,000 consumers
    and 12,000 business accounts and could require re-verification or access limits.\n\n\n\n>
    A requested saved-record read was unavailable. The writer used the material available.\n",

    accounts move into our app on day 1 post-close. One unified account, one balance,
    full access to our product set.\nNo re-verification — they were already KYC''d
    by Harbor.\nHarbor holds MTLs in 38 states, we hold 41. Combined that''s 44 —
    nice win, opens four new markets.\nHarbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut
    down in 2024. We have pass/fail results for everyone, but not the underlying documents
    for users onboarded before 2023.\nHarbor''s monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
    contract terminates at close. Plan is to repoint their transaction feed at our
    engine on day 1.\nMarketing wants a \"Welcome\" campaign with a $50 bonus on first
    transfer, launching close+1.\nDiligence flagged that Harbor has ~40 open alerts
    and \"a handful\" of SARs from the last year. Nobody''s read them yet.\n\nDoes

      path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8
    request_text: '# Original Request


      From: Dana, PM — Growth & Integration

      Subject: Harbor migration — anything here need legal?


      We''re acquiring Harbor Pay. Close is targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks). Migration
      plan:


      240k consumer users, 12k business accounts move into our app on day 1 post-close.
      One unified account, one balance, full access to our product set.

      No re-verification — they were already KYC''d by Harbor.

      Harbor holds MTLs in 38 states, we hold 41. Combined that''s 44 — nice win,
      opens four new markets.

      Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024. We have pass/fail
      results for everyone, but not the underlying documents for users onboarded before
      2023.

      Harbor''s monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close.
      Plan is to repoint their transaction feed at our engine on day 1.

      Marketing wants a "Welcome" campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer, launching
      close+1.

      Diligence flagged that Harbor has ~40 open alerts and "a handful" of SARs from
      the last year. Nobody''s read them yet.


      Does any of this need legal before close? It''s really just a data migration.

      '
    recommendation:
      matter_id: MAT-20260909-d89ad8
      path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/recommendations.md
      content: '## Working position


        The Harbor Pay migration needs legal and compliance review before the planned
        close. The leading concern is that an asset purchase generally requires Mosaic
        Relay to confirm its own authority to operate in each state; the current plan
        to use or assume Harbor''s licenses is not established as legally effective.


        The second concern is BSA/AML readiness. Mosaic Relay has not confirmed whether
        its AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC, and underlying
        records are missing for some pre-2023 users. Harbor''s open alerts and SAR
        history also remain unread. These gaps make a day-one migration without re-verification
        or account restrictions difficult to support.


        Transaction monitoring continuity is also material because Harbor''s vendor
        ends at close. The repointed feed should be tested and validated before migrated
        users receive full access. The $50 bonus is lower priority but still needs
        review once its eligibility, funding, terms, and disclosures are known.


        ## Plausible alternatives


        A narrower launch could exclude the four new markets, restrict users whose
        KYC evidence is incomplete, or delay full product access until alert review
        and monitoring validation finish. A full day-one launch remains possible only
        if state licensing, AML/CIP reliance, alert handling, and monitoring continuity
        are confirmed.


        ## Material facts and assumptions


        Reported facts include the asset-purchase structure, the current plan to rely
        on Harbor''s licenses, the lack of a compliance answer on KYC reliance, and
        the unread alerts and SAR history. The analysis assumes both entities conduct
        regulated money-transmission activity and that Mosaic Relay will become the
        operating provider immediately after close. It does not assume that Harbor''s
        licenses transfer or that Harbor''s KYC is sufficient.


        ## What could change this view


        The view could change if state counsel confirms an effective licensing path
        for each affected state, compliance confirms permissible reliance with adequate
        records or remediation, diligence clears the alerts and SAR history, and testing
        shows no monitoring gap. The bonus structure remains unknown.


        ## Support limit


        This is generated analysis based on reported matter facts. No external authority
        was retrieved.'

          current plan to use or assume Harbor''s licenses is not established as legally
          effective.


          The second concern is BSA/AML readiness. Mosaic Relay has not confirmed
          whether its AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC, and
          underlying records are missing for some pre-2023 users. Harbor''s open alerts
          and SAR history also remain unread. These gaps make a day-one migration
          without re-verification or account restrictions difficult to support.


          Transaction monitoring continuity is also material because Harbor''s vendor
          ends at close. The repointed feed should be tested and validated before
          migrated users receive full access. The $50 bonus is lower priority but
          still needs review once its eligibility, funding, terms, and disclosures
          are known.

          <summary>Earlier saved position — 2026-09-09T20:57:53+00:00</summary>


          **Working position**


          The Harbor Pay migration needs legal and compliance review before the planned
          close. The leading concern is that an asset purchase generally requires
          Mosaic Relay to confirm its own authority to operate in each state; the
          current plan to use or assume Harbor''s licenses is not established as legally
          effective.


          The second concern is BSA/AML readiness. Mosaic Relay has not confirmed
          whether its AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC, and
          underlying records are missing for some pre-2023 users. Harbor''s open alerts
          and SAR history also remain unread. These gaps make a day-one migration
          without re-verification or account restrictions difficult to support.


          Transaction monitoring continuity is also material because Harbor''s vendor
          ends at close. The repointed feed should be tested and validated before
          migrated users receive full access. The $50 bonus is lower priority but
          still needs review once its eligibility, funding, terms, and disclosures
          are known.


          **Plausible alternatives**


          A narrower launch could exclude the four new markets, restrict users whose
          KYC evidence is incomplete, or delay full product access until alert review
          and monitoring validation finish. A full day-one launch remains possible
          only if state licensing, AML/CIP reliance, alert handling, and monitoring
          continuity are confirmed.


          **Material facts and assumptions**


          Reported facts include the asset-purchase structure, the current plan to
          rely on Harbor''s licenses, the lack of a compliance answer on KYC reliance,
          and the unread alerts and SAR history. The analysis assumes both entities
          conduct regulated money-transmission activity and that Mosaic Relay will
          become the operating provider immediately after close. It does not assume
          that Harbor''s licenses transfer or that Harbor''s KYC is sufficient.


          **What could change this view**


          The view could change if state counsel confirms an effective licensing path
          for each affected state, compliance confirms permissible reliance with adequate
          records or remediation, diligence clears the alerts and SAR history, and
          testing shows no monitoring gap. The bonus structure remains unknown.


          **Support limit**


          This is generated analysis based on reported matter facts. No external authority
          was retrieved.


          </details>'

                available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


                  - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                  weeks out).

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                  - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by
                  Harbor.

                  - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                  Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                  markets.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                  has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed
                  at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                  - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                  transfer, launching close+1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance.

                  - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                  were already KYC''d.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                  results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to
                  Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                  - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                  (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                  - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                  on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
                  is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                  - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                  the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                  Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                  apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                  - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                  what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                  identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known
                  whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s
                  prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                  - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                  year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
                  and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                  what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                  before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                  to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                  ## Assumptions


                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                  and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                  the acquisition without new state approval

                  - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                  Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                  documents

                  - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                  and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                  - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                  to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                  in 41 states (per the request).

                  - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                  purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert
                  obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                  '

              - source_id: SRC-LOCAL-db6468aeb552bb44aa7b
                source_hash: 916b7009f261c21b7029be2ac4bab07fb4fd2909920244882bc8c02250c75dac

                path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-db6468aeb552bb44aa7b.md
                original_path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/issues.md
                title: issues.md
                support_state: supplied
                source_type: workspace
                available_excerpt: '# Issues and workstreams


                  - Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
                  under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs
                  transfer/survive the acquisition

                  - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with
                  missing underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic
                  Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations

                  - SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage
                  Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

                  - Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
                  when the SaaS contract terminates at close

                  - Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
                  money transmission or consumer protection implications

                  - Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
                  -->

                  - Open alerts, suspicious activity history, and acquisition diligence
                  <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-d22ea3957f21252a -->

                  - State money-transmission authority after the asset purchase <!--
                  issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-65ae94508dcda1bf -->

                  - Reliance on Harbor’s prior identity verification <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-30caa16a9234ccf2
                  -->

                  - Transaction-monitoring continuity at cutover <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-1d13a6636b8fbe60
                  -->

                  - Purchase-agreement authority and risk allocation <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-29efc151650e76a2
                  -->

                  - Customer terms, privacy, data transfers, and welcome bonus <!--
                  issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-fcd3954739e05481 -->

                  '

                  text: "14 \n \nARTICLE V \nMoney Transmission Licenses \nSection
                    5.01 License Required. \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the
                    business of money transmission or \nadvertise, solicit, or hold
                    itself out as providing money transmission unless the person is
                    licensed \nunder this [Act]; \n(b) \n[Section 5.01(a)] does not
                    apply to: \n(1) \nA person that is an authorized delegate of a
                    person licensed under \nthis [Act] acting within the scope of
                    authority conferred by a written contract with the \nlicensee;
                    or \n(2) \nA person that is exempt pursuant to [Section 3.01]
                    and does not \nengage in money transmission outside the scope
                    of such exemption. \n(c) \nA license issued under [Section 5.05]
                    is not transferable or assignable. \nSection 5.02 Consistent State
                    Licensing. \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing between [this
                    state] and other states, the \n[Commissioner] is authorized and
                    encouraged to: \n(1) \nimplement all licensing provisions of this
                    [Act] in a manner that is \nconsistent with other states that
                    have adopted this [Act]or multistate licensing processes; \nand
                    \n(2) \nparticipate in nationwide protocols for licensing cooperation
                    and \ncoordination among state regulators provided that such protocols
                    are consistent with this \n[Act]. \n(b) \nIn order to fulfill
                    the purposes of this [Act], the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized
                    and encouraged to establish relationships or contracts with NMLS
                    or other entities \ndesignated by NMLS to enable the [Commissioner]
                    to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain records; \n(2) \ncoordinate multistate
                    licensing processes and supervision processes; \n(3) \nprocess
                    fees; and \n(4) \nfacilitate communication between [state] and
                    licensees or other \npersons subject to this [Act]. \n(c) \nThe
                    [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS for
                    all \naspects of licensing in accordance with this [Act], including
                    but not limited to, license applications, \napplications for acquisitions
                    of control, surety bonds, reporting, criminal history background\n"

                  section_label: null
                  body_hash: b04604e2ac48d187b219bf1482524ee2b75b3d6c17bb0bb3e9ca87aeaff99147
                  path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000019.md
                  text: "19 \n \n(C) \nEmployment history; \n(D) \nMedia history,
                    including an electronic search of national and \nlocal publications,
                    wire services, and business applications; and \n(E) \nFinancial
                    services-related regulatory history, including but \nnot limited
                    to, money transmission, securities, banking, insurance, and mortgage-\nrelated
                    industries. \nSection 5.05 Issuance of License. \n(a) \nWhen an
                    application for an original license under this [Act] appears to
                    \ninclude all the items and addresses all of the matters that
                    are required, the application is complete \nand the [Commissioner]
                    shall promptly notify the applicant in a record of the date on
                    which the \napplication is determined to be complete, and:13 \n(1)
                    \nThe [Commissioner] shall approve or deny the application within
                    \n120 days after the completion date; or \n(2) \nif the application
                    is not approved or denied within 120 days after the \ncompletion
                    date: \n(A) \nthe application is approved; and \n(B) \nthe license
                    takes effect as of the first business day after \nexpiration of
                    the 120-day period. \n(C) \nThe [Commissioner] may for good cause
                    extend the \napplication period. \n(b) \nA determination by the
                    [Commissioner] that an application is complete and \nis accepted
                    for processing means only that the application, on its face, appears
                    to include all of the \nitems, including the Criminal Background
                    Check response from the FBI, and address all of the \nmatters
                    that are required, and is not an assessment of the substance of
                    the application or of the \nsufficiency of the information provided.
                    \n(c) \nWhen an application is filed and considered complete under
                    this [Section \n5.05], the [Commissioner] shall investigate the
                    applicant's financial condition and responsibility, \nfinancial
                    and business experience, character, and general fitness. The [Commissioner]
                    may \nconduct an on-site investigation of the applicant, the reasonable
                    cost of which the applicant must \npay. The [Commissioner] shall
                    issue a license to an applicant under this [Section 5.05] if the
                    \n[Commissioner] finds that all of the following conditions have
                    been fulfilled: \n \n13 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and
                    streamline the process of communicating when applications are
                    \nreceived and when states consider them to have been complete.
                    The intent of this [Act] is for the application period to \nbegin
                    on the day an application is determined to be complete.\n"

                  path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000021.md
                  text: "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. The
                    renewal report must state or contain a \ndescription of each material
                    change in information submitted by the licensee in its original
                    license \napplication which has not been reported to the [Commissioner].
                    \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] for good cause may grant an extension
                    of the renewal \ndate. \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized
                    and encouraged to utilize NMLS to \nprocess license renewals provided
                    that such functionality is consistent with this [Section 5.06].
                    \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of License. \n(a) \nIf a licensee does
                    not continue to meet the qualifications or satisfy the \nrequirements
                    that apply to an applicant for a new money transmission license,
                    the [Commissioner] \nmay suspend or revoke the licensee's license
                    in accordance with the procedures established by this \n[Act]
                    or other applicable state law for such suspension or revocation.
                    \n(b) \nAn applicant for a money transmission license must demonstrate
                    that it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission licensee
                    must at all times meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01,
                    10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of
                    Control and Change of Key Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition
                    of Control. \n(a) \nAny person, or group of persons acting in
                    concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall obtain
                    the written approval of the [Commissioner] prior to acquiring
                    control. \nAn individual is not deemed to acquire control of a
                    licensee and is not subject to these acquisition \nof control
                    provisions when that individual becomes a key individual in the
                    ordinary course of \nbusiness. \n(b) \nA person, or group of persons
                    acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee
                    shall, in cooperation with the licensee: \n(1) \nSubmit an application
                    in a form and in a medium prescribed by the \n[Commissioner];
                    and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable fee of [$X] with the request
                    for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner] may permit
                    a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons acting in concert,
                    to submit some or all information required by the \n[Commissioner]
                    pursuant to [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe
                    application required by [Section 6.01(b)(1)] shall include information
                    \nrequired by [Section 5.04] for any new key individuals that
                    have not previously completed the \nrequirements of [Section 5.04]
                    for a licensee.\n"

                  \n(a) \nAny person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking
                  to acquire control \nof a licensee shall obtain the written approval

                - unit_id: p000022

                  body_hash: 175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748
                  path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000022.md
                  text: "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control
                    under this [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items and
                    address all of the matters that are required, the application
                    shall \nbe considered complete and the [Commissioner] shall promptly
                    notify the applicant in a record of \nthe date on which the application
                    was determined to be complete and:15 \n \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner]
                    shall approve or deny the application within 60 \ndays after the
                    completion date; or \n(2) \nif the application is not approved
                    or denied within 60 days after the \ncompletion date: \n(A) \nthe
                    application is approved; and \n(B) \nthe person, or group of persons
                    acting in concert, are not \nprohibited from acquiring control.
                    \n(3) \nThe [Commissioner] may for good cause extend the application
                    \nperiod. \n(f) \nA determination by the [Commissioner] that an
                    application is complete and \nis accepted for processing means
                    only that the application, on its face, appears to include all
                    of the \nitems and address all of the matters that are required,
                    and is not an assessment of the substance of \nthe application
                    or of the sufficiency of the information provided. \n(g) \nWhen
                    an application is filed and considered complete under [Section
                    \n6.01(e)], the [Commissioner] shall investigate the financial
                    condition and responsibility, financial \nand business experience,
                    character, and general fitness of the person, or group of persons
                    acting in \nconcert, seeking to acquire control. The [Commissioner]
                    shall approve an acquisition of control \npursuant to this [Section
                    6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds that all of the following conditions
                    have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe requirements of subsections
                    (b) and (d) have been met, as \napplicable; and \n(2) \nthe financial
                    condition and responsibility, financial and business \nexperience,
                    competence, character, and general fitness of the person, or group
                    of persons \nacting in concert, seeking to acquire control; and
                    the competence, experience, character, \nand general fitness of
                    the key individuals and persons that would be in control of the
                    \nlicensee after the acquisition of control indicate that it is
                    in the interest of the public to \npermit the person, or group
                    of persons acting in concert, to control the licensee. \n(h) \nIf
                    an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to a multistate
                    licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and streamline
                    the process of communicating when applications are \nreceived
                    and when states consider them to have been complete. The intent
                    of this Act is for the application period to \nbegin on the day
                    an application is determined to be complete.\n"

                path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000022.md
                source_hash: 175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748
                source_label: '[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — Page
                  22, characters 0–2612'
                unit_id: p000022
                locator: Page 22, characters 0–2612
                available_excerpt: "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition
                  of control under this [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the
                  items and address all of the matters that are required, the application
                  shall \nbe considered complete and the [Commissioner] shall promptly
                  notify the applicant in a record of \nthe date on which the application
                  was determined to be complete and:15 \n \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner]
                  shall approve or deny the application within 60 \ndays after the
                  completion date; or \n(2) \nif the application is not approved or
                  denied within 60 days after the \ncompletion date: \n(A) \nthe application
                  is approved; and \n(B) \nthe person, or group of persons acting
                  in concert, are not \nprohibited from acquiring control. \n(3) \nThe
                  [Commissioner] may for good cause extend the application \nperiod.
                  \n(f) \nA determination by the [Commissioner] that an application
                  is complete and \nis accepted for processing means only that the
                  application, on its face, appears to include all of the \nitems
                  and address all of the matters that are required, and is not an
                  assessment of the substance of \nthe application or of the sufficiency
                  of the information provided. \n(g) \nWhen an application is filed
                  and considered complete under [Section \n6.01(e)], the [Commissioner]
                  shall investigate the financial condition and responsibility, financial
                  \nand business experience, character, and general fitness of the
                  person, or group of persons acting in \nconcert, seeking to acquire
                  control. The [Commissioner] shall approve an acquisition of control
                  \npursuant to this [Section 6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds that
                  all of the following conditions have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe
                  requirements of subsections (b) and (d) have been met, as \napplicable;
                  and \n(2) \nthe financial condition and responsibility, financial
                  and business \nexperience, competence, character, and general fitness
                  of the person, or group of persons \nacting in concert, seeking
                  to acquire control; and the competence, experience, character, \nand
                  general fitness of the key individuals and persons that would be
                  in control of the \nlicensee after the acquisition of control indicate
                  that it is in the interest of the public to \npermit the person,
                  or group of persons acting in concert, to control the licensee.
                  \n(h) \nIf an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to
                  a multistate licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate
                  and streamline the process of communicating when applications are
                  \nreceived and when states consider them to have been complete.
                  The intent of this Act is for the application period to \nbegin
                  on the day an application is determined to be complete.\n"
              - source_id: SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538
                source_version: dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a
                title: '[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act'
                extraction_state: complete
                selected_passages:

                  page_number: 23
                  section_label: null
                  body_hash: 83a664c778fbc9de0b4d13270e2a918f6488b461db1a6617e3d36032163068ca
                  path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000023.md
                  text: "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized
                    and encouraged to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead
                    investigative state for the purpose of [Section 6.01(g)] if the
                    \nlead investigative state has sufficient staffing, expertise,
                    and minimum standards; or \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead investigative
                    state, the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to investigate
                    the applicant pursuant to [Section 6.01(g)] and \nthe timeframes
                    established by agreement through the multistate licensing process.
                    \n(i) \nThe [Commissioner] shall issue a formal written notice
                    of the denial of an \napplication to acquire control within thirty
                    (30) days of the decision to deny the application. The \n[Commissioner]
                    shall set forth in the notice of denial the specific reasons for
                    the denial of the \napplication. An applicant whose application
                    is denied by the [Commissioner] under this [Section \n6.01(i)]
                    may appeal within thirty (30) days16 after receipt of the written
                    notice of the denial \n[pursuant to state administrative law procedures].
                    \n(j) \nThe requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply
                    to any of the \nfollowing: \n(1) \nA person that acts as a proxy
                    for the sole purpose of voting at a \ndesignated meeting of the
                    shareholders or holders of voting shares or voting interests of
                    a \nlicensee or a person in control of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person
                    that acquires control of a licensee by devise or descent; \n(3)
                    \nA person that acquires control of a licensee as a personal \nrepresentative,
                    custodian, guardian, conservator, or trustee, or as an officer
                    appointed by a \ncourt of competent jurisdiction or by operation
                    of law; \n(4) \nA person that is exempt under [Section 3.01(g)];
                    \n(5) \nA person that the [Commissioner] determines is not subject
                    to \n[Section 6.01(a)] based on the public interest; \n(6) \nA
                    public offering of securities of a licensee or a person in control
                    of \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn internal reorganization of a person
                    in control of the licensee \nwhere the ultimate person in control
                    of the licensee remains the same. \n(k) \nPersons in [Sections
                    6.01(j)(2), (3), (4), (6), (7)] in cooperation with the \nlicensee
                    shall notify the [Commissioner] within [15] days after the acquisition
                    of control.17 \n \n16 Commentary: Administrative procedures for
                    challenging a departmental decision may be derived from other
                    \naspects of state law. In such a case, this Act should be adjusted
                    to reflect the relevant administrative process. \n17 Commentary:
                    Notice is satisfied upon updating the licensee’s NMLS record.\n"

                  text: "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1) \nThe
                    requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson
                    that has complied with and received approval to engage in money
                    transmission \nunder this [Act] or was identified as a person
                    in control in a prior application filed with and \napproved by
                    the [Commissioner] or by an MSB accredited state pursuant to a
                    multistate \nlicensing process, provided that: \n(A) \nthe person
                    has not had a license revoked or suspended or \ncontrolled a licensee
                    that has had a license revoked or suspended while the person \nwas
                    in control of the licensee in the previous 5-years; \n(B) \nif
                    the person is a licensee, the person is well managed and \nhas
                    received at least a satisfactory rating for compliance at its
                    most recent \nexamination by an MSB accredited state if such rating
                    was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee to be acquired is projected to
                    meet the \nrequirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03]
                    of this [Act] after the acquisition \nof control is completed,
                    and if the person acquiring control is a licensee, that \nlicensee
                    is also projected to meet the requirements of [Sections 10.01,
                    10.02, and \n10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition of control
                    is completed; \n(D) \nthe licensee to be acquired will not implement
                    any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result of the
                    acquisition of control, and if the person \nacquiring control
                    is a licensee, that licensee also will not implement any material
                    \nchanges to its business plan as a result of the acquisition
                    of control;  and \n(E) \nthe person provides notice of the acquisition
                    in cooperation \nwith the licensee and attests to [Section 6.01(l)(1)(A),
                    (B), (C), and (D)] in a form \nand in a medium prescribed by the
                    [Commissioner]. \n(2) \nIf the notice is not disapproved within
                    30 days after the date on \nwhich the notice was determined to
                    be complete, the notice is deemed approved. \n(m) \nBefore filing
                    an application for approval to acquire control of a licensee a
                    \nperson may request in writing a determination from the [Commissioner]
                    as to whether the person \nwould be considered a person in control
                    of a licensee upon consummation of a proposed \ntransaction. If
                    the [Commissioner] determines that the person would not be a person
                    in control of \na licensee, the proposed Person and transaction
                    is not subject to the requirements of [Section \n6.01(a) and (b)]
                    of this [Act]. \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing process includes
                    a determination pursuant to \n[Section 6.01(m)] and an applicant
                    avails itself or is otherwise subject to the multistate licensing
                    \nprocess: \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged
                    to accept the \ncontrol determination of a lead investigative
                    state with sufficient staffing, expertise, and \nminimum standards
                    for the purpose of [Section 6.01(m)]; or\n"

                source_hash: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409

                path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md
                original_path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md
                title: facts.md
                support_state: supplied
                source_type: workspace
                available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


                  - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                  weeks out).

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                  - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by
                  Harbor.

                  - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                  Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                  markets.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                  has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed
                  at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                  - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                  transfer, launching close+1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance.

                  - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                  were already KYC''d.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                  results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to
                  Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                  - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                  (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                  - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                  on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
                  is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                  - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                  the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                  Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                  apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                  - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                  what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                  identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known
                  whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s
                  prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                  - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                  year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
                  and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                  what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                  before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                  to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                  ## Assumptions


                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                  and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                  the acquisition without new state approval

                  - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                  Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                  documents

                  - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                  and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                  - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                  to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                  in 41 states (per the request).

                  text: '# Known Facts


                    - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15
                    (~10 weeks out).

                    - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                    into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                    account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                    - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
                    by Harbor.

                    - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
                    Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening
                    four new markets.

                    - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                    has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                    for users onboarded before 2023.

                    - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                    contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction
                    feed at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                    - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                    transfer, launching close+1.

                    - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
                    from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                    - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                    into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                    account and balance.

                    - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor
                    users were already KYC''d.

                    - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                    results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing
                    for users onboarded before 2023.

                    - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                    contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
                    feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                    - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
                    from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                    - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                    (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                    - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                    on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
                    is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                    - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                    the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                    - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                    Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses
                    or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                    - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                    what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                    identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet
                    known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance
                    on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                    - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                    year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
                    and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                    - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                    what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                    before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                    to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                    ## Assumptions


                    - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                    and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                    the acquisition without new state approval

                    - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                    Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                    documents

                    - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                    and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                    - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                    to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet
                    confirmed).

                    - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                    in 41 states (per the request).

                    - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                    purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert
                    obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                    '

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract

                  at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                  - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                  transfer, launching close+1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance.

                  - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                  were already KYC''d.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                  results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to
                  Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                  - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                  (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                  - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                  on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
                  is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                  - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                  the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                  Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                  apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                  - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                  what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                  identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known
                  whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s
                  prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                  - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                  year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
                  and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                  what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                  before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                  to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                  ## Assumptions


                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                  and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                  the acquisition without new state approval

                  - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                  Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                  documents

                  - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                  and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                  - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                  to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                  in 41 states (per the request).

                  - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                  purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert
                  obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                  '

                  text: '# Known Facts


                    - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15
                    (~10 weeks out).

                    - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                    into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                    account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                    - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
                    by Harbor.

                    - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
                    Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening
                    four new markets.

                    - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                    has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                    for users onboarded before 2023.

                    - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                    contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction
                    feed at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                    - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                    transfer, launching close+1.

                    - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
                    from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                    - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                    into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                    account and balance.

                    - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor
                    users were already KYC''d.

                    - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                    results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing
                    for users onboarded before 2023.

                    - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                    contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
                    feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                    - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
                    from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                    - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                    (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                    - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                    on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
                    is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                    - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                    the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                    - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                    Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses
                    or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                    - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                    what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                    identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet
                    known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance
                    on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                    - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                    year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
                    and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                    - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                    what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                    before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                    to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                    ## Assumptions


                    - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                    and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                    the acquisition without new state approval

                    - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                    Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                    documents

                    - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                    and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                    - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                    to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet
                    confirmed).

                    - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                    in 41 states (per the request).

                    - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                    purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert
                    obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                    '

                - unit_id: p000027
                  start: 0

                  page_number: 27
                  section_label: null
                  body_hash: 512d4a7a3e1afc61a66c79b53548e6795e9f434d557b21d346fd4662aaafc705
                  path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000027.md
                  text: "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements shall include
                    or be accompanied by a \ncertificate of opinion of the independent
                    certified public accountant or independent public \naccountant
                    that is satisfactory in form and content to the [Commissioner].
                    If the certificate or \nopinion is qualified, the [Commissioner]
                    may order the licensee to take any action as the \n[Commissioner]
                    may find necessary to enable the independent or certified public
                    accountant or \nindependent public accountant to remove the qualification.
                    \nSection 7.03 Authorized Delegate Reporting. \n(a) \nEach licensee
                    shall submit a report of authorized delegates within 45 days \nof
                    the end of the calendar quarter.20 The [Commissioner] is authorized
                    and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS for the submission of the report
                    required by this [Section 7.03(a)] provided that such \nfunctionality
                    is consistent with the requirements of this [Section 7.03]. \n(b)
                    \nThe authorized delegate report shall include, at a minimum,
                    each authorized \ndelegate's: \n(1) \nCompany legal name; \n(2)
                    \nTaxpayer employer identification number; \n(3) \nPrincipal provider
                    identifier; \n(4) \nPhysical address; \n(5) \nMailing address;
                    \n(6) \nAny business conducted in other states; \n(7) \nAny fictitious
                    or trade name; \n(8) \nContact person name, phone number, and
                    email \n(9) \nStart date as licensee’s authorized delegate; \n(10)
                    \nEnd date acting as licensee’s authorized delegate, if applicable;
                    \ \n(11) \n[Court orders pursuant to [Section 8.03];] and \n(12)
                    \nAny other information the [Commissioner] reasonably requires
                    with \nrespect to the authorized delegate. \nSection 7.04 Reports
                    of Certain Events.21 \n \n20 Commentary: This language is designed
                    to implement state use of the NMLS Uniform Authorized Agent Reporting
                    \n(UAAR) process. \n21 Commentary: States are encouraged to utilize
                    NMLS to satisfy Section 7.04 reporting requirements if NMLS \ndevelops
                    new functionality to prioritize reporting of significant events.\n"

                  \nSection 7.03 Authorized Delegate Reporting. \n(a) \nEach licensee
                  shall submit a report of authorized delegates within 45 days \nof

                source_version: dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a
                title: '[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act'
                extraction_state: complete
                selected_passages:
                - unit_id: p000028

                  page_number: 28
                  section_label: null
                  body_hash: 80c098d06593529d6d6335e3b8a4fe8e8db356a8c5d82eb34a2001d27d642973
                  path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000028.md
                  text: "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner]
                    within one business \nday after the licensee has reason to know
                    of the occurrence of any of the following events: \n(1) \nthe
                    filing of a petition by or against the licensee under the \nUnited
                    States Bankruptcy Code, 11 U.S.C. Section 101-110, as amended
                    or recodified from \ntime to time, for bankruptcy or reorganization;
                    \n(2) \nthe filing of a petition by or against the licensee for
                    \nreceivership, the commencement of any other judicial or administrative
                    proceeding for its \ndissolution or reorganization, or the making
                    of a general assignment for the benefit of its \ncreditors; or
                    \n(3) \nthe commencement of a proceeding to revoke or suspend
                    its \nlicense in a state or country in which the licensee engages
                    in business or is licensed. \n(b) \nA licensee shall file a report
                    with the [Commissioner] within three business \nday after the
                    licensee has reason to know of the occurrence of any of the following
                    events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of the licensee or of
                    a key individual \nor person in control of the licensee for a
                    felony; or \n(2) \na [charge or] conviction of an authorized delegate
                    for a \nfelony. \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee
                    and an authorized delegate shall file all reports required by
                    federal currency \nreporting, record keeping, and suspicious activity
                    reporting requirements as set forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act
                    and other federal and state laws pertaining to money laundering.
                    The timely filing of \na complete and accurate report required
                    under this [Section 7.05] with the appropriate federal \nagency
                    is deemed compliant with the requirements of this [Section 7.05].
                    \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a) \nLicensee shall maintain the following
                    records, for determining its \ncompliance with this [Act] for
                    at least [three] years: \n(1) \na record of each outstanding money
                    transmission obligation \nsold; \n(2) \na general ledger posted
                    at least monthly containing all asset, \nliability, capital, income,
                    and expense accounts; \n(3) \nbank statements and bank reconciliation
                    records; \n(4) \nrecords of outstanding money transmission obligations;\n"

                available_excerpt: "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a report with
                  the [Commissioner] within one business \nday after the licensee
                  has reason to know of the occurrence of any of the following events:
                  \n(1) \nthe filing of a petition by or against the licensee under
                  the \nUnited States Bankruptcy Code, 11 U.S.C. Section 101-110,
                  as amended or recodified from \ntime to time, for bankruptcy or
                  reorganization; \n(2) \nthe filing of a petition by or against the
                  licensee for \nreceivership, the commencement of any other judicial
                  or administrative proceeding for its \ndissolution or reorganization,
                  or the making of a general assignment for the benefit of its \ncreditors;
                  or \n(3) \nthe commencement of a proceeding to revoke or suspend
                  its \nlicense in a state or country in which the licensee engages
                  in business or is licensed. \n(b) \nA licensee shall file a report
                  with the [Commissioner] within three business \nday after the licensee
                  has reason to know of the occurrence of any of the following events:
                  \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of the licensee or of a key individual
                  \nor person in control of the licensee for a felony; or \n(2) \na
                  [charge or] conviction of an authorized delegate for a \nfelony.
                  \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee and an authorized
                  delegate shall file all reports required by federal currency \nreporting,
                  record keeping, and suspicious activity reporting requirements as
                  set forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and other federal and state
                  laws pertaining to money laundering. The timely filing of \na complete
                  and accurate report required under this [Section 7.05] with the
                  appropriate federal \nagency is deemed compliant with the requirements
                  of this [Section 7.05]. \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a) \nLicensee
                  shall maintain the following records, for determining its \ncompliance
                  with this [Act] for at least [three] years: \n(1) \na record of
                  each outstanding money transmission obligation \nsold; \n(2) \na
                  general ledger posted at least monthly containing all asset, \nliability,
                  capital, income, and expense accounts; \n(3) \nbank statements and
                  bank reconciliation records; \n(4) \nrecords of outstanding money
                  transmission obligations;\n"
