      "pdf_text", "text": "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1)
      \nThe requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson that
      has complied with and received approval to engage in money transmission \nunder
      this [Act] or was identified as a person in control in a prior application filed
      with and \napproved by the [Commissioner] or by an MSB accredited state pursuant
      to a multistate \nlicensing process, provided that: \n(A) \nthe person has not
      had a license revoked or suspended or \ncontrolled a licensee that has had a
      license revoked or suspended while the person \nwas in control of the licensee
      in the previous 5-years; \n(B) \nif the person is a licensee, the person is
      well managed and \nhas received at least a satisfactory rating for compliance
      at its most recent \nexamination by an MSB accredited state if such rating was
      given; \n(C) \nthe licensee to be acquired is projected to meet the \nrequirements
      of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition \nof
      control is completed, and if the person acquiring control is a licensee, that
      \nlicensee is also projected to meet the requirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02,
      and \n10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition of control is completed; \n(D)
      \nthe licensee to be acquired will not implement any material \nchanges to its
      business plan as a result of the acquisition of control, and if the person \nacquiring
      control is a licensee, that licensee also will not implement any material \nchanges
      to its business plan as a result of the acquisition of control;  and \n(E) \nthe
      person provides notice of the acquisition in cooperation \nwith the licensee
      and attests to [Section 6.01(l)(1)(A), (B), (C), and (D)] in a form \nand in
      a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. \n(2) \nIf the notice is not disapproved
      within 30 days after the date on \nwhich the notice was determined to be complete,
      the notice is deemed approved. \n(m) \nBefore filing an application for approval
      to acquire control of a licensee a \nperson may request in writing a determination
      from the [Commissioner] as to whether the person \nwould be considered a person
      in control of a licensee upon consummation of a proposed \ntransaction. If the
      [Commissioner] determines that the person would not be a person in control of
      \na licensee, the proposed Person and transaction is not subject to the requirements
      of [Section \n6.01(a) and (b)] of this [Act]. \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing

      avails itself or is otherwise subject to the multistate licensing \nprocess:
      \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to accept the \ncontrol

      "start": 0, "end": 2835, "page_number": 15, "section_label": null, "extraction_method":
      "pdf_text", "text": "15 \n \nchecks, credit checks, fee processing, and examinations.9
      \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS forms,
      \nprocesses, and functionalities in accordance with this [Act].10 In the event
      NMLS does not provide \nfunctionality, forms, or processes for a provision of
      this [Act], the [Commissioner] is authorized \nand encouraged to strive to implement
      the requirements in a manner that facilitates uniformity \nwith respect to licensing,
      supervision, reporting, and regulation of licensees which are licensed in \nmultiple
      jurisdictions. \n(e) \nWaive or Modify Requirements.\u2014 For the purpose of
      participating in the \nNationwide Multistate Licensing System & Registry, the
      Commissioner is authorized to waive or \nmodify, in whole or in part, by rule,
      regulation or order, any or all of the requirements and to \nestablish new requirements
      as reasonably necessary to participate in the Nationwide Multistate \nLicensing
      System & Registry. \n[Alternative to Section 5.02(e)]: The [Commissioner] is
      authorized and encouraged to establish \nand adopt, by rule or regulation, requirements
      for participation by applicants and licensees in \nNMLS upon the [Department''s]
      determination that each requirement is consistent with law, public \ninterest,
      and the purposes of this [Section 5.02].] \nSection 5.03 Application for License.
      \n(a) \nApplicants for a license shall apply in a form and in a medium as prescribed
      \nby the [Commissioner]. Each such form shall contain content as set forth by
      rule, regulation, \ninstruction or procedure of the [Commissioner] and may be
      changed or updated by the \n[Commissioner] in accordance with applicable law
      in order to carry out the purposes of this [Act] \nand maintain consistency
      with NMLS licensing standards and practices. The application must state \nor
      contain, as applicable: \n(1) \nthe legal name and residential and business
      addresses of the \napplicant and any fictitious or trade name used by the applicant
      in conducting its business; \n(2) \na list of any criminal convictions of the

      that such functionality is consistent with this [Section 5.06]. \nSection 5.07
      Maintenance of License. \n(a) \nIf a licensee does not continue to meet the
      qualifications or satisfy the \nrequirements that apply to an applicant for
      a new money transmission license, the [Commissioner] \nmay suspend or revoke
      the licensee''s license in accordance with the procedures established by this
      \n[Act] or other applicable state law for such suspension or revocation. \n(b)
      \nAn applicant for a money transmission license must demonstrate that it \nmeets
      or will meet, and a money transmission licensee must at all times meet, the
      requirements in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act]. \nARTICLE
      VI \nAcquisition of Control and Change of Key Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition
      of Control. \n(a) \nAny person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking
      to acquire control \nof a licensee shall obtain the written approval of the
      [Commissioner] prior to acquiring control. \nAn individual is not deemed to
      acquire control of a licensee and is not subject to these acquisition \nof control
      provisions when that individual becomes a key individual in the ordinary course
      of \nbusiness. \n(b) \nA person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking
      to acquire control \nof a licensee shall, in cooperation with the licensee:
      \n(1) \nSubmit an application in a form and in a medium prescribed by the \n[Commissioner];
      and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable fee of [$X] with the request for approval.
      \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner] may permit a licensee or the person,
      or \ngroup of persons acting in concert, to submit some or all information required
      by the \n[Commissioner] pursuant to [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS.
      \n(d) \nThe application required by [Section 6.01(b)(1)] shall include information
      \nrequired by [Section 5.04] for any new key individuals that have not previously
      completed the \nrequirements of [Section 5.04] for a licensee.\n", "has_more_in_unit":

      money and monetary value net of fees received for \nmoney transmission for the
      benefit of the licensee; \n(6) \nrequire the authorized delegate to prepare
      and maintain records as \nrequired by this [Act] or regulations implementing
      this [Act], or as reasonably requested \nby the [Commissioner]; \n(7) \nacknowledge
      that the authorized delegate consents to examination \nor investigation by the
      [Commissioner]; \n(8) \nstate that the licensee is subject to regulation by
      the [Commissioner] \nand that, as part of that regulation, the [Commissioner]
      may suspend or revoke an \nauthorized delegate designation or require the licensee
      to terminate an authorized delegate \ndesignation; and \n(9) \n(9)  acknowledge
      receipt of the written policies and procedures \nrequired under [Section 8.01(b)(1)].
      \n(e) \nIf the licensee''s license is suspended, revoked, surrendered, or expired,
      the \nlicensee must, within five (5) business days, provide documentation to
      the [Commissioner] that \nthe licensee has notified all applicable authorized
      delegates of the licensee whose names are in a \nrecord filed with the [Commissioner]
      of the suspension, revocation, surrender, or expiration of a \nlicense. Upon
      suspension, revocation, surrender, or expiration of a license, applicable authorized
      \ndelegates shall immediately cease to provide money transmission as an authorized
      delegate of the \nlicensee. \n(f) \nAn authorized delegate of a licensee holds
      in trust for the benefit of the \nlicensee all money net of fees received from

      \nAn authorized delegate may not use a subdelegate to conduct money \ntransmission
      on behalf of a licensee. \nSection 8.02 Unauthorized Activities \nA person shall
      not engage in the business of money transmission on behalf of a person \nnot
      licensed under this [Act]  or not exempt pursuant to [Article III] of this [Act].
      A person that \nengages in such activity provides money transmission to the
      same extent as if the person were a \nlicensee, and shall be jointly and severally
      liable with the unlicensed or nonexempt person. \nSection 8.03 [Optional]: Prohibited
      Authorized Delegates. \n(a) \nThe [appropriate court] in an action brought by
      a licensee shall have \njurisdiction to grant appropriate equitable or legal
      relief, including without limitation prohibiting \nthe authorized delegate from
      directly or indirectly acting as an authorized delegate for any licensee \nin
      this state and the payment of restitution, damages or other monetary relief,
      if the [appropriate \ncourt] finds that an authorized delegate failed to remit
      money in accordance with the written \ncontract required by [Section 8.01(b)]
      or as otherwise directed by the licensee or required by law. \n(b) \nIf the
      [appropriate court] issues an order prohibiting a person from acting as \nan
      authorized delegate for any licensee pursuant to [Section 8.03(a)], the licensee
      that brought the \naction shall report the order to the [Commissioner] within
      thirty (30) days and shall report the \norder through NMLS within ninety (90)
      days. \n(c) \nAn authorized delegate who holds money in trust for the benefit
      of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails to remit more than [$XXX] of such money
      is guilty of a [reference \nto state classification] felony. \n(d) \nAn authorized
      delegate who holds money in trust for the benefit of a \nlicensee and knowingly
      fails to remit no more than [$XXX] of such money is guilty of a [reference \nto
      state classification] misdemeanor. \nARTICLE IX  \nTimely Transmission, Refunds,
      and Disclosures \nSection 9.01 Timely Transmission. \n(a) \nEvery licensee shall
      forward all money received for transmission in \naccordance with the terms of
      the agreement between the licensee and the sender unless the licensee \nhas
      a reasonable belief or a reasonable basis to believe that the sender may be
      a victim of fraud or \nthat a crime or violation of law, rule, or regulation
      has occurred, is occurring, or may occur. \n(b) \nIf a licensee fails to forward
      money received for transmission in accordance \nwith this section, the licensee
      must respond to inquiries by the sender with the reason for the failure \n \n22

        title: How To Get A Money Transmitter License (MTL) in the U.S. - Fenergo

        section_label: Section 2
        body_offset: 297
        score: 47
        snippet: ions. Key requirements across states include demonstrating financial
          viability, often requiring a surety bond and capital reserves, passing comprehensive

      text: "14 \n \nARTICLE V \nMoney Transmission Licenses \nSection 5.01 License
        Required. \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the business of money transmission
        or \nadvertise, solicit, or hold itself out as providing money transmission
        unless the person is licensed \nunder this [Act]; \n(b) \n[Section 5.01(a)]
        does not apply to: \n(1) \nA person that is an authorized delegate of a person
        licensed under \nthis [Act] acting within the scope of authority conferred
        by a written contract with the \nlicensee; or \n(2) \nA person that is exempt
        pursuant to [Section 3.01] and does not \nengage in money transmission outside
        the scope of such exemption. \n(c) \nA license issued under [Section 5.05]
        is not transferable or assignable. \nSection 5.02 Consistent State Licensing.
        \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing between [this state] and other states,
        the \n[Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to: \n(1) \nimplement all
        licensing provisions of this [Act] in a manner that is \nconsistent with other
        states that have adopted this [Act]or multistate licensing processes; \nand
        \n(2) \nparticipate in nationwide protocols for licensing cooperation and
        \ncoordination among state regulators provided that such protocols are consistent
        with this \n[Act]. \n(b) \nIn order to fulfill the purposes of this [Act],
        the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to establish relationships
        or contracts with NMLS or other entities \ndesignated by NMLS to enable the
        [Commissioner] to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain records; \n(2) \ncoordinate
        multistate licensing processes and supervision processes; \n(3) \nprocess
        fees; and \n(4) \nfacilitate communication between [state] and licensees or
        other \npersons subject to this [Act]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized
        and encouraged to utilize NMLS for all \naspects of licensing in accordance
        with this [Act], including but not limited to, license applications, \napplications
        for acquisitions of control, surety bonds, reporting, criminal history background\n"
      has_more_in_unit: false
      paragraph_continues: false

    03b540a99c0c23d4323465a73826390a4c67148085e59172743982a87846ae06:
      status: read
      source_id: SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538

      body_hash: 175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748

      page_number: 22
      section_label: null
      extraction_method: pdf_text
      text: "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control under this
        [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items and address all of the matters
        that are required, the application shall \nbe considered complete and the
        [Commissioner] shall promptly notify the applicant in a record of \nthe date
        on which the application was determined to be complete and:15 \n \n(1) \nThe
        [Commissioner] shall approve or deny the application within 60 \ndays after
        the completion date; or \n(2) \nif the application is not approved or denied
        within 60 days after the \ncompletion date: \n(A) \nthe application is approved;
        and \n(B) \nthe person, or group of persons acting in concert, are not \nprohibited
        from acquiring control. \n(3) \nThe [Commissioner] may for good cause extend
        the application \nperiod. \n(f) \nA determination by the [Commissioner] that
        an application is complete and \nis accepted for processing means only that
        the application, on its face, appears to include all of the \nitems and address
        all of the matters that are required, and is not an assessment of the substance
        of \nthe application or of the sufficiency of the information provided. \n(g)
        \nWhen an application is filed and considered complete under [Section \n6.01(e)],
        the [Commissioner] shall investigate the financial condition and responsibility,
        financial \nand business experience, character, and general fitness of the
        person, or group of persons acting in \nconcert, seeking to acquire control.
        The [Commissioner] shall approve an acquisition of control \npursuant to this
        [Section 6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds that all of the following conditions
        have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe requirements of subsections (b) and (d)
        have been met, as \napplicable; and \n(2) \nthe financial condition and responsibility,
        financial and business \nexperience, competence, character, and general fitness
        of the person, or group of persons \nacting in concert, seeking to acquire
        control; and the competence, experience, character, \nand general fitness
        of the key individuals and persons that would be in control of the \nlicensee
        after the acquisition of control indicate that it is in the interest of the
        public to \npermit the person, or group of persons acting in concert, to control
        the licensee. \n(h) \nIf an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject
        to a multistate licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and streamline
        the process of communicating when applications are \nreceived and when states
        consider them to have been complete. The intent of this Act is for the application
        period to \nbegin on the day an application is determined to be complete.\n"
      has_more_in_unit: false
      paragraph_continues: false

      text: "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged
        to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead investigative state for the
        purpose of [Section 6.01(g)] if the \nlead investigative state has sufficient
        staffing, expertise, and minimum standards; or \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead
        investigative state, the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to
        investigate the applicant pursuant to [Section 6.01(g)] and \nthe timeframes
        established by agreement through the multistate licensing process. \n(i) \nThe
        [Commissioner] shall issue a formal written notice of the denial of an \napplication
        to acquire control within thirty (30) days of the decision to deny the application.
        The \n[Commissioner] shall set forth in the notice of denial the specific
        reasons for the denial of the \napplication. An applicant whose application
        is denied by the [Commissioner] under this [Section \n6.01(i)] may appeal
        within thirty (30) days16 after receipt of the written notice of the denial
        \n[pursuant to state administrative law procedures]. \n(j) \nThe requirements
        of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to any of the \nfollowing: \n(1)
        \nA person that acts as a proxy for the sole purpose of voting at a \ndesignated
        meeting of the shareholders or holders of voting shares or voting interests
        of a \nlicensee or a person in control of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person that
        acquires control of a licensee by devise or descent; \n(3) \nA person that
        acquires control of a licensee as a personal \nrepresentative, custodian,
        guardian, conservator, or trustee, or as an officer appointed by a \ncourt
        of competent jurisdiction or by operation of law; \n(4) \nA person that is
        exempt under [Section 3.01(g)]; \n(5) \nA person that the [Commissioner] determines
        is not subject to \n[Section 6.01(a)] based on the public interest; \n(6)
        \nA public offering of securities of a licensee or a person in control of
        \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn internal reorganization of a person in control
        of the licensee \nwhere the ultimate person in control of the licensee remains
        the same. \n(k) \nPersons in [Sections 6.01(j)(2), (3), (4), (6), (7)] in
        cooperation with the \nlicensee shall notify the [Commissioner] within [15]
        days after the acquisition of control.17 \n \n16 Commentary: Administrative
        procedures for challenging a departmental decision may be derived from other
        \naspects of state law. In such a case, this Act should be adjusted to reflect
        the relevant administrative process. \n17 Commentary: Notice is satisfied
        upon updating the licensee’s NMLS record.\n"

      text: "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1) \nThe requirements
        of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson that has complied
        with and received approval to engage in money transmission \nunder this [Act]
        or was identified as a person in control in a prior application filed with
        and \napproved by the [Commissioner] or by an MSB accredited state pursuant
        to a multistate \nlicensing process, provided that: \n(A) \nthe person has
        not had a license revoked or suspended or \ncontrolled a licensee that has
        had a license revoked or suspended while the person \nwas in control of the
        licensee in the previous 5-years; \n(B) \nif the person is a licensee, the
        person is well managed and \nhas received at least a satisfactory rating for
        compliance at its most recent \nexamination by an MSB accredited state if
        such rating was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee to be acquired is projected to
        meet the \nrequirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act]
        after the acquisition \nof control is completed, and if the person acquiring
        control is a licensee, that \nlicensee is also projected to meet the requirements
        of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and \n10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition
        of control is completed; \n(D) \nthe licensee to be acquired will not implement
        any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result of the acquisition
        of control, and if the person \nacquiring control is a licensee, that licensee
        also will not implement any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result
        of the acquisition of control;  and \n(E) \nthe person provides notice of
        the acquisition in cooperation \nwith the licensee and attests to [Section
        6.01(l)(1)(A), (B), (C), and (D)] in a form \nand in a medium prescribed by
        the [Commissioner]. \n(2) \nIf the notice is not disapproved within 30 days
        after the date on \nwhich the notice was determined to be complete, the notice
        is deemed approved. \n(m) \nBefore filing an application for approval to acquire
        control of a licensee a \nperson may request in writing a determination from
        the [Commissioner] as to whether the person \nwould be considered a person
        in control of a licensee upon consummation of a proposed \ntransaction. If
        the [Commissioner] determines that the person would not be a person in control
        of \na licensee, the proposed Person and transaction is not subject to the
        requirements of [Section \n6.01(a) and (b)] of this [Act]. \n(n) \nIf a multistate
        licensing process includes a determination pursuant to \n[Section 6.01(m)]
        and an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to the multistate licensing
        \nprocess: \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to accept
        the \ncontrol determination of a lead investigative state with sufficient
        staffing, expertise, and \nminimum standards for the purpose of [Section 6.01(m)];
        or\n"

      text: "15 \n \nchecks, credit checks, fee processing, and examinations.9 \n(d)
        \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS forms, \nprocesses,
        and functionalities in accordance with this [Act].10 In the event NMLS does
        not provide \nfunctionality, forms, or processes for a provision of this [Act],
        the [Commissioner] is authorized \nand encouraged to strive to implement the
        requirements in a manner that facilitates uniformity \nwith respect to licensing,
        supervision, reporting, and regulation of licensees which are licensed in
        \nmultiple jurisdictions. \n(e) \nWaive or Modify Requirements.— For the purpose
        of participating in the \nNationwide Multistate Licensing System & Registry,
        the Commissioner is authorized to waive or \nmodify, in whole or in part,
        by rule, regulation or order, any or all of the requirements and to \nestablish
        new requirements as reasonably necessary to participate in the Nationwide
        Multistate \nLicensing System & Registry. \n[Alternative to Section 5.02(e)]:
        The [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to establish \nand adopt,
        by rule or regulation, requirements for participation by applicants and licensees
        in \nNMLS upon the [Department's] determination that each requirement is consistent
        with law, public \ninterest, and the purposes of this [Section 5.02].] \nSection
        5.03 Application for License. \n(a) \nApplicants for a license shall apply
        in a form and in a medium as prescribed \nby the [Commissioner]. Each such
        form shall contain content as set forth by rule, regulation, \ninstruction
        or procedure of the [Commissioner] and may be changed or updated by the \n[Commissioner]
        in accordance with applicable law in order to carry out the purposes of this
        [Act] \nand maintain consistency with NMLS licensing standards and practices.
        The application must state \nor contain, as applicable: \n(1) \nthe legal
        name and residential and business addresses of the \napplicant and any fictitious
        or trade name used by the applicant in conducting its business; \n(2) \na
        list of any criminal convictions of the applicant and any material \nlitigation
        in which the applicant has been involved in the [10]-year period next preceding
        \nthe submission of the application; \n(3) \na description of any money transmission
        previously provided by the \napplicant and the money transmission that the
        applicant seeks to provide in this state; \n \n9 Commentary: The [Commissioner]
        acting through its representatives should review and ensure that NMLS \nfunctionalities,
        forms, and processes are consistent with this Act before adopting such NMLS
        functionalities, forms, \nand processes. \n10 Commentary: The [Commissioner]
        acting through its representatives should review and ensure that NMLS \nfunctionalities,
        forms, and processes are consistent with this Act before adopting such NMLS
        functionalities, forms, \nand processes.\n"

      text: "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. The renewal report
        must state or contain a \ndescription of each material change in information
        submitted by the licensee in its original license \napplication which has
        not been reported to the [Commissioner]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] for good
        cause may grant an extension of the renewal \ndate. \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner]
        is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS to \nprocess license renewals
        provided that such functionality is consistent with this [Section 5.06]. \nSection
        5.07 Maintenance of License. \n(a) \nIf a licensee does not continue to meet
        the qualifications or satisfy the \nrequirements that apply to an applicant
        for a new money transmission license, the [Commissioner] \nmay suspend or
        revoke the licensee's license in accordance with the procedures established
        by this \n[Act] or other applicable state law for such suspension or revocation.
        \n(b) \nAn applicant for a money transmission license must demonstrate that
        it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission licensee must at all times
        meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act].
        \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control and Change of Key Individual \nSection
        6.01 Acquisition of Control. \n(a) \nAny person, or group of persons acting
        in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall obtain the written
        approval of the [Commissioner] prior to acquiring control. \nAn individual
        is not deemed to acquire control of a licensee and is not subject to these
        acquisition \nof control provisions when that individual becomes a key individual
        in the ordinary course of \nbusiness. \n(b) \nA person, or group of persons
        acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall, in cooperation
        with the licensee: \n(1) \nSubmit an application in a form and in a medium
        prescribed by the \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable fee
        of [$X] with the request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner]
        may permit a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons acting in concert,
        to submit some or all information required by the \n[Commissioner] pursuant
        to [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe application required
        by [Section 6.01(b)(1)] shall include information \nrequired by [Section 5.04]
        for any new key individuals that have not previously completed the \nrequirements
        of [Section 5.04] for a licensee.\n"

      text: "30 \n \n(1) \nappoint the person signing the contract as the licensee's
        authorized \ndelegate with the authority to conduct money transmission on
        behalf of the licensee; \n(2) \nset forth the nature and scope of the relationship
        between the \nlicensee and the authorized delegate and the respective rights
        and responsibilities of the \nparties; \n(3) \nrequire the authorized delegate
        to agree to fully comply with all \napplicable state and federal laws, rules,
        and regulations pertaining to money transmission, \nincluding this [Act] and
        regulations implementing this [Act], relevant provisions of the \nBank Secrecy
        Act and the USA PATRIOT ACT; \n(4) \nrequire the authorized delegate to remit
        and handle money and \nmonetary value in accordance with the terms of the
        contract between the licensee and the \nauthorized delegate; \n(5) \nimpose
        a trust on money and monetary value net of fees received for \nmoney transmission
        for the benefit of the licensee; \n(6) \nrequire the authorized delegate to
        prepare and maintain records as \nrequired by this [Act] or regulations implementing
        this [Act], or as reasonably requested \nby the [Commissioner]; \n(7) \nacknowledge
        that the authorized delegate consents to examination \nor investigation by
        the [Commissioner]; \n(8) \nstate that the licensee is subject to regulation
        by the [Commissioner] \nand that, as part of that regulation, the [Commissioner]
        may suspend or revoke an \nauthorized delegate designation or require the
        licensee to terminate an authorized delegate \ndesignation; and \n(9) \n(9)
        \ acknowledge receipt of the written policies and procedures \nrequired under
        [Section 8.01(b)(1)]. \n(e) \nIf the licensee's license is suspended, revoked,
        surrendered, or expired, the \nlicensee must, within five (5) business days,
        provide documentation to the [Commissioner] that \nthe licensee has notified
        all applicable authorized delegates of the licensee whose names are in a \nrecord
        filed with the [Commissioner] of the suspension, revocation, surrender, or
        expiration of a \nlicense. Upon suspension, revocation, surrender, or expiration
        of a license, applicable authorized \ndelegates shall immediately cease to
        provide money transmission as an authorized delegate of the \nlicensee. \n(f)
        \nAn authorized delegate of a licensee holds in trust for the benefit of the
        \nlicensee all money net of fees received from money transmission.  If any
        authorized delegate \ncommingles any funds received from money transmission
        with any other funds or property owned \nor controlled by the authorized delegate,
        all commingled funds and other property shall be \nconsidered held in trust
        in favor of the licensee in an amount equal to the amount of money net of\n"

      text: "31 \n \nfees received from money transmission.22 \n(g) \nAn authorized
        delegate may not use a subdelegate to conduct money \ntransmission on behalf
        of a licensee. \nSection 8.02 Unauthorized Activities \nA person shall not
        engage in the business of money transmission on behalf of a person \nnot licensed
        under this [Act]  or not exempt pursuant to [Article III] of this [Act]. A
        person that \nengages in such activity provides money transmission to the
        same extent as if the person were a \nlicensee, and shall be jointly and severally
        liable with the unlicensed or nonexempt person. \nSection 8.03 [Optional]:
        Prohibited Authorized Delegates. \n(a) \nThe [appropriate court] in an action
        brought by a licensee shall have \njurisdiction to grant appropriate equitable
        or legal relief, including without limitation prohibiting \nthe authorized
        delegate from directly or indirectly acting as an authorized delegate for
        any licensee \nin this state and the payment of restitution, damages or other
        monetary relief, if the [appropriate \ncourt] finds that an authorized delegate
        failed to remit money in accordance with the written \ncontract required by
        [Section 8.01(b)] or as otherwise directed by the licensee or required by
        law. \n(b) \nIf the [appropriate court] issues an order prohibiting a person
        from acting as \nan authorized delegate for any licensee pursuant to [Section
        8.03(a)], the licensee that brought the \naction shall report the order to
        the [Commissioner] within thirty (30) days and shall report the \norder through
        NMLS within ninety (90) days. \n(c) \nAn authorized delegate who holds money
        in trust for the benefit of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails to remit more
        than [$XXX] of such money is guilty of a [reference \nto state classification]
        felony. \n(d) \nAn authorized delegate who holds money in trust for the benefit
        of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails to remit no more than [$XXX] of such money
        is guilty of a [reference \nto state classification] misdemeanor. \nARTICLE
        IX  \nTimely Transmission, Refunds, and Disclosures \nSection 9.01 Timely
        Transmission. \n(a) \nEvery licensee shall forward all money received for
        transmission in \naccordance with the terms of the agreement between the licensee
        and the sender unless the licensee \nhas a reasonable belief or a reasonable
        basis to believe that the sender may be a victim of fraud or \nthat a crime
        or violation of law, rule, or regulation has occurred, is occurring, or may
        occur. \n(b) \nIf a licensee fails to forward money received for transmission
        in accordance \nwith this section, the licensee must respond to inquiries
        by the sender with the reason for the failure \n \n22 Commentary: An express
        trust account or segregated bank account is not required.\n"

    support_state: supplied
    source_type: workspace
    available_excerpt: "# Research this issue for the dossier: Money transmission
      licensing: whether\n\n## Question\n\nResearch this issue for the dossier: Money
      transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate under the combined
      44-state footprint and whether Harbor's MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition.\nProposed
      date leads; resolve each reference in saved records before using it: [{\"role\":
      \"target acquisition close\", \"value\": \"Nov 15\", \"source_reference_id\":
      \"MSG-20260909-982278\", \"note\": \"The source describes this date as about
      ten weeks away. It does not expressly state the year or timezone.\"}, {\"role\":
      \"identity-verification vendor closure\", \"value\": \"2024\", \"source_reference_id\":

          ## Question


          Research this issue for the dossier: State money-transmission authority
          after the asset purchase. The migration plan assumes Harbor’s licenses will
          permit service in four new markets. An asset purchase might not transfer
          those licenses or their operating authority to Mosaic.

          Lawyer''s accepted priorities (private matter context):

          Confirm that Mosaic can lawfully serve each migrated account and market.:
          The asset-purchase structure and incomplete identity records undermine the
          planned day-one launch.

    b71b1504e47b8872a1a9689774342bdfad27c322db495001527f7f701e6acd9c:
      summary: Read saved source passage.
      data:
        status: read
        source_id: SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538

        unit_id: p000014
        body_hash: 5b5d2f6c388b9bcf98252d205bb001dbdce26951229e0e6896dfecf0358be545
        start: 0
        end: 1963
        page_number: 14
        section_label: null
        extraction_method: pdf_text
        text: "14 \n \nARTICLE V \nMoney Transmission Licenses \nSection 5.01 License
          Required. \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the business of money transmission
          or \nadvertise, solicit, or hold itself out as providing money transmission
          unless the person is licensed \nunder this [Act]; \n(b) \n[Section 5.01(a)]
          does not apply to: \n(1) \nA person that is an authorized delegate of a
          person licensed under \nthis [Act] acting within the scope of authority
          conferred by a written contract with the \nlicensee; or \n(2) \nA person
          that is exempt pursuant to [Section 3.01] and does not \nengage in money
          transmission outside the scope of such exemption. \n(c) \nA license issued
          under [Section 5.05] is not transferable or assignable. \nSection 5.02 Consistent
          State Licensing. \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing between [this
          state] and other states, the \n[Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged
          to: \n(1) \nimplement all licensing provisions of this [Act] in a manner
          that is \nconsistent with other states that have adopted this [Act]or multistate
          licensing processes; \nand \n(2) \nparticipate in nationwide protocols for
          licensing cooperation and \ncoordination among state regulators provided
          that such protocols are consistent with this \n[Act]. \n(b) \nIn order to
          fulfill the purposes of this [Act], the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and
          encouraged to establish relationships or contracts with NMLS or other entities
          \ndesignated by NMLS to enable the [Commissioner] to: \n(1) \ncollect and
          maintain records; \n(2) \ncoordinate multistate licensing processes and
          supervision processes; \n(3) \nprocess fees; and \n(4) \nfacilitate communication
          between [state] and licensees or other \npersons subject to this [Act].
          \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS
          for all \naspects of licensing in accordance with this [Act], including
          but not limited to, license applications, \napplications for acquisitions
          of control, surety bonds, reporting, criminal history background\n"
        has_more_in_unit: false
        paragraph_continues: false

    3b243c52451a4850c952d0204a27629c66b2e767f31e20122fa00f2c403ad985:
      summary: Read saved source passage.
      data:
        status: read
        source_id: SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538
        source_version: dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a
        unit_id: p000022
        body_hash: 175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748
        start: 0
        end: 2612
        page_number: 22
        section_label: null
        extraction_method: pdf_text
        text: "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control under
          this [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items and address all of
          the matters that are required, the application shall \nbe considered complete
          and the [Commissioner] shall promptly notify the applicant in a record of
          \nthe date on which the application was determined to be complete and:15
          \n \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] shall approve or deny the application within
          60 \ndays after the completion date; or \n(2) \nif the application is not
          approved or denied within 60 days after the \ncompletion date: \n(A) \nthe
          application is approved; and \n(B) \nthe person, or group of persons acting
          in concert, are not \nprohibited from acquiring control. \n(3) \nThe [Commissioner]
          may for good cause extend the application \nperiod. \n(f) \nA determination
          by the [Commissioner] that an application is complete and \nis accepted
          for processing means only that the application, on its face, appears to
          include all of the \nitems and address all of the matters that are required,
          and is not an assessment of the substance of \nthe application or of the
          sufficiency of the information provided. \n(g) \nWhen an application is
          filed and considered complete under [Section \n6.01(e)], the [Commissioner]
          shall investigate the financial condition and responsibility, financial
          \nand business experience, character, and general fitness of the person,
          or group of persons acting in \nconcert, seeking to acquire control. The
          [Commissioner] shall approve an acquisition of control \npursuant to this
          [Section 6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds that all of the following conditions
          have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe requirements of subsections (b) and (d)
          have been met, as \napplicable; and \n(2) \nthe financial condition and
          responsibility, financial and business \nexperience, competence, character,
          and general fitness of the person, or group of persons \nacting in concert,
          seeking to acquire control; and the competence, experience, character, \nand
          general fitness of the key individuals and persons that would be in control
          of the \nlicensee after the acquisition of control indicate that it is in
          the interest of the public to \npermit the person, or group of persons acting
          in concert, to control the licensee. \n(h) \nIf an applicant avails itself
          or is otherwise subject to a multistate licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS
          will accommodate and streamline the process of communicating when applications
          are \nreceived and when states consider them to have been complete. The
          intent of this Act is for the application period to \nbegin on the day an
          application is determined to be complete.\n"
        has_more_in_unit: false
        paragraph_continues: false

        page_number: 23
        section_label: null
        extraction_method: pdf_text
        text: "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged
          to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead investigative state for
          the purpose of [Section 6.01(g)] if the \nlead investigative state has sufficient
          staffing, expertise, and minimum standards; or \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead
          investigative state, the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to
          investigate the applicant pursuant to [Section 6.01(g)] and \nthe timeframes
          established by agreement through the multistate licensing process. \n(i)
          \nThe [Commissioner] shall issue a formal written notice of the denial of
          an \napplication to acquire control within thirty (30) days of the decision
          to deny the application. The \n[Commissioner] shall set forth in the notice
          of denial the specific reasons for the denial of the \napplication. An applicant
          whose application is denied by the [Commissioner] under this [Section \n6.01(i)]
          may appeal within thirty (30) days16 after receipt of the written notice
          of the denial \n[pursuant to state administrative law procedures]. \n(j)
          \nThe requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to any of the
          \nfollowing: \n(1) \nA person that acts as a proxy for the sole purpose
          of voting at a \ndesignated meeting of the shareholders or holders of voting
          shares or voting interests of a \nlicensee or a person in control of a licensee;
          \n(2) \nA person that acquires control of a licensee by devise or descent;
          \n(3) \nA person that acquires control of a licensee as a personal \nrepresentative,
          custodian, guardian, conservator, or trustee, or as an officer appointed
          by a \ncourt of competent jurisdiction or by operation of law; \n(4) \nA
          person that is exempt under [Section 3.01(g)]; \n(5) \nA person that the
          [Commissioner] determines is not subject to \n[Section 6.01(a)] based on
          the public interest; \n(6) \nA public offering of securities of a licensee
          or a person in control of \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn internal reorganization
          of a person in control of the licensee \nwhere the ultimate person in control
          of the licensee remains the same. \n(k) \nPersons in [Sections 6.01(j)(2),
          (3), (4), (6), (7)] in cooperation with the \nlicensee shall notify the
          [Commissioner] within [15] days after the acquisition of control.17 \n \n16
          Commentary: Administrative procedures for challenging a departmental decision
          may be derived from other \naspects of state law. In such a case, this Act
          should be adjusted to reflect the relevant administrative process. \n17
          Commentary: Notice is satisfied upon updating the licensee’s NMLS record.\n"

        text: "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1) \nThe requirements
          of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson that has complied
          with and received approval to engage in money transmission \nunder this
          [Act] or was identified as a person in control in a prior application filed
          with and \napproved by the [Commissioner] or by an MSB accredited state
          pursuant to a multistate \nlicensing process, provided that: \n(A) \nthe
          person has not had a license revoked or suspended or \ncontrolled a licensee
          that has had a license revoked or suspended while the person \nwas in control
          of the licensee in the previous 5-years; \n(B) \nif the person is a licensee,
          the person is well managed and \nhas received at least a satisfactory rating
          for compliance at its most recent \nexamination by an MSB accredited state
          if such rating was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee to be acquired is projected
          to meet the \nrequirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03] of this
          [Act] after the acquisition \nof control is completed, and if the person
          acquiring control is a licensee, that \nlicensee is also projected to meet
          the requirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and \n10.03] of this [Act] after
          the acquisition of control is completed; \n(D) \nthe licensee to be acquired
          will not implement any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result
          of the acquisition of control, and if the person \nacquiring control is
          a licensee, that licensee also will not implement any material \nchanges
          to its business plan as a result of the acquisition of control;  and \n(E)
          \nthe person provides notice of the acquisition in cooperation \nwith the
          licensee and attests to [Section 6.01(l)(1)(A), (B), (C), and (D)] in a
          form \nand in a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. \n(2) \nIf the
          notice is not disapproved within 30 days after the date on \nwhich the notice
          was determined to be complete, the notice is deemed approved. \n(m) \nBefore
          filing an application for approval to acquire control of a licensee a \nperson
          may request in writing a determination from the [Commissioner] as to whether
          the person \nwould be considered a person in control of a licensee upon
          consummation of a proposed \ntransaction. If the [Commissioner] determines
          that the person would not be a person in control of \na licensee, the proposed
          Person and transaction is not subject to the requirements of [Section \n6.01(a)
          and (b)] of this [Act]. \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing process includes
          a determination pursuant to \n[Section 6.01(m)] and an applicant avails
          itself or is otherwise subject to the multistate licensing \nprocess: \n(1)
          \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to accept the \ncontrol
          determination of a lead investigative state with sufficient staffing, expertise,
          and \nminimum standards for the purpose of [Section 6.01(m)]; or\n"

        text: "15 \n \nchecks, credit checks, fee processing, and examinations.9 \n(d)
          \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS forms,
          \nprocesses, and functionalities in accordance with this [Act].10 In the
          event NMLS does not provide \nfunctionality, forms, or processes for a provision
          of this [Act], the [Commissioner] is authorized \nand encouraged to strive
          to implement the requirements in a manner that facilitates uniformity \nwith
          respect to licensing, supervision, reporting, and regulation of licensees
          which are licensed in \nmultiple jurisdictions. \n(e) \nWaive or Modify
          Requirements.— For the purpose of participating in the \nNationwide Multistate
          Licensing System & Registry, the Commissioner is authorized to waive or
          \nmodify, in whole or in part, by rule, regulation or order, any or all
          of the requirements and to \nestablish new requirements as reasonably necessary
          to participate in the Nationwide Multistate \nLicensing System & Registry.
          \n[Alternative to Section 5.02(e)]: The [Commissioner] is authorized and
          encouraged to establish \nand adopt, by rule or regulation, requirements
          for participation by applicants and licensees in \nNMLS upon the [Department's]
          determination that each requirement is consistent with law, public \ninterest,
          and the purposes of this [Section 5.02].] \nSection 5.03 Application for
          License. \n(a) \nApplicants for a license shall apply in a form and in a
          medium as prescribed \nby the [Commissioner]. Each such form shall contain
          content as set forth by rule, regulation, \ninstruction or procedure of
          the [Commissioner] and may be changed or updated by the \n[Commissioner]
          in accordance with applicable law in order to carry out the purposes of
          this [Act] \nand maintain consistency with NMLS licensing standards and
          practices. The application must state \nor contain, as applicable: \n(1)
          \nthe legal name and residential and business addresses of the \napplicant
          and any fictitious or trade name used by the applicant in conducting its
          business; \n(2) \na list of any criminal convictions of the applicant and
          any material \nlitigation in which the applicant has been involved in the
          [10]-year period next preceding \nthe submission of the application; \n(3)
          \na description of any money transmission previously provided by the \napplicant
          and the money transmission that the applicant seeks to provide in this state;
          \n \n9 Commentary: The [Commissioner] acting through its representatives
          should review and ensure that NMLS \nfunctionalities, forms, and processes
          are consistent with this Act before adopting such NMLS functionalities,
          forms, \nand processes. \n10 Commentary: The [Commissioner] acting through
          its representatives should review and ensure that NMLS \nfunctionalities,
          forms, and processes are consistent with this Act before adopting such NMLS
          functionalities, forms, \nand processes.\n"

        text: "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. The renewal report
          must state or contain a \ndescription of each material change in information
          submitted by the licensee in its original license \napplication which has
          not been reported to the [Commissioner]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] for
          good cause may grant an extension of the renewal \ndate. \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner]
          is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS to \nprocess license renewals
          provided that such functionality is consistent with this [Section 5.06].
          \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of License. \n(a) \nIf a licensee does not continue
          to meet the qualifications or satisfy the \nrequirements that apply to an
          applicant for a new money transmission license, the [Commissioner] \nmay
          suspend or revoke the licensee's license in accordance with the procedures
          established by this \n[Act] or other applicable state law for such suspension
          or revocation. \n(b) \nAn applicant for a money transmission license must
          demonstrate that it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission licensee
          must at all times meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02, and
          10.03] of this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control and Change of
          Key Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition of Control. \n(a) \nAny person,
          or group of persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a
          licensee shall obtain the written approval of the [Commissioner] prior to
          acquiring control. \nAn individual is not deemed to acquire control of a
          licensee and is not subject to these acquisition \nof control provisions
          when that individual becomes a key individual in the ordinary course of
          \nbusiness. \n(b) \nA person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking
          to acquire control \nof a licensee shall, in cooperation with the licensee:
          \n(1) \nSubmit an application in a form and in a medium prescribed by the
          \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable fee of [$X] with the
          request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner] may permit
          a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons acting in concert, to submit
          some or all information required by the \n[Commissioner] pursuant to [Section
          6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe application required by [Section
          6.01(b)(1)] shall include information \nrequired by [Section 5.04] for any
          new key individuals that have not previously completed the \nrequirements
          of [Section 5.04] for a licensee.\n"

        text: "30 \n \n(1) \nappoint the person signing the contract as the licensee's
          authorized \ndelegate with the authority to conduct money transmission on
          behalf of the licensee; \n(2) \nset forth the nature and scope of the relationship
          between the \nlicensee and the authorized delegate and the respective rights
          and responsibilities of the \nparties; \n(3) \nrequire the authorized delegate
          to agree to fully comply with all \napplicable state and federal laws, rules,
          and regulations pertaining to money transmission, \nincluding this [Act]
          and regulations implementing this [Act], relevant provisions of the \nBank
          Secrecy Act and the USA PATRIOT ACT; \n(4) \nrequire the authorized delegate
          to remit and handle money and \nmonetary value in accordance with the terms
          of the contract between the licensee and the \nauthorized delegate; \n(5)
          \nimpose a trust on money and monetary value net of fees received for \nmoney
          transmission for the benefit of the licensee; \n(6) \nrequire the authorized
          delegate to prepare and maintain records as \nrequired by this [Act] or
          regulations implementing this [Act], or as reasonably requested \nby the
          [Commissioner]; \n(7) \nacknowledge that the authorized delegate consents
          to examination \nor investigation by the [Commissioner]; \n(8) \nstate that
          the licensee is subject to regulation by the [Commissioner] \nand that,
          as part of that regulation, the [Commissioner] may suspend or revoke an
          \nauthorized delegate designation or require the licensee to terminate an
          authorized delegate \ndesignation; and \n(9) \n(9)  acknowledge receipt
          of the written policies and procedures \nrequired under [Section 8.01(b)(1)].
          \n(e) \nIf the licensee's license is suspended, revoked, surrendered, or
          expired, the \nlicensee must, within five (5) business days, provide documentation
          to the [Commissioner] that \nthe licensee has notified all applicable authorized
          delegates of the licensee whose names are in a \nrecord filed with the [Commissioner]
          of the suspension, revocation, surrender, or expiration of a \nlicense.
          Upon suspension, revocation, surrender, or expiration of a license, applicable
          authorized \ndelegates shall immediately cease to provide money transmission
          as an authorized delegate of the \nlicensee. \n(f) \nAn authorized delegate
          of a licensee holds in trust for the benefit of the \nlicensee all money
          net of fees received from money transmission.  If any authorized delegate
          \ncommingles any funds received from money transmission with any other funds
          or property owned \nor controlled by the authorized delegate, all commingled
          funds and other property shall be \nconsidered held in trust in favor of
          the licensee in an amount equal to the amount of money net of\n"

        extraction_method: pdf_text
        text: "31 \n \nfees received from money transmission.22 \n(g) \nAn authorized
          delegate may not use a subdelegate to conduct money \ntransmission on behalf
          of a licensee. \nSection 8.02 Unauthorized Activities \nA person shall not
          engage in the business of money transmission on behalf of a person \nnot
          licensed under this [Act]  or not exempt pursuant to [Article III] of this
          [Act]. A person that \nengages in such activity provides money transmission
          to the same extent as if the person were a \nlicensee, and shall be jointly
          and severally liable with the unlicensed or nonexempt person. \nSection
          8.03 [Optional]: Prohibited Authorized Delegates. \n(a) \nThe [appropriate
          court] in an action brought by a licensee shall have \njurisdiction to grant
          appropriate equitable or legal relief, including without limitation prohibiting
          \nthe authorized delegate from directly or indirectly acting as an authorized
          delegate for any licensee \nin this state and the payment of restitution,
          damages or other monetary relief, if the [appropriate \ncourt] finds that
          an authorized delegate failed to remit money in accordance with the written
          \ncontract required by [Section 8.01(b)] or as otherwise directed by the
          licensee or required by law. \n(b) \nIf the [appropriate court] issues an
          order prohibiting a person from acting as \nan authorized delegate for any
          licensee pursuant to [Section 8.03(a)], the licensee that brought the \naction
          shall report the order to the [Commissioner] within thirty (30) days and
          shall report the \norder through NMLS within ninety (90) days. \n(c) \nAn
          authorized delegate who holds money in trust for the benefit of a \nlicensee
          and knowingly fails to remit more than [$XXX] of such money is guilty of
          a [reference \nto state classification] felony. \n(d) \nAn authorized delegate
          who holds money in trust for the benefit of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails
          to remit no more than [$XXX] of such money is guilty of a [reference \nto
          state classification] misdemeanor. \nARTICLE IX  \nTimely Transmission,
          Refunds, and Disclosures \nSection 9.01 Timely Transmission. \n(a) \nEvery
          licensee shall forward all money received for transmission in \naccordance
          with the terms of the agreement between the licensee and the sender unless
          the licensee \nhas a reasonable belief or a reasonable basis to believe
          that the sender may be a victim of fraud or \nthat a crime or violation
          of law, rule, or regulation has occurred, is occurring, or may occur. \n(b)
          \nIf a licensee fails to forward money received for transmission in accordance
          \nwith this section, the licensee must respond to inquiries by the sender
          with the reason for the failure \n \n22 Commentary: An express trust account
          or segregated bank account is not required.\n"
        has_more_in_unit: false
        paragraph_continues: false

    - unit_id: p000014
      start: 0
      end: 1963
      page_number: 14
      section_label: null
      body_hash: 5b5d2f6c388b9bcf98252d205bb001dbdce26951229e0e6896dfecf0358be545
      path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000014.md
      text: "14 \n \nARTICLE V \nMoney Transmission Licenses \nSection 5.01 License
        Required. \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the business of money transmission
        or \nadvertise, solicit, or hold itself out as providing money transmission
        unless the person is licensed \nunder this [Act]; \n(b) \n[Section 5.01(a)]
        does not apply to: \n(1) \nA person that is an authorized delegate of a person
        licensed under \nthis [Act] acting within the scope of authority conferred
        by a written contract with the \nlicensee; or \n(2) \nA person that is exempt
        pursuant to [Section 3.01] and does not \nengage in money transmission outside
        the scope of such exemption. \n(c) \nA license issued under [Section 5.05]
        is not transferable or assignable. \nSection 5.02 Consistent State Licensing.
        \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing between [this state] and other states,
        the \n[Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to: \n(1) \nimplement all
        licensing provisions of this [Act] in a manner that is \nconsistent with other
        states that have adopted this [Act]or multistate licensing processes; \nand
        \n(2) \nparticipate in nationwide protocols for licensing cooperation and
        \ncoordination among state regulators provided that such protocols are consistent
        with this \n[Act]. \n(b) \nIn order to fulfill the purposes of this [Act],
        the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to establish relationships
        or contracts with NMLS or other entities \ndesignated by NMLS to enable the
        [Commissioner] to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain records; \n(2) \ncoordinate
        multistate licensing processes and supervision processes; \n(3) \nprocess
        fees; and \n(4) \nfacilitate communication between [state] and licensees or
        other \npersons subject to this [Act]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized
        and encouraged to utilize NMLS for all \naspects of licensing in accordance
        with this [Act], including but not limited to, license applications, \napplications
        for acquisitions of control, surety bonds, reporting, criminal history background\n"
    - unit_id: p000022
      start: 0
      end: 2612
      page_number: 22
      section_label: null
      body_hash: 175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748
      path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000022.md
      text: "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control under this
        [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items and address all of the matters
        that are required, the application shall \nbe considered complete and the
        [Commissioner] shall promptly notify the applicant in a record of \nthe date
        on which the application was determined to be complete and:15 \n \n(1) \nThe
        [Commissioner] shall approve or deny the application within 60 \ndays after
        the completion date; or \n(2) \nif the application is not approved or denied
        within 60 days after the \ncompletion date: \n(A) \nthe application is approved;
        and \n(B) \nthe person, or group of persons acting in concert, are not \nprohibited
        from acquiring control. \n(3) \nThe [Commissioner] may for good cause extend
        the application \nperiod. \n(f) \nA determination by the [Commissioner] that
        an application is complete and \nis accepted for processing means only that
        the application, on its face, appears to include all of the \nitems and address
        all of the matters that are required, and is not an assessment of the substance
        of \nthe application or of the sufficiency of the information provided. \n(g)
        \nWhen an application is filed and considered complete under [Section \n6.01(e)],
        the [Commissioner] shall investigate the financial condition and responsibility,
        financial \nand business experience, character, and general fitness of the
        person, or group of persons acting in \nconcert, seeking to acquire control.
        The [Commissioner] shall approve an acquisition of control \npursuant to this
        [Section 6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds that all of the following conditions
        have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe requirements of subsections (b) and (d)
        have been met, as \napplicable; and \n(2) \nthe financial condition and responsibility,
        financial and business \nexperience, competence, character, and general fitness
        of the person, or group of persons \nacting in concert, seeking to acquire
        control; and the competence, experience, character, \nand general fitness
        of the key individuals and persons that would be in control of the \nlicensee
        after the acquisition of control indicate that it is in the interest of the
        public to \npermit the person, or group of persons acting in concert, to control
        the licensee. \n(h) \nIf an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject
        to a multistate licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and streamline
        the process of communicating when applications are \nreceived and when states
        consider them to have been complete. The intent of this Act is for the application
        period to \nbegin on the day an application is determined to be complete.\n"
    - unit_id: p000023
      start: 0
      end: 2523
      page_number: 23
      section_label: null
      body_hash: 83a664c778fbc9de0b4d13270e2a918f6488b461db1a6617e3d36032163068ca
      path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000023.md
      text: "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged
        to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead investigative state for the
        purpose of [Section 6.01(g)] if the \nlead investigative state has sufficient
        staffing, expertise, and minimum standards; or \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead
        investigative state, the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to
        investigate the applicant pursuant to [Section 6.01(g)] and \nthe timeframes
        established by agreement through the multistate licensing process. \n(i) \nThe
        [Commissioner] shall issue a formal written notice of the denial of an \napplication
        to acquire control within thirty (30) days of the decision to deny the application.
        The \n[Commissioner] shall set forth in the notice of denial the specific
        reasons for the denial of the \napplication. An applicant whose application
        is denied by the [Commissioner] under this [Section \n6.01(i)] may appeal
        within thirty (30) days16 after receipt of the written notice of the denial
        \n[pursuant to state administrative law procedures]. \n(j) \nThe requirements
        of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to any of the \nfollowing: \n(1)
        \nA person that acts as a proxy for the sole purpose of voting at a \ndesignated
        meeting of the shareholders or holders of voting shares or voting interests
        of a \nlicensee or a person in control of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person that
        acquires control of a licensee by devise or descent; \n(3) \nA person that
        acquires control of a licensee as a personal \nrepresentative, custodian,
        guardian, conservator, or trustee, or as an officer appointed by a \ncourt
        of competent jurisdiction or by operation of law; \n(4) \nA person that is
        exempt under [Section 3.01(g)]; \n(5) \nA person that the [Commissioner] determines
        is not subject to \n[Section 6.01(a)] based on the public interest; \n(6)
        \nA public offering of securities of a licensee or a person in control of
        \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn internal reorganization of a person in control
        of the licensee \nwhere the ultimate person in control of the licensee remains
        the same. \n(k) \nPersons in [Sections 6.01(j)(2), (3), (4), (6), (7)] in
        cooperation with the \nlicensee shall notify the [Commissioner] within [15]
        days after the acquisition of control.17 \n \n16 Commentary: Administrative
        procedures for challenging a departmental decision may be derived from other
        \naspects of state law. In such a case, this Act should be adjusted to reflect
        the relevant administrative process. \n17 Commentary: Notice is satisfied
        upon updating the licensee’s NMLS record.\n"
    - unit_id: p000024
      start: 0
      end: 2799
      page_number: 24
      section_label: null
      body_hash: 4732d9c2b053975a4d3cb27db8e99faa4baf45f71eb350fa519e31b5890ac680
      path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000024.md
      text: "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1) \nThe requirements
        of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson that has complied
        with and received approval to engage in money transmission \nunder this [Act]
        or was identified as a person in control in a prior application filed with
        and \napproved by the [Commissioner] or by an MSB accredited state pursuant
        to a multistate \nlicensing process, provided that: \n(A) \nthe person has
        not had a license revoked or suspended or \ncontrolled a licensee that has
        had a license revoked or suspended while the person \nwas in control of the
        licensee in the previous 5-years; \n(B) \nif the person is a licensee, the
        person is well managed and \nhas received at least a satisfactory rating for
        compliance at its most recent \nexamination by an MSB accredited state if
        such rating was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee to be acquired is projected to
        meet the \nrequirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act]
        after the acquisition \nof control is completed, and if the person acquiring
        control is a licensee, that \nlicensee is also projected to meet the requirements
        of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and \n10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition
        of control is completed; \n(D) \nthe licensee to be acquired will not implement
        any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result of the acquisition
        of control, and if the person \nacquiring control is a licensee, that licensee
        also will not implement any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result
        of the acquisition of control;  and \n(E) \nthe person provides notice of
        the acquisition in cooperation \nwith the licensee and attests to [Section
        6.01(l)(1)(A), (B), (C), and (D)] in a form \nand in a medium prescribed by
        the [Commissioner]. \n(2) \nIf the notice is not disapproved within 30 days
        after the date on \nwhich the notice was determined to be complete, the notice
        is deemed approved. \n(m) \nBefore filing an application for approval to acquire
        control of a licensee a \nperson may request in writing a determination from
        the [Commissioner] as to whether the person \nwould be considered a person
        in control of a licensee upon consummation of a proposed \ntransaction. If
        the [Commissioner] determines that the person would not be a person in control
        of \na licensee, the proposed Person and transaction is not subject to the
        requirements of [Section \n6.01(a) and (b)] of this [Act]. \n(n) \nIf a multistate
        licensing process includes a determination pursuant to \n[Section 6.01(m)]
        and an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to the multistate licensing
        \nprocess: \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to accept
        the \ncontrol determination of a lead investigative state with sufficient
        staffing, expertise, and \nminimum standards for the purpose of [Section 6.01(m)];
        or\n"
    - unit_id: p000015
      start: 0
      end: 2835
      page_number: 15
      section_label: null
      body_hash: bba81d751ac954c1c9099842578104bf494b4912b32ce1f2e32cc8fac953e9e7
      path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000015.md
      text: "15 \n \nchecks, credit checks, fee processing, and examinations.9 \n(d)
        \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS forms, \nprocesses,
        and functionalities in accordance with this [Act].10 In the event NMLS does
        not provide \nfunctionality, forms, or processes for a provision of this [Act],
        the [Commissioner] is authorized \nand encouraged to strive to implement the
        requirements in a manner that facilitates uniformity \nwith respect to licensing,
        supervision, reporting, and regulation of licensees which are licensed in
        \nmultiple jurisdictions. \n(e) \nWaive or Modify Requirements.— For the purpose
        of participating in the \nNationwide Multistate Licensing System & Registry,
        the Commissioner is authorized to waive or \nmodify, in whole or in part,
        by rule, regulation or order, any or all of the requirements and to \nestablish
        new requirements as reasonably necessary to participate in the Nationwide
        Multistate \nLicensing System & Registry. \n[Alternative to Section 5.02(e)]:
        The [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to establish \nand adopt,
        by rule or regulation, requirements for participation by applicants and licensees
        in \nNMLS upon the [Department's] determination that each requirement is consistent
        with law, public \ninterest, and the purposes of this [Section 5.02].] \nSection
        5.03 Application for License. \n(a) \nApplicants for a license shall apply
        in a form and in a medium as prescribed \nby the [Commissioner]. Each such
        form shall contain content as set forth by rule, regulation, \ninstruction
        or procedure of the [Commissioner] and may be changed or updated by the \n[Commissioner]
        in accordance with applicable law in order to carry out the purposes of this
        [Act] \nand maintain consistency with NMLS licensing standards and practices.
        The application must state \nor contain, as applicable: \n(1) \nthe legal
        name and residential and business addresses of the \napplicant and any fictitious
        or trade name used by the applicant in conducting its business; \n(2) \na
        list of any criminal convictions of the applicant and any material \nlitigation
        in which the applicant has been involved in the [10]-year period next preceding
        \nthe submission of the application; \n(3) \na description of any money transmission
        previously provided by the \napplicant and the money transmission that the
        applicant seeks to provide in this state; \n \n9 Commentary: The [Commissioner]
        acting through its representatives should review and ensure that NMLS \nfunctionalities,
        forms, and processes are consistent with this Act before adopting such NMLS
        functionalities, forms, \nand processes. \n10 Commentary: The [Commissioner]
        acting through its representatives should review and ensure that NMLS \nfunctionalities,
        forms, and processes are consistent with this Act before adopting such NMLS
        functionalities, forms, \nand processes.\n"
