      body_hash: 5638ae03ab2c6c110a80e30639b8ccd42a1c585fdc2818a38e4f2f0fc69a5e06
      path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000021.md
      text: "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. The renewal report
        must state or contain a \ndescription of each material change in information
        submitted by the licensee in its original license \napplication which has
        not been reported to the [Commissioner]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] for good
        cause may grant an extension of the renewal \ndate. \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner]
        is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS to \nprocess license renewals
        provided that such functionality is consistent with this [Section 5.06]. \nSection
        5.07 Maintenance of License. \n(a) \nIf a licensee does not continue to meet
        the qualifications or satisfy the \nrequirements that apply to an applicant
        for a new money transmission license, the [Commissioner] \nmay suspend or
        revoke the licensee's license in accordance with the procedures established
        by this \n[Act] or other applicable state law for such suspension or revocation.
        \n(b) \nAn applicant for a money transmission license must demonstrate that
        it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission licensee must at all times
        meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act].
        \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control and Change of Key Individual \nSection
        6.01 Acquisition of Control. \n(a) \nAny person, or group of persons acting
        in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall obtain the written
        approval of the [Commissioner] prior to acquiring control. \nAn individual
        is not deemed to acquire control of a licensee and is not subject to these
        acquisition \nof control provisions when that individual becomes a key individual
        in the ordinary course of \nbusiness. \n(b) \nA person, or group of persons
        acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall, in cooperation
        with the licensee: \n(1) \nSubmit an application in a form and in a medium
        prescribed by the \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable fee
        of [$X] with the request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner]
        may permit a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons acting in concert,
        to submit some or all information required by the \n[Commissioner] pursuant
        to [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe application required
        by [Section 6.01(b)(1)] shall include information \nrequired by [Section 5.04]
        for any new key individuals that have not previously completed the \nrequirements
        of [Section 5.04] for a licensee.\n"
    - unit_id: p000030
      start: 0
      end: 2670
      page_number: 30
      section_label: null
      body_hash: 0d032292dd6b007bb0772b41f7c3f21512a56d4557c8c7b69696774b6248c842
      path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000030.md
      text: "30 \n \n(1) \nappoint the person signing the contract as the licensee's
        authorized \ndelegate with the authority to conduct money transmission on
        behalf of the licensee; \n(2) \nset forth the nature and scope of the relationship
        between the \nlicensee and the authorized delegate and the respective rights
        and responsibilities of the \nparties; \n(3) \nrequire the authorized delegate
        to agree to fully comply with all \napplicable state and federal laws, rules,
        and regulations pertaining to money transmission, \nincluding this [Act] and
        regulations implementing this [Act], relevant provisions of the \nBank Secrecy
        Act and the USA PATRIOT ACT; \n(4) \nrequire the authorized delegate to remit
        and handle money and \nmonetary value in accordance with the terms of the
        contract between the licensee and the \nauthorized delegate; \n(5) \nimpose
        a trust on money and monetary value net of fees received for \nmoney transmission
        for the benefit of the licensee; \n(6) \nrequire the authorized delegate to
        prepare and maintain records as \nrequired by this [Act] or regulations implementing
        this [Act], or as reasonably requested \nby the [Commissioner]; \n(7) \nacknowledge
        that the authorized delegate consents to examination \nor investigation by
        the [Commissioner]; \n(8) \nstate that the licensee is subject to regulation
        by the [Commissioner] \nand that, as part of that regulation, the [Commissioner]
        may suspend or revoke an \nauthorized delegate designation or require the
        licensee to terminate an authorized delegate \ndesignation; and \n(9) \n(9)
        \ acknowledge receipt of the written policies and procedures \nrequired under
        [Section 8.01(b)(1)]. \n(e) \nIf the licensee's license is suspended, revoked,
        surrendered, or expired, the \nlicensee must, within five (5) business days,
        provide documentation to the [Commissioner] that \nthe licensee has notified
        all applicable authorized delegates of the licensee whose names are in a \nrecord
        filed with the [Commissioner] of the suspension, revocation, surrender, or
        expiration of a \nlicense. Upon suspension, revocation, surrender, or expiration
        of a license, applicable authorized \ndelegates shall immediately cease to
        provide money transmission as an authorized delegate of the \nlicensee. \n(f)
        \nAn authorized delegate of a licensee holds in trust for the benefit of the
        \nlicensee all money net of fees received from money transmission.  If any
        authorized delegate \ncommingles any funds received from money transmission
        with any other funds or property owned \nor controlled by the authorized delegate,
        all commingled funds and other property shall be \nconsidered held in trust
        in favor of the licensee in an amount equal to the amount of money net of\n"
    - unit_id: p000031
      start: 0
      end: 2704
      page_number: 31
      section_label: null
      body_hash: 994d5382d8c2640923eca8c8aabbca98c8fbaeec037edafbf7675c1a3819b1e7
      path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000031.md
      text: "31 \n \nfees received from money transmission.22 \n(g) \nAn authorized
        delegate may not use a subdelegate to conduct money \ntransmission on behalf
        of a licensee. \nSection 8.02 Unauthorized Activities \nA person shall not
        engage in the business of money transmission on behalf of a person \nnot licensed
        under this [Act]  or not exempt pursuant to [Article III] of this [Act]. A
        person that \nengages in such activity provides money transmission to the
        same extent as if the person were a \nlicensee, and shall be jointly and severally
        liable with the unlicensed or nonexempt person. \nSection 8.03 [Optional]:
        Prohibited Authorized Delegates. \n(a) \nThe [appropriate court] in an action
        brought by a licensee shall have \njurisdiction to grant appropriate equitable
        or legal relief, including without limitation prohibiting \nthe authorized
        delegate from directly or indirectly acting as an authorized delegate for
        any licensee \nin this state and the payment of restitution, damages or other
        monetary relief, if the [appropriate \ncourt] finds that an authorized delegate
        failed to remit money in accordance with the written \ncontract required by
        [Section 8.01(b)] or as otherwise directed by the licensee or required by
        law. \n(b) \nIf the [appropriate court] issues an order prohibiting a person
        from acting as \nan authorized delegate for any licensee pursuant to [Section
        8.03(a)], the licensee that brought the \naction shall report the order to
        the [Commissioner] within thirty (30) days and shall report the \norder through
        NMLS within ninety (90) days. \n(c) \nAn authorized delegate who holds money
        in trust for the benefit of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails to remit more
        than [$XXX] of such money is guilty of a [reference \nto state classification]
        felony. \n(d) \nAn authorized delegate who holds money in trust for the benefit
        of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails to remit no more than [$XXX] of such money
        is guilty of a [reference \nto state classification] misdemeanor. \nARTICLE
        IX  \nTimely Transmission, Refunds, and Disclosures \nSection 9.01 Timely
        Transmission. \n(a) \nEvery licensee shall forward all money received for
        transmission in \naccordance with the terms of the agreement between the licensee
        and the sender unless the licensee \nhas a reasonable belief or a reasonable
        basis to believe that the sender may be a victim of fraud or \nthat a crime
        or violation of law, rule, or regulation has occurred, is occurring, or may
        occur. \n(b) \nIf a licensee fails to forward money received for transmission
        in accordance \nwith this section, the licensee must respond to inquiries
        by the sender with the reason for the failure \n \n22 Commentary: An express
        trust account or segregated bank account is not required.\n"

    matter_id: MAT-20260909-d89ad8
    captured_at: '2026-09-13T03:59:01.176554+00:00'
    inputs:
      business_question:
        question_id: BQ-c9d7c39f6380eb60
        text: Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal review
          before the Nov 15 close?
        revision: legacy:6abf4a45ae87313af8db04b89d546e0e1a1c6137341b3d3c0d159c66cf64d54c
      facts:
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-182bcc
        text: Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
          out).
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-551367
        text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
          Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and
          full access to Mosaic's product set.
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9a0c61
        text: Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC'd by Harbor.
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-33293c
        text: Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
          Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-aea8ec
        text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has
          pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users
          onboarded before 2023.
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-073838
        text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
          terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor's transaction feed at Mosaic's
          engine on day 1.
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-19aebc
        text: Marketing wants a 'Welcome' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
          launching close+1.
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-adf2cb
        text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from the last
          year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.
        source_ids:
        - REQ-20260909-283892
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-4c1fd8
        text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic
          Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-9835ba
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f2c49f
        text: Plan is no re-verification of Harbor's existing KYC; Harbor users were
          already KYC'd.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-9835ba
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-13d4c1
        text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
          results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users
          onboarded before 2023.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-9835ba
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-78d5cd
        text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
          terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay's
          engine on day 1.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-9835ba
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9f7bde
        text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from the last
          year at Harbor; none have been read yet.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-9835ba
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-ed9f06
        text: How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
          buys Harbor's assets)
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-2e549e
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-b5e71e
        text: Does Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
          institution's prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification required?
          — Not sure / need to check with compliance
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-2e549e
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-849b00
        text: What is known about Harbor's ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last
          year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-2e549e
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f0fb01
        text: For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
          Relay plan to operate under Harbor's existing licenses or apply for its
          own? — Use/assume Harbor's licenses
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-2e549e
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-620c62
        text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
          is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
          and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's
          AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must
          confirm.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-2e549e
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-070aec
        text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
          been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
          have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-2e549e
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      - fact_id: FACT-20260909-771ee1
        text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
          is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before onboarding
          those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's
          licenses for the four new markets.
        source_ids:
        - MSG-20260909-2e549e
        origin: null
        verification_status: null
      assumptions:
      - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-29b823
        text: Mosaic Relay's existing money transmission licenses and Harbor's MTLs
          are transferable or can be maintained through the acquisition without new
          state approval
        reason: Needed to continue
      - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-3c5756
        text: The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own
          BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents
        reason: Needed to continue
      - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-1a519f
        text: The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and validated before
          close without a monitoring gap
        reason: Needed to continue
      - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-ca7dfd
        text: Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state MTL regimes
          and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).
        reason: Needed to continue
      - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-d40239
        text: Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per
          the request).
        reason: Needed to continue
      - assumption_id: ASM-20260909-57e86b
        text: The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase, which affects
          whether Harbor's licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure
          not yet confirmed).
        reason: Needed to continue
      issues:
      - issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045
        title: 'Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate under
          the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive
          the acquisition'
        why_it_matters: ''
        parent_issue_id: null
        fact_ids: []
        disposition: null
      - issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045
        title: 'BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing
          underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent
          CIP/AML obligations'
        why_it_matters: ''
        parent_issue_id: null
        fact_ids: []
        disposition: null
      - issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38
        title: 'SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor''s
          ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability'
        why_it_matters: ''
        parent_issue_id: null
        fact_ids: []
        disposition: null
      - issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-4825f0af7ec75542
        title: 'Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
          when the SaaS contract terminates at close'
        why_it_matters: ''
        parent_issue_id: null
        fact_ids: []
        disposition: null
      - issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-72810d0a43d3ce66
        title: 'Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state money
          transmission or consumer protection implications'
        why_it_matters: ''
        parent_issue_id: null
        fact_ids: []
        disposition: null
      - issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
        title: Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights
        why_it_matters: An asset purchase does not by itself establish that customer
          accounts, contracts, balances, or personal data can move into Mosaic's app
          on day one.
        parent_issue_id: null
        fact_ids:
        - FACT-20260909-ed9f06
        - FACT-20260909-551367
        - FACT-20260909-4c1fd8
        disposition: null
      - issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-d22ea3957f21252a
        title: Open alerts, suspicious activity history, and acquisition diligence
        why_it_matters: About 40 open alerts and several suspicious activity reports
          remain unreviewed. Their contents could affect the acquisition decision,
          deal protections, remediation, and account migration.
        parent_issue_id: null
        fact_ids: []
        disposition: null
      - issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-65ae94508dcda1bf
        title: State money-transmission authority after the asset purchase
        why_it_matters: The migration plan assumes Harbor’s licenses will permit service
          in four new markets. An asset purchase might not transfer those licenses
          or their operating authority to Mosaic.
        parent_issue_id: null
        fact_ids: []
        disposition: null
      - issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-30caa16a9234ccf2
        title: Reliance on Harbor’s prior identity verification
        why_it_matters: The plan would migrate 240,000 consumers and 12,000 business
          accounts without new verification. Harbor’s former vendor closed in 2024,
          and only pass or fail results are reported as available.
        parent_issue_id: null
        fact_ids: []
        disposition: null
      - issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-1d13a6636b8fbe60
        title: Transaction-monitoring continuity at cutover
        why_it_matters: Harbor’s monitoring feed will move to Mosaic’s system when
          Harbor’s current service ends at close. An incomplete change could create
          a gap in required monitoring.
        parent_issue_id: null
        fact_ids: []
        disposition: null
      - issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-29efc151650e76a2
        title: Purchase-agreement authority and risk allocation
        why_it_matters: Pre-close data transfers, testing, customer communications,
          or operating changes could conflict with transaction covenants, consent
          limits, closing conditions, or liability allocations.
        parent_issue_id: null
        fact_ids: []
        disposition: null
      - issue_id: ISS-c9d7c39f63-fcd3954739e05481
        title: Customer terms, privacy, data transfers, and welcome bonus
        why_it_matters: Migration could change the service provider, account access,
          available products, data recipients, and customer rights. The proposed $50
          bonus adds advertising and offer-term risk.
        parent_issue_id: null
        fact_ids: []
        disposition: null
      questions:
      - question_id: Q-SAR
        text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
          been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
        consequence: Unread open alerts and SARs are the highest-risk item; they can
          create BSA/AML exposure that must be addressed before close and could affect
          the deal itself.
        state: answered
        answer: The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain
          in diligence.
        answer_kind: reported_fact
        linked_fact_ids:
        - FACT-20260909-070aec
      - question_id: Q-KYC
        text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
          is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
          and recordkeeping obligations?
        consequence: Whether the missing underlying documents create a compliance
          gap depends on how Mosaic plans to satisfy its own CIP/recordkeeping obligations
          for these users.
        state: answered
        answer: It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program permits
          reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must confirm.
        answer_kind: reported_fact
        linked_fact_ids:
        - FACT-20260909-620c62
      - question_id: Q-MTL
        text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what
          is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before onboarding
          those customers?
        consequence: Whether the four new markets can be served at close depends on
          license transferability and state approval, which is a gating regulatory
          question.
        state: answered
        answer: Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's licenses for
          the four new markets.
        answer_kind: reported_fact
        linked_fact_ids:
        - FACT-20260909-771ee1
      - question_id: Q-BONUS
        text: How is the $50 welcome bonus structured?
        consequence: The structure determines whether the bonus triggers consumer
          disclosure, funds-flow, or state promotional requirements.
        state: left_open
        answer: null
        answer_kind: null
        linked_fact_ids: []
      decisions: []
      files: {}

        - unit_id: p000014
          start: 0
          end: 1963
          page_number: 14
          section_label: null
          body_hash: 5b5d2f6c388b9bcf98252d205bb001dbdce26951229e0e6896dfecf0358be545
          path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000014.md
          text: "14 \n \nARTICLE V \nMoney Transmission Licenses \nSection 5.01 License
            Required. \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the business of money transmission
            or \nadvertise, solicit, or hold itself out as providing money transmission
            unless the person is licensed \nunder this [Act]; \n(b) \n[Section 5.01(a)]
            does not apply to: \n(1) \nA person that is an authorized delegate of
            a person licensed under \nthis [Act] acting within the scope of authority
            conferred by a written contract with the \nlicensee; or \n(2) \nA person
            that is exempt pursuant to [Section 3.01] and does not \nengage in money
            transmission outside the scope of such exemption. \n(c) \nA license issued
            under [Section 5.05] is not transferable or assignable. \nSection 5.02
            Consistent State Licensing. \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing
            between [this state] and other states, the \n[Commissioner] is authorized
            and encouraged to: \n(1) \nimplement all licensing provisions of this
            [Act] in a manner that is \nconsistent with other states that have adopted
            this [Act]or multistate licensing processes; \nand \n(2) \nparticipate
            in nationwide protocols for licensing cooperation and \ncoordination among
            state regulators provided that such protocols are consistent with this
            \n[Act]. \n(b) \nIn order to fulfill the purposes of this [Act], the [Commissioner]
            is \nauthorized and encouraged to establish relationships or contracts
            with NMLS or other entities \ndesignated by NMLS to enable the [Commissioner]
            to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain records; \n(2) \ncoordinate multistate
            licensing processes and supervision processes; \n(3) \nprocess fees; and
            \n(4) \nfacilitate communication between [state] and licensees or other
            \npersons subject to this [Act]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized
            and encouraged to utilize NMLS for all \naspects of licensing in accordance
            with this [Act], including but not limited to, license applications, \napplications
            for acquisitions of control, surety bonds, reporting, criminal history
            background\n"
        - unit_id: p000022
          start: 0
          end: 2612
          page_number: 22
          section_label: null
          body_hash: 175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748
          path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000022.md
          text: "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control under
            this [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items and address all
            of the matters that are required, the application shall \nbe considered
            complete and the [Commissioner] shall promptly notify the applicant in
            a record of \nthe date on which the application was determined to be complete
            and:15 \n \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] shall approve or deny the application
            within 60 \ndays after the completion date; or \n(2) \nif the application
            is not approved or denied within 60 days after the \ncompletion date:
            \n(A) \nthe application is approved; and \n(B) \nthe person, or group
            of persons acting in concert, are not \nprohibited from acquiring control.
            \n(3) \nThe [Commissioner] may for good cause extend the application \nperiod.
            \n(f) \nA determination by the [Commissioner] that an application is complete
            and \nis accepted for processing means only that the application, on its
            face, appears to include all of the \nitems and address all of the matters
            that are required, and is not an assessment of the substance of \nthe
            application or of the sufficiency of the information provided. \n(g) \nWhen
            an application is filed and considered complete under [Section \n6.01(e)],
            the [Commissioner] shall investigate the financial condition and responsibility,
            financial \nand business experience, character, and general fitness of
            the person, or group of persons acting in \nconcert, seeking to acquire
            control. The [Commissioner] shall approve an acquisition of control \npursuant
            to this [Section 6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds that all of the following
            conditions have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe requirements of subsections
            (b) and (d) have been met, as \napplicable; and \n(2) \nthe financial
            condition and responsibility, financial and business \nexperience, competence,
            character, and general fitness of the person, or group of persons \nacting
            in concert, seeking to acquire control; and the competence, experience,
            character, \nand general fitness of the key individuals and persons that
            would be in control of the \nlicensee after the acquisition of control
            indicate that it is in the interest of the public to \npermit the person,
            or group of persons acting in concert, to control the licensee. \n(h)
            \nIf an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to a multistate
            licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and streamline the
            process of communicating when applications are \nreceived and when states
            consider them to have been complete. The intent of this Act is for the
            application period to \nbegin on the day an application is determined
            to be complete.\n"
        - unit_id: p000023
          start: 0
          end: 2523
          page_number: 23
          section_label: null
          body_hash: 83a664c778fbc9de0b4d13270e2a918f6488b461db1a6617e3d36032163068ca
          path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000023.md
          text: "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged
            to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead investigative state for
            the purpose of [Section 6.01(g)] if the \nlead investigative state has
            sufficient staffing, expertise, and minimum standards; or \n(2) \nif [state]
            is a lead investigative state, the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and
            encouraged to investigate the applicant pursuant to [Section 6.01(g)]
            and \nthe timeframes established by agreement through the multistate licensing
            process. \n(i) \nThe [Commissioner] shall issue a formal written notice
            of the denial of an \napplication to acquire control within thirty (30)
            days of the decision to deny the application. The \n[Commissioner] shall
            set forth in the notice of denial the specific reasons for the denial
            of the \napplication. An applicant whose application is denied by the
            [Commissioner] under this [Section \n6.01(i)] may appeal within thirty
            (30) days16 after receipt of the written notice of the denial \n[pursuant
            to state administrative law procedures]. \n(j) \nThe requirements of [Section
            6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to any of the \nfollowing: \n(1) \nA person
            that acts as a proxy for the sole purpose of voting at a \ndesignated
            meeting of the shareholders or holders of voting shares or voting interests
            of a \nlicensee or a person in control of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person
            that acquires control of a licensee by devise or descent; \n(3) \nA person
            that acquires control of a licensee as a personal \nrepresentative, custodian,
            guardian, conservator, or trustee, or as an officer appointed by a \ncourt
            of competent jurisdiction or by operation of law; \n(4) \nA person that
            is exempt under [Section 3.01(g)]; \n(5) \nA person that the [Commissioner]
            determines is not subject to \n[Section 6.01(a)] based on the public interest;
            \n(6) \nA public offering of securities of a licensee or a person in control
            of \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn internal reorganization of a person in
            control of the licensee \nwhere the ultimate person in control of the
            licensee remains the same. \n(k) \nPersons in [Sections 6.01(j)(2), (3),
            (4), (6), (7)] in cooperation with the \nlicensee shall notify the [Commissioner]
            within [15] days after the acquisition of control.17 \n \n16 Commentary:
            Administrative procedures for challenging a departmental decision may
            be derived from other \naspects of state law. In such a case, this Act
            should be adjusted to reflect the relevant administrative process. \n17
            Commentary: Notice is satisfied upon updating the licensee’s NMLS record.\n"
        - unit_id: p000024
          start: 0
          end: 2799
          page_number: 24
          section_label: null
          body_hash: 4732d9c2b053975a4d3cb27db8e99faa4baf45f71eb350fa519e31b5890ac680
          path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000024.md
          text: "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1) \nThe requirements
            of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson that has complied
            with and received approval to engage in money transmission \nunder this
            [Act] or was identified as a person in control in a prior application
            filed with and \napproved by the [Commissioner] or by an MSB accredited
            state pursuant to a multistate \nlicensing process, provided that: \n(A)
            \nthe person has not had a license revoked or suspended or \ncontrolled
            a licensee that has had a license revoked or suspended while the person
            \nwas in control of the licensee in the previous 5-years; \n(B) \nif the
            person is a licensee, the person is well managed and \nhas received at
            least a satisfactory rating for compliance at its most recent \nexamination
            by an MSB accredited state if such rating was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee
            to be acquired is projected to meet the \nrequirements of [Sections 10.01,
            10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition \nof control is
            completed, and if the person acquiring control is a licensee, that \nlicensee
            is also projected to meet the requirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02,
            and \n10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition of control is completed;
            \n(D) \nthe licensee to be acquired will not implement any material \nchanges
            to its business plan as a result of the acquisition of control, and if
            the person \nacquiring control is a licensee, that licensee also will
            not implement any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result
            of the acquisition of control;  and \n(E) \nthe person provides notice
            of the acquisition in cooperation \nwith the licensee and attests to [Section
            6.01(l)(1)(A), (B), (C), and (D)] in a form \nand in a medium prescribed
            by the [Commissioner]. \n(2) \nIf the notice is not disapproved within
            30 days after the date on \nwhich the notice was determined to be complete,
            the notice is deemed approved. \n(m) \nBefore filing an application for
            approval to acquire control of a licensee a \nperson may request in writing
            a determination from the [Commissioner] as to whether the person \nwould
            be considered a person in control of a licensee upon consummation of a
            proposed \ntransaction. If the [Commissioner] determines that the person
            would not be a person in control of \na licensee, the proposed Person
            and transaction is not subject to the requirements of [Section \n6.01(a)
            and (b)] of this [Act]. \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing process includes
            a determination pursuant to \n[Section 6.01(m)] and an applicant avails
            itself or is otherwise subject to the multistate licensing \nprocess:
            \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to accept the
            \ncontrol determination of a lead investigative state with sufficient
            staffing, expertise, and \nminimum standards for the purpose of [Section
            6.01(m)]; or\n"
        - unit_id: p000015
          start: 0
          end: 2835
          page_number: 15
          section_label: null
          body_hash: bba81d751ac954c1c9099842578104bf494b4912b32ce1f2e32cc8fac953e9e7
          path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000015.md
          text: "15 \n \nchecks, credit checks, fee processing, and examinations.9
            \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS
            forms, \nprocesses, and functionalities in accordance with this [Act].10
            In the event NMLS does not provide \nfunctionality, forms, or processes
            for a provision of this [Act], the [Commissioner] is authorized \nand
            encouraged to strive to implement the requirements in a manner that facilitates
            uniformity \nwith respect to licensing, supervision, reporting, and regulation
            of licensees which are licensed in \nmultiple jurisdictions. \n(e) \nWaive
            or Modify Requirements.— For the purpose of participating in the \nNationwide
            Multistate Licensing System & Registry, the Commissioner is authorized
            to waive or \nmodify, in whole or in part, by rule, regulation or order,
            any or all of the requirements and to \nestablish new requirements as
            reasonably necessary to participate in the Nationwide Multistate \nLicensing
            System & Registry. \n[Alternative to Section 5.02(e)]: The [Commissioner]
            is authorized and encouraged to establish \nand adopt, by rule or regulation,
            requirements for participation by applicants and licensees in \nNMLS upon
            the [Department's] determination that each requirement is consistent with
            law, public \ninterest, and the purposes of this [Section 5.02].] \nSection
            5.03 Application for License. \n(a) \nApplicants for a license shall apply
            in a form and in a medium as prescribed \nby the [Commissioner]. Each
            such form shall contain content as set forth by rule, regulation, \ninstruction
            or procedure of the [Commissioner] and may be changed or updated by the
            \n[Commissioner] in accordance with applicable law in order to carry out
            the purposes of this [Act] \nand maintain consistency with NMLS licensing
            standards and practices. The application must state \nor contain, as applicable:
            \n(1) \nthe legal name and residential and business addresses of the \napplicant
            and any fictitious or trade name used by the applicant in conducting its
            business; \n(2) \na list of any criminal convictions of the applicant
            and any material \nlitigation in which the applicant has been involved
            in the [10]-year period next preceding \nthe submission of the application;
            \n(3) \na description of any money transmission previously provided by
            the \napplicant and the money transmission that the applicant seeks to
            provide in this state; \n \n9 Commentary: The [Commissioner] acting through
            its representatives should review and ensure that NMLS \nfunctionalities,
            forms, and processes are consistent with this Act before adopting such
            NMLS functionalities, forms, \nand processes. \n10 Commentary: The [Commissioner]
            acting through its representatives should review and ensure that NMLS
            \nfunctionalities, forms, and processes are consistent with this Act before
            adopting such NMLS functionalities, forms, \nand processes.\n"
        - unit_id: p000021
          start: 0
          end: 2389
          page_number: 21
          section_label: null
          body_hash: 5638ae03ab2c6c110a80e30639b8ccd42a1c585fdc2818a38e4f2f0fc69a5e06
          path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000021.md
          text: "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. The renewal
            report must state or contain a \ndescription of each material change in
            information submitted by the licensee in its original license \napplication
            which has not been reported to the [Commissioner]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner]
            for good cause may grant an extension of the renewal \ndate. \n(d) \nThe
            [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS to \nprocess
            license renewals provided that such functionality is consistent with this
            [Section 5.06]. \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of License. \n(a) \nIf a licensee
            does not continue to meet the qualifications or satisfy the \nrequirements
            that apply to an applicant for a new money transmission license, the [Commissioner]
            \nmay suspend or revoke the licensee's license in accordance with the
            procedures established by this \n[Act] or other applicable state law for
            such suspension or revocation. \n(b) \nAn applicant for a money transmission
            license must demonstrate that it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission
            licensee must at all times meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01,
            10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control
            and Change of Key Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition of Control. \n(a)
            \nAny person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire
            control \nof a licensee shall obtain the written approval of the [Commissioner]
            prior to acquiring control. \nAn individual is not deemed to acquire control
            of a licensee and is not subject to these acquisition \nof control provisions
            when that individual becomes a key individual in the ordinary course of
            \nbusiness. \n(b) \nA person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking
            to acquire control \nof a licensee shall, in cooperation with the licensee:
            \n(1) \nSubmit an application in a form and in a medium prescribed by
            the \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable fee of [$X] with
            the request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner] may
            permit a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons acting in concert,
            to submit some or all information required by the \n[Commissioner] pursuant
            to [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe application required
            by [Section 6.01(b)(1)] shall include information \nrequired by [Section
            5.04] for any new key individuals that have not previously completed the
            \nrequirements of [Section 5.04] for a licensee.\n"
        - unit_id: p000030
          start: 0
          end: 2670
          page_number: 30
          section_label: null
          body_hash: 0d032292dd6b007bb0772b41f7c3f21512a56d4557c8c7b69696774b6248c842
          path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000030.md
          text: "30 \n \n(1) \nappoint the person signing the contract as the licensee's
            authorized \ndelegate with the authority to conduct money transmission
            on behalf of the licensee; \n(2) \nset forth the nature and scope of the
            relationship between the \nlicensee and the authorized delegate and the
            respective rights and responsibilities of the \nparties; \n(3) \nrequire
            the authorized delegate to agree to fully comply with all \napplicable
            state and federal laws, rules, and regulations pertaining to money transmission,
            \nincluding this [Act] and regulations implementing this [Act], relevant
            provisions of the \nBank Secrecy Act and the USA PATRIOT ACT; \n(4) \nrequire
            the authorized delegate to remit and handle money and \nmonetary value
            in accordance with the terms of the contract between the licensee and
            the \nauthorized delegate; \n(5) \nimpose a trust on money and monetary
            value net of fees received for \nmoney transmission for the benefit of
            the licensee; \n(6) \nrequire the authorized delegate to prepare and maintain
            records as \nrequired by this [Act] or regulations implementing this [Act],
            or as reasonably requested \nby the [Commissioner]; \n(7) \nacknowledge
            that the authorized delegate consents to examination \nor investigation
            by the [Commissioner]; \n(8) \nstate that the licensee is subject to regulation
            by the [Commissioner] \nand that, as part of that regulation, the [Commissioner]
            may suspend or revoke an \nauthorized delegate designation or require
            the licensee to terminate an authorized delegate \ndesignation; and \n(9)
            \n(9)  acknowledge receipt of the written policies and procedures \nrequired
            under [Section 8.01(b)(1)]. \n(e) \nIf the licensee's license is suspended,
            revoked, surrendered, or expired, the \nlicensee must, within five (5)
            business days, provide documentation to the [Commissioner] that \nthe
            licensee has notified all applicable authorized delegates of the licensee
            whose names are in a \nrecord filed with the [Commissioner] of the suspension,
            revocation, surrender, or expiration of a \nlicense. Upon suspension,
            revocation, surrender, or expiration of a license, applicable authorized
            \ndelegates shall immediately cease to provide money transmission as an
            authorized delegate of the \nlicensee. \n(f) \nAn authorized delegate
            of a licensee holds in trust for the benefit of the \nlicensee all money
            net of fees received from money transmission.  If any authorized delegate
            \ncommingles any funds received from money transmission with any other
            funds or property owned \nor controlled by the authorized delegate, all
            commingled funds and other property shall be \nconsidered held in trust
            in favor of the licensee in an amount equal to the amount of money net
            of\n"

          text: "31 \n \nfees received from money transmission.22 \n(g) \nAn authorized
            delegate may not use a subdelegate to conduct money \ntransmission on
            behalf of a licensee. \nSection 8.02 Unauthorized Activities \nA person
            shall not engage in the business of money transmission on behalf of a
            person \nnot licensed under this [Act]  or not exempt pursuant to [Article
            III] of this [Act]. A person that \nengages in such activity provides
            money transmission to the same extent as if the person were a \nlicensee,
            and shall be jointly and severally liable with the unlicensed or nonexempt
            person. \nSection 8.03 [Optional]: Prohibited Authorized Delegates. \n(a)
            \nThe [appropriate court] in an action brought by a licensee shall have
            \njurisdiction to grant appropriate equitable or legal relief, including
            without limitation prohibiting \nthe authorized delegate from directly
            or indirectly acting as an authorized delegate for any licensee \nin this
            state and the payment of restitution, damages or other monetary relief,
            if the [appropriate \ncourt] finds that an authorized delegate failed
            to remit money in accordance with the written \ncontract required by [Section
            8.01(b)] or as otherwise directed by the licensee or required by law.
            \n(b) \nIf the [appropriate court] issues an order prohibiting a person
            from acting as \nan authorized delegate for any licensee pursuant to [Section
            8.03(a)], the licensee that brought the \naction shall report the order
            to the [Commissioner] within thirty (30) days and shall report the \norder
            through NMLS within ninety (90) days. \n(c) \nAn authorized delegate who
            holds money in trust for the benefit of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails
            to remit more than [$XXX] of such money is guilty of a [reference \nto
            state classification] felony. \n(d) \nAn authorized delegate who holds
            money in trust for the benefit of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails to
            remit no more than [$XXX] of such money is guilty of a [reference \nto
            state classification] misdemeanor. \nARTICLE IX  \nTimely Transmission,
            Refunds, and Disclosures \nSection 9.01 Timely Transmission. \n(a) \nEvery
            licensee shall forward all money received for transmission in \naccordance
            with the terms of the agreement between the licensee and the sender unless
            the licensee \nhas a reasonable belief or a reasonable basis to believe
            that the sender may be a victim of fraud or \nthat a crime or violation
            of law, rule, or regulation has occurred, is occurring, or may occur.
            \n(b) \nIf a licensee fails to forward money received for transmission
            in accordance \nwith this section, the licensee must respond to inquiries
            by the sender with the reason for the failure \n \n22 Commentary: An express
            trust account or segregated bank account is not required.\n"
